# GPT lane ownership — Plan 2b-2: the lane runs — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A rostered `codex` lane *runs* under ccrc. `ccgpt-runtime` builds an isolated LiteLLM runtime and gates it on a behaviour probe. `ccrc codex start|stop|status|login <id>` runs the lane's two tiers as transient user services, or under `nohup` where there is no user manager, through one new platform helper. The per-session launcher `ccrc-codex` starts the lane and execs Claude Code against it. Install and update build the runtime and restart stale tiers. Uninstall and account removal stop the lane and reap it.

**Architecture:** Lifecycle lives in `ccd/ccrc` (`cmd_codex` plus a `_codex_*` lane library). Its one new process primitive is `_svc_run_supervised`, added to the byte-identical platform region of `ccd/ccd` and `ccd/ccrc`. Two new standalone executables sit under `ccd/`:
- `ccgpt-runtime` owns `~/.ccrc/runtime/codex/`: probed generations and a `current` symlink.
- `ccrc-codex` is the thin launcher every generated Codex wrapper execs.

**Nothing on any real box changes behaviour.** No roster on any box names a `codex` lane (0 rows, measured 2026-09-23), so every new step is a no-op there until Plan 3's cutover edits a roster.

**Tech Stack:** bash (`ccd/ccrc`, `ccd/ccd`, the two new executables), Python 3 (the embedded behaviour probe), Node ESM (`deploy/models-op.mjs`, `shared/*.mjs`), vitest (`server/test`).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-gpt-lane-ownership-design.md`, sections §5 (install), §7 (lifecycle), §8 (per-lane config), §9 (login), §11 (placement), §13 (uninstall) and §18 (mutation table). Where this plan departs from the spec, the departure is a numbered deviation in [Deviations found](#deviations-found), and Task 12 amends the spec text.

> **Measurements.** Facts cited as "the 2026-09-23 … measurement" or "census" were taken read-only on the operator's fleet box and this tree while the plan was written. Their reports are not tracked. Every fact a task depends on is stated in the task, and an implementer re-measures before relying on it.

## The launcher is `ccrc-codex`, not `ccgpt`

This is the one decision that shapes every task, so it is stated before them.

On the operator's fleet box, `~/.local/bin/ccgpt` is **another repository's live launcher**: a 22 KB regular file, with no ccrc marker. Both live Codex lanes reach it, one through a symlink and one through a launcher that execs it by path. It backs two running transient tier units, measured read-only on 2026-09-23.

The spec placed ccrc's launcher at that same path. `_inst_atomic` has no ownership check (measured), so the first `ccrc update` onto this plan would have overwritten a live program: a silent cutover, done by an installer.

Even an ownership-guarded placement would force every lane to cut over in one sitting. ccrc's launcher serves only lanes the roster declares `codex`, so the moment it replaced the other one, every lane not yet migrated would lose its launcher. The spec's own cutover (§15.3) is one lane at a time.

A distinct name removes the collision by construction:
- nothing of the other repository's is written or deleted until the cutover the operator authorises;
- lanes cut over independently;
- rollback is putting a lane's old launcher back.

Renaming Plan 1's shipped target is safe for one reason: no roster on any box names a `codex` lane, so no generated launcher execs `ccgpt` anywhere. Recorded as **D-3478**.

## Global Constraints

Every task's requirements implicitly include this section.

**Repository and process**
- **Node floor `>=22.13.0`**, identical across the three engines. Never lower an `engines` field to make a test green.
- **The repository is PUBLIC (AGPL-3.0).** No real account id, lane name, label, email, host, port, credential, OAuth path, session codename, operator username or real model id may appear in any tracked byte. Fixture vocabulary:
  - ids `codex-a`, `codex-b` (kind `codex`), `claude` (upstream), `claude2` (generated);
  - `authDir` `.local/share/ccrc/codex/<id>`;
  - tokens `test-token-not-a-secret`;
  - model ids `gpt-x` and `probe-model`.
- **`ccd/ccd` is GENERATED and must be re-stamped after any edit** (`ownership.test.ts` catches a missed stamp). **`ccd/ccrc` is hand-written and carries NO marker**; never add one (D-3171).
- **No live lane id in any added line** (ruling R40). The operator's two live lane ids are recorded in the gitignored `deploy/reference-fleet.md` and never here; no added line may name either. A new case that needs an `external` lane uses the tree's existing non-live `router` row; a new external row with `telemetry: "codex"` uses `ext-a`. Existing untouched lines stay as they are.
- **The base moved once already; every quoted number is an example** (ruling R41). The plan was measured at `aed80210`; the branch was rebased onto `bbb5e714` before review. Rebase onto `origin/main` again before Task 1. Every line number, census count and case count quoted below is an example to RE-DERIVE, never a value to paste. Post-condition diffs compare against the task's own recorded base (`BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` at its Step 0), never against `origin/main`.
- **Fixture HOMEs only.** Never run `ccrc`, `ccd`, `ccgpt-runtime`, `ccrc-codex` or either Python file against the live `$HOME`. Harnesses:
  - `makeCcdHarness` (`server/test/ccdWsHelpers.ts`);
  - `installFixtureTree` (`server/test/installTreeFixture.ts`);
  - `ccgptHarness.ts`;
  - `codexLaneFixture.ts` (Task 4).
- **Never run the destructive `ccd` verbs** (`ws-rm`, `ws-reap`, `ws-gc --prune`, `ws-archive`, `ws-restore`). Never touch tmux, `~/.cc-sessions`, `~/.cc-limits` or any `claude-session@*` unit.
- **Single source of truth.** Runtime lists are derived from one declaration, never hand-kept twice (`single-definition.test.ts`).
- **Mutation-table discipline.** Every guard ships with a case that goes RED when the guard is mutated, measured both ways with counts. If a demanded mutation does not red, **report that it does not**. Never manufacture code to force a bind (D-3152).
- **Suites.**
  - Run in the FOREGROUND from inside the package, with `timeout ≥ 600000` ms: `cd server && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/<file>.test.ts`. Never bare `npx vitest`.
  - **`tsc --noEmit` does not read `server/test/`.** When a task writes a test file, its typecheck step is `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/typecheck-tests.test.ts` (D-3163).
- **Locate every subject by name plus a grep, at execution time.** This plan carries no line numbers, deliberately.
- **Deviation numbers are API-issued.** The ones this plan uses are defined in [Deviations found](#deviations-found). A task that finds a new departure reports it; the controller allocates the number. Never write a range.
- **Commit trailer:** `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

**The live box (binding, new in this plan)**
- **Never write, move or delete** `~/.local/bin/ccgpt`, `~/.local/bin/ccgpt-proxy`, `~/.local/bin/ccgpt-usage`, or any `~/.config/systemd/user/ccgpt-usage*` file. They are the other repository's live lane.
- **Never start, stop, restart or `reset-failed` any `ccgpt-*` unit on the real user manager**, and never bind or probe a live lane's port.
- **Never read or print a live unit's `Environment=`, or any key-bearing file** (`runtime.env`, `auth.json`, a secrets file, `~/.handoff/env`). The other repository's live tiers carry the gateway key in unit metadata. Any check on one is count-only, e.g. `systemctl --user show -p Environment <unit> | grep -c 'LITELLM_MASTER_KEY='` (ruling R43).
  - Lifecycle tests use **dynamic free ports** (`freePort()`), never a hard-coded port for a real listener.
  - `45010`/`45011`/`45020`/`45021` remain the vocabulary for pure-parse fixtures that open no socket.
- **Every `systemd-run` and `systemctl` a test can reach is a fixture.** Today the ccrc install, update, uninstall and doctor harnesses contain no `systemd-run` (measured), so on this box a spine path that reached one would drive the real user manager. A task that adds such a path plants a recorder in that harness **in the same commit**.
- **No real litellm in the default suite.** Cases needing it are opt-in: `describe.skipIf(!process.env.CCRC_TEST_LITELLM_PY)`. Anything that imports litellm sets:
  - `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`;
  - a `mkTmp` HOME and a synthetic token directory.

  Measured: `import litellm` otherwise fetches a remote file with three retries, and `Authenticator()` mkdirs its token directory.

**Portability**
- **New bash files join `macos-platform.test.ts`' GNU-spelling corpus automatically**, so they carry none of:
  - `sha256sum`: use `_plat_sha256` inside ccrc, and `shasum -a 256` or python `hashlib` in a standalone file;
  - bare `timeout` or `uuidgen`;
  - template-less `mktemp`;
  - `stat -c`, `date -d`, or `mv -T`: use the `ln -s` + `mv` idiom `_inst_graphify_engine` uses, or python `os.replace`.

**Order invariants**
- Nothing follows `_inst_installed`, and `cmd_install` ends with `cmd_doctor`.
- **Every commit on `main` installs.** An install line never precedes its file; a file may precede its install line (Plan 2a's precedent).
- **The whole plan must be squash-merged** if any intermediate commit fails that rule.

(1) `ccrc-install.test.ts`'s survival case: another repository's `ccgpt`, `ccgpt-proxy` and `ccgpt-usage`, plus an alias to the first, survive `install --role fleet` and `uninstall` byte for byte. (2) The re-aimed fixture-tree absence pin over `ccd/ccrc-codex` and `ccd/ccgpt-runtime`. Task 9, which places both files, flips pin (2) on purpose.

**Why:**

*The name is taken on the one box that matters.* The measurements (the 2026-09-23 live-box census–§2, the 2026-09-23 install-spine measurement) found this on the fleet box:
- `~/.local/bin/ccgpt` is a 22 KB regular file, mode 755, with **no** `# ccrc:generated` marker. It is another repository's live launcher.
- One live Codex lane is a symlink to it. The other lane is a small file that execs it by path.
- It backs two running transient tier units.

`_inst_atomic` has no ownership check: when `cmp` differs it copies and renames. So a ccrc file placed at `~/.local/bin/ccgpt` would cut over every live lane at once, silently. It would also repoint the symlinked lane. D-3478 moves ccrc's launcher to a free path instead of designing a swap.

*A Plan 1 wrapper aimed there would pick the wrong lane.* the 2026-09-23 tier-interface measurement measures the live launcher. It defaults `CCGPT_ACCOUNT_ID` to its first lane when the variable is unset, and derives the lane's config dir, token dir and config path from that one id. A Plan 1 Codex wrapper exports only `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and then `exec "$HOME/.local/bin/ccgpt" "$@"` (the 2026-09-23 ccd-launcher measurement). On that box it would therefore have run a `codex-a` session on the other repository's first lane, with that lane's OAuth: the wrong-lane-credential class. Only one thing keeps this from happening: no roster on any box has a `codex` row (`grep -c '"codex"' deploy/accounts.default.json` → 0; the 2026-09-23 live-box census measured the live rosters). The same fact makes the rename free today. After this task, such a wrapper fails with ENOENT until the launcher is placed. That is a loud failure at spawn, not a quiet wrong lane.

*The target is spelled in exactly five shipped places, all written by Plan 1* (the 2026-09-23 verbs measurement, the 2026-09-23 ccd-launcher measurement):
- the writer (`shared/wrapper.mjs`);
- the orphan-scan skip set (`deploy/gen-wrappers.mjs`);
- the two roster mirrors' reservation;
- the doctor's expected target.

`grep -rn ccgpt agent/src server/src` finds one prose comment and no call site. Nothing reads the literal back except `_check_wrappers`.

*`ccgpt` leaves `TOOLCHAIN_EXECUTABLES` but stays reserved.*
- **Why it leaves the set.** The set is "ccrc's OWN executables" (its header). Keeping a name ccrc will never place would make Task 9's reverse derivation (Set ⊆ `_inst_bins`) red forever on `ccgpt`.
- **Why that is safe on the live box.** The orphan scan tests the set first and the marker second. The live `ccgpt` is unmarked (measured), so `verifyMarker` answers `foreign` and the scan skips it, which is the same outcome as today. A new case pins exactly that shape.
- **Why it stays reserved.** An account with id `ccgpt` would get a wrapper written at the other repository's live path. `ccrc-adopt` on that box also meets `ccgpt` as a candidate. The reservation is what refuses it at parse, and it keeps doing so.

*What this does NOT make true.* The dotless-name agreement stays one-directional. The only enforced direction is `gen-wrappers.test.ts`' D-93 case, `_inst_bins` ⊆ `TOOLCHAIN_EXECUTABLES`. After this task, Set − `_inst_bins` = {`ccrc-codex`, `ccgpt-runtime`}. That is D-3173's shape with one name swapped, and **the TOOLCHAIN→`_inst_bins` direction stays unenforced until Task 9**. Mutation M3b below measures that gap on purpose: dropping `ccrc-codex` from the set is caught only by this task's literal case, and the D-93 case stays green.

**Every bare `ccgpt` in the code trees, classified.** The census command:

```bash
grep -rnP '(?<![A-Za-z0-9_.-])ccgpt(?![A-Za-z0-9_.-])' shared deploy ccd server/test server/src agent/src agent/test pwa/src install.sh
```

At `aed80210` it finds 110 hits in 35 files; the task's two narrower greps (`'ccgpt'` and `ccgpt"`) are subsets of it. The rule for classifying a hit:
- **rename**: it names ccrc's own launcher-to-be;
- **comment-only**: prose about ccrc's launcher-to-be;
- **keep**: it is the other repository's file, the external arm, a reservation, the `/ccgpt/lane` route, or a verbatim spec quote.

|---|---|---|
| `shared/wrapper.mjs` (1) | the exec target | **rename** |

**1i. `server/test/ccrc-install.test.ts`, the survival case.** Append a new `describeLinux` at the end of the file. That puts it below every citation into this file, and the citations here are already stale. It follows `a FOREIGN ccgpt-usage@ unit pair and its enabled instance survive install --role fleet and uninstall` exactly. It is Linux-only like that precedent, because this suite's only uninstall run is Linux-gated, and the measured collision is on the Linux fleet box.

```ts
describeLinux('ccrc install and uninstall leave another repository\'s GPT-lane files alone (D-3478)', () => {
  it('a foreign ccgpt, ccgpt-proxy and ccgpt-usage in ~/.local/bin, and an alias to the first, survive install --role fleet and uninstall, byte for byte', () => {
    // The fleet box's shape (m-livebox): three dotless files another repository
    // owns — the launcher both live Codex lanes exec, its shim, its publisher —
    // and a lane alias symlinked to the launcher. `_inst_atomic` has no ownership
    // check, so ONE placement at any of these names silently cuts over every live
    // lane at once; that is why ccrc's launcher is `ccrc-codex`. This case reads
    // what the verbs DID, so it also sees a placement or removal from a function
    // `install-census.test.ts` does not read.
    const home = freshBox('ccrc-install-foreign-ccgpt-bins-');
    mkdirSync(join(home, '.ccrc'), { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'agent.env'),
      'CCRC_SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7788\nCCRC_AGENT_TOKEN=fixture-not-a-real-token\n');
    const bin = join(home, '.local', 'bin');
    // Invisible to every scan on purpose — no CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, no marker — so
    // this case is about placement and removal, never about a doctor verdict.
    const foreign: Record<string, string> = {
      'ccgpt': '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# FOREIGN-FIXTURE-2b2: another repository owns this launcher\nexit 0\n',
      'ccgpt-proxy': '#!/usr/bin/env python3\n# FOREIGN-FIXTURE-2b2: another repository owns this shim\n',
      'ccgpt-usage': '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# FOREIGN-FIXTURE-2b2: another repository owns this publisher\nexit 0\n',
    };
    for (const [name, text] of Object.entries(foreign)) writeFileSync(join(bin, name), text, { mode: 0o755 });
    symlinkSync('ccgpt', join(bin, 'ext-a'));
    const untouched = (stage: string): void => {
      for (const [name, text] of Object.entries(foreign)) {
        const p = join(bin, name);
        expect(existsSync(p), `${stage}: ${name} is gone`).toBe(true);
        expect(lstatSync(p).isFile(), `${stage}: ${name} is no longer a regular file`).toBe(true);
        expect(read(p), `${stage}: ${name} changed`).toBe(text);
        expect(statSync(p).mode & 0o777, `${stage}: ${name} mode`).toBe(0o755);
      }
      expect(lstatSync(join(bin, 'ext-a')).isSymbolicLink(), `${stage}: the alias is gone`).toBe(true);
      expect(readlinkSync(join(bin, 'ext-a')), `${stage}: the alias was repointed`).toBe('ccgpt');
    };
    const inst = runInstall(home, ['install', '--role', 'fleet']);
    expect(inst.code, inst.stderr).toBe(0);
    untouched('after install --role fleet');
    const un = runInstall(home, ['uninstall']);
    expect(un.code, `stderr: ${un.stderr}\nstdout: ${un.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    untouched('after uninstall');
  });
});
```

If install exits non-zero because doctor flags one of the planted files, the fixture is wrong. It must be invisible to every scan. Strip the file until nothing reads it as a launcher; do not weaken the assertions.

> **Departures from Appendix A's TEXT (additive; none changes a name or an interface; each has a test and a
> mutation row).** They all follow one rule: one contract, two arms. Whatever one arm cannot report after the
> start is either probed before either arm runs, or made identical on both arms.
> 1. **`<log>` and `<envfile>` must be absolute** (else 64). systemd.exec(5) takes neither `append:` nor
>    `EnvironmentFile=` relative. That is documented, not measured here, because no test may reach a real manager.
>    The nohup arm would otherwise accept a path the systemd arm fails on.
>    `-`-prefixed envfiles (systemd's ignore-if-missing form) are refused too: a lane whose key file is missing
>    must not start keyless.
> 2. **Two state probes run before EITHER arm** (else 1, one stderr line): `<envfile>` is a readable regular file,
>    and `<log>` opens for append. A backgrounded child answers 0 whatever happens next. `systemd-run` reports that
>    the unit was CREATED, not that its process started. This is the argument `_svc_run_detached`'s `command -v`
>    probe already makes.
> 3. **The nohup arm's missing command prints one stderr line** before returning 1. The design contract (Appendix A) had a bare
>    `return 1`. Every other state failure here names itself.
> 4. **Precedence on the nohup arm matches systemd's.** The design contract (Appendix A) spelled `. envfile; exec nohup env
>    NAME=value … "$@"`, where a pair beats the envfile. systemd.exec(5) documents the reverse: `EnvironmentFile=`
>    overrides `Environment=` (documented, not measured). So the pairs go to the child's `env -i` FIRST and the file
>    is sourced after them, inside that clean environment (item 7). No shipped caller is affected, because the key
>    is never a pair (the refusal) and `runtime.env` holds only the key. The point is parity, and the test pins it.
> 5. **The nohup child runs in `$HOME`** (`cd -- "$HOME"`, before `env -i` and the pairs), as
>    `--working-directory="$HOME"` does on the systemd arm. It also reads stdin from `/dev/null` explicitly. A block
>    that an operator sources into an interactive shell has job control on, and there an async job keeps the
>    terminal.
> 6. **Refusals never echo a value.** A secret-looking name is echoed by NAME only. An argument that does not parse
>    as `NAME=value` is echoed by POSITION only, because it may be a value passed by mistake.
> 7. **The nohup arm starts from a scrubbed environment (ruling R2).** Appendix A's `exec nohup env NAME=value …
>    "$@"` handed the child the caller's WHOLE environment, which a transient unit never gets: its environment is the
>    manager's, plus `--setenv`, plus the envfile. So a caller's `ANTHROPIC_*`/`CHATGPT_*`/`CLAUDE_*` reached a tier
>    on the nohup arm only. The child now runs `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" ${LANG:+LANG="$LANG"}` plus the
>    pairs, then a `sh -c` that sources the envfile INSIDE that clean environment and `exec`s `nohup` and the command.
>    The file's assignments are sourced by that `sh`, never listed as `env` arguments: listed, the key would sit in
>    `env`'s argv, which `ps` shows to every user on the box, for the life of that process. That is the one channel the
>    refusal exists to close. Sourcing it after the pairs also keeps item 4's precedence. A case plants a sentinel in
>    the caller and proves the child does not see it.

**Why:**
- **The helper is missing, and where it goes is fixed.** `_svc_run_detached` (`grep -n '^_svc_run_detached()'
  ccd/ccd ccd/ccrc`) takes no unit name, slice, restart policy or log. Its Linux arm is one line,
  `systemd-run --user --collect --quiet "$@"`, and it has **no** fallback.
  - the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement: "a box whose `systemd-run --user` fails … gets the failure back, never a `nohup`".
  - Its Darwin arm DISCARDS output (`nohup "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 &`).
  - Spec §7.1 puts the new sibling above the closing sentinel in BOTH files. The sentinel's own comment says why:
    the compared region is sliced by the two sentinels, and `macos-platform.test.ts` asserts every
    `^(_plat_|_svc_)…()` definition sits inside them (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement).
  - `_svc_run_detached` stays untouched. Its Linux-arm regex (`['_svc_run_detached', …]` in `arms`), both ccd
    callers (`grep -n '_svc_run_detached ' ccd/ccd`), three suites that shadow it by name, and an in-flight
    branch's recorder all key on its exact argv (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement).
- **The user-manager probe is new, not inherited (D-3483).**
  - Spec §7.3 calls the fallback probe "`_svc_run_detached`'s existing argument, inherited". Only the Darwin
    `command -v` probe exists.
  - `grep -nE 'is-system-running|show-environment|_have_user_systemd' ccd/ccd ccd/ccrc deploy/*.sh` → nothing
    (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement).
  - `_have_systemctl` is PATH presence only, and its own comment says so.
  - The two-conjunct spelling is the live launcher's `_have_user_systemd`, read from the box (the 2026-09-23 tier-interface measurement). So
    is the systemd-run flag set: `--user --quiet --collect --unit=… --slice=app.slice --working-directory="$HOME"
    -p Restart=always -p RestartSec=3 -p StartLimitIntervalSec=300 -p StartLimitBurst=20 -p "StandardOutput=append:$log"
    -p "StandardError=append:$log"`.
- **The secret refusal closes a hazard measured live, not a hypothetical one.** the 2026-09-23 tier-interface measurement/§5 read
  (never printed) the two live tier units' `Environment=` property. Both carry the gateway key, because the live
  launcher passes it with `--setenv`. The same units carry `EnvironmentFile=` as a path only
  (`systemctl show -p EnvironmentFiles` → the path, no bytes). That is the shape this helper enforces. Spec §7.4's
  pin says "no key in any property", and §18's row says "the key moves back into `--setenv`".
  - **Do not re-measure that fact by reading the property (ruling R43).** Nothing in this task depends on it. A
    live unit's `Environment=` holds the other repository's gateway key, and reading it puts that key into the
    session transcript. If a check is ever needed, it is a COUNT and nothing else:
    `systemctl --user show -p Environment <unit> | grep -c 'LITELLM_MASTER_KEY='`. Take `<unit>` from
    `systemctl --user list-units 'ccgpt-*' --no-legend`, and never type a lane's name.
  - **The rule reads the NAME's tail (ruling R1).** Appendix A's substring rule refused `CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR`,
    LiteLLM's own variable, which `_codex_start_tier` must pass for the litellm tier, so the helper would have
    refused the only caller the plan gives it on its first start. R1's rule refuses a NAME whose last `_`-segment
    ends with `KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` or `PASSWD`, so that name passes and no exemption list exists.
    None of the five words contains `_`, so "the last segment ends with W" is the same test as "the NAME ends with
    W". The `case` spells the second form. Measured: the two spellings agree on the plan's five names, their
    lowercase spellings, and twelve more names, including every name Appendix A's callers pass.
  - **What the tail rule lets through, stated so nobody is surprised:** a secret word that is not last, such as
    `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `…_TOKEN_FILE` or `…_KEY_PATH`. The rule catches the names that match it. It does not
    replace the rule that secrets go in the envfile (Hazard 4).
- **No existing instrument pins any of this.**
  - `grep -rn nohup server/test/*.ts` → 0, so the Darwin arm of `_svc_run_detached` is pinned by nothing
    (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement). Spec §18's "the Darwin arm probes before backgrounding" has no instrument today.
  - No fixture models "systemctl present, user bus absent" (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement).
  - A planted `systemctl show` answer would be a control derived from the measurement (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement).
  - **The honest fixture-level evidence is the `systemd-run` argv**, so the census below is a `toEqual` over it.
    This departs from spec §5.4's pin, which also says "assert over `systemctl show` output in a fixture". The
    departure is **D-3491** (ruling R46), and the systemd-arm case's comment cites it.
- **Why the tests force `CCD_OS` in the payload rather than pick a platform.** This suite runs on the Linux CI
  leg and on the non-required macOS leg (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `test-macos`, which runs the whole server
  suite).
  - An env var named `CCD_OS` does nothing, because the block overwrites it at source time.
  - Assigning it after the block in the same payload is the idiom the `_plat_mv_notdir` forced-Darwin describe
    already uses (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement).
  - So every case below runs both arms on both legs, and no case needs `itLinux`/`itDarwin`. That is also why none
    trips the platform-title rule, which scans only those four wrappers.
- **Containment is three layers, because a leak here would start a real transient unit** on the developer's user
  manager (design contract LIVE-BOX RULES):
  - PATH recorders are planted in EVERY case, even where the subject never reaches them, so a mutant that does
    reach one meets a recorder.
  - A payload preamble exits 99 unless `command -v` resolves each manager name to its stub.
  - `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` point at nothing.
  - No fixture unit is named `ccgpt-*`.
  - `ghContainedEnv` is not used. These cases source only the platform block, never ccd, so there is no `gh`
    path to poison. The ccd coverage scan (`ccd-workspaces.test.ts`) matches only `/^ccd.*\.ts$/` files and does
    not scan this one.

Then the new `describe`, placed after the forced-Darwin `_plat_mv_notdir` describe's closing `});`:

```ts
// ── _svc_have_user_manager / _svc_run_supervised: both arms, on whichever box runs this ──
// UNCONDITIONAL. Every case sources the REAL block and FORCES `CCD_OS` in the
// same payload — the idiom the describe above uses — so the Linux arms run on
// the macOS leg and the Darwin arm runs here. Nothing below is platform-gated.
//
// CONTAINMENT, THREE LAYERS, because a leaked call would start a real transient
// unit on the developer's own user manager: recording `systemd-run` and
// `systemctl` first on PATH in EVERY case, including the ones whose subject
// never reaches them (a mutant that does must meet a recorder); a preamble that
// exits 99 unless `command -v` resolves each name to its stub; and a bus address
// that points at nothing. No fixture unit carries a real lane's unit prefix.
describe('_svc_run_supervised and _svc_have_user_manager — both arms, forced, on whichever box runs this', () => {
  type Fx = { home: string; bin: string; runLog: string; ctlLog: string };

  /** A fixture HOME with RECORDING `systemd-run` and `systemctl` in `stub-bin/`. */
  function svcFixture(opts: { withSystemdRun?: boolean } = {}): Fx {
    const home = mkTmp('ccrc-svc-sup-');
    const bin = path.join(home, 'stub-bin');
    mkdirSync(bin);
    const runLog = path.join(home, 'systemd-run.argv');
    const ctlLog = path.join(home, 'systemctl.calls');
    if (opts.withSystemdRun !== false) {
      // ONE ARGV ELEMENT PER LINE and a terminator per call: an element that
      // carries a space stays one element, and `toEqual` sees the order.
      writeFileSync(path.join(bin, 'systemd-run'), [
        '#!/bin/sh',
        `for a in "$@"; do printf '%s\\n' "$a"; done >> '${runLog}'`,
        `printf '%s\\n' '--end-of-call--' >> '${runLog}'`,
        'exit "${SVC_RUN_RC:-0}"',
      ].join('\n') + '\n', { mode: 0o755 });
    }
    writeFileSync(path.join(bin, 'systemctl'), [
      '#!/bin/sh',
      `printf '%s\\n' "$*" >> '${ctlLog}'`,
      'case "$*" in "--user show-environment") exit "${SVC_SHOWENV_RC:-0}" ;; esac',
      'exit 0',
    ].join('\n') + '\n', { mode: 0o755 });
    return { home, bin, runLog, ctlLog };
  }

  const lines = (f: string): string[] =>
    (existsSync(f) ? readFileSync(f, 'utf8').split('\n').filter((l) => l !== '') : []);
  /** Every `systemd-run` call, each as its own argv. */
  const runCalls = (fx: Fx): string[][] => {
    const calls: string[][] = [];
    let cur: string[] = [];
    for (const l of lines(fx.runLog)) {
      if (l === '--end-of-call--') { calls.push(cur); cur = []; } else cur.push(l);
    }
    return calls;
  };
  /** Everything either manager binary was asked, in one list — empty means "never asked". */
  const managerCalls = (fx: Fx): string[] =>
    [...lines(fx.ctlLog), ...runCalls(fx).map((a) => `systemd-run ${a.join(' ')}`)];
  const pause = (ms: number): void => { Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms); };
  /** Bounded wait; the caller asserts afterwards, so a timeout reds with the caller's message. */
  const until = (pred: () => boolean, ms = 10_000): void => {
    const end = Date.now() + ms;
    while (!pred() && Date.now() < end) pause(50);
  };
  const argsOf = (pid: number): string =>
    (spawnSync('ps', ['-o', 'args=', '-p', String(pid)], { encoding: 'utf8' }).stdout ?? '').trim();
  const reap = (pid: number): void => { try { process.kill(pid, 'SIGKILL'); } catch { /* already gone */ } };

  /** Source the block, force the platform, put the stubs first on PATH, and
   *  refuse (99) unless every manager name resolves to its stub. `stubsOnly`
   *  replaces PATH with the stub directory alone — the one way to model "no
   *  systemd-run on this box" on a box that has one. */
  function svc(fx: Fx, os: 'linux' | 'darwin', expr: string,
    opts: { env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv; stubsOnly?: boolean; cwd?: string } = {}):
    { status: number | null; stdout: string; stderr: string } {
    const run = path.join(fx.bin, 'systemd-run');
    const ctl = path.join(fx.bin, 'systemctl');
    const script = [
      'set -uo pipefail',
      platformBlock(ccd),
      `CCD_OS=${os}`,
      opts.stubsOnly ? `export PATH='${fx.bin}'` : `export PATH='${fx.bin}':"$PATH"`,
      `[ "$(command -v systemctl)" = '${ctl}' ] || { echo 'containment: systemctl is not the stub' >&2; exit 99; }`,
      opts.stubsOnly
        ? `[ -z "$(command -v systemd-run)" ] || { echo 'containment: a systemd-run is reachable' >&2; exit 99; }`
        : `[ "$(command -v systemd-run)" = '${run}' ] || { echo 'containment: systemd-run is not the stub' >&2; exit 99; }`,
      expr,
    ].join('\n') + '\n';
    const r = spawnSync('bash', ['-c', script], {
      encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 15_000, cwd: opts.cwd ?? fx.home,
      env: {
        ...process.env,
        HOME: fx.home,
        XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: path.join(fx.home, 'no-runtime-dir'),
        DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS: `unix:path=${path.join(fx.home, 'no-bus')}`,
        ...opts.env,
      },
    });
    expect(r.status, `the payload's containment preamble refused: ${r.stderr}`).not.toBe(99);
    return { status: r.status, stdout: (r.stdout ?? '').trim(), stderr: (r.stderr ?? '').trim() };
  }

  it('_svc_have_user_manager answers 0 only off Darwin, with systemd-run on PATH AND a manager that answers', () => {
    // The probe the live launcher runs, and the one `_svc_run_detached` never
    // had: "systemctl installed, no user bus" must answer NO, which is the row

      { os: 'linux', sr: true, showEnvRc: 0, want: 'rc=0', asked: ['--user show-environment'] },
      { os: 'linux', sr: true, showEnvRc: 1, want: 'rc=1', asked: ['--user show-environment'] },
      { os: 'linux', sr: false, showEnvRc: 0, want: 'rc=1', asked: [] },

  it('the systemd arm: one transient unit, its whole argv in order, and no key material anywhere', () => {

    const fx = svcFixture();

    const elsewhere = mkTmp('ccrc-svc-cwd-');
    const r = svc(fx, 'linux', [
      '_svc_have_user_manager() { return 1; }',

      `  -- sh -c 'echo "pair=$SVC_PAIR file=$FROM_ENVFILE shared=$SHARED cwd=$(pwd -P)"; exec sleep 30'`,
      'echo "rc=$?"',

      until(() => readFileSync(log, 'utf8').includes('pair='));

      expect(readFileSync(log, 'utf8'))
        .toBe(`an-earlier-line\npair=pair-value file=file-value shared=from-file cwd=${fx.home}\n`);
      // EXACT, not a substring: every shell in the chain carries `sleep 30` in

      until(() => argsOf(pid) === 'sleep 30');

  it('the nohup arm starts from a SCRUBBED environment: a variable the caller exported never reaches the child; HOME, PATH, the pairs and a set LANG do', () => {
    // A unit's environment is the manager's, never the caller's, so the nohup
    // child starts from `env -i` too. The sentinel belongs to NO family on
    // purpose: `env -i` names none, and a sentinel named `CLAUDE_…` would also
    // pass a mutant that scrubbed only `CLAUDE_*`. The child prints NAMED
    // variables only, never `env`, so a mutant that leaks the caller's whole
    // environment cannot copy a developer's own token into this log or a diff.
    const fx = svcFixture();
    const rows: Array<{ lang: string | undefined; want: string }> = [
      { lang: 'C', want: 'lang=C' },
      // `${LANG:+…}`: a caller with no LANG gives the child no LANG, not an empty one.
      { lang: undefined, want: 'lang=absent' },

        '_svc_have_user_manager() { return 1; }',

        `_svc_run_supervised fixture-scrub.service '${log}' - SVC_PAIR=pair-value \\`,
        `  -- sh -c 'echo "sentinel=\${SVC_CALLER_SENTINEL-absent} pair=\${SVC_PAIR-absent} home=\${HOME-absent} path-head=\${PATH%%:*} lang=\${LANG-absent}"'`,
        'echo "rc=$?"',
      ].join('\n'), { env: { SVC_CALLER_SENTINEL: 'planted-by-the-caller', LANG: row.lang } });
      const m = /^caller=planted-by-the-caller\nnohup (\d+)\nrc=0$/.exec(r.stdout);
      expect(m, `${row.want}: stdout: ${r.stdout} / stderr: ${r.stderr}`).not.toBeNull();
      const pid = Number(m![1]);
      try {
        until(() => readFileSync(log, 'utf8').includes('sentinel='));

          .toBe(`sentinel=absent pair=pair-value home=${fx.home} path-head=${fx.bin} ${row.want}\n`);
      } finally {
        reap(pid);
      }
    }
    expect(runCalls(fx), 'the nohup arm never reaches systemd-run').toEqual([]);
  });
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement — ONE text, inserted into both files**

**The insert.** These exact bytes go between `_svc_run_detached`'s closing `}` and `# ── END PLATFORM LAYER`. The
first line is blank, and the last line is `}` with no blank line after it, so the sentinel follows directly, as it
does today. The comment cites D-3483 by its number.

```bash

# `_svc_have_user_manager` — can this box start a TRANSIENT USER SERVICE now?
#
# NEW LOGIC, NOT INHERITED (D-3483). `_svc_run_detached` above
# never asks: its Linux arm runs `systemd-run --user` and hands back whatever
# that answers, with no fallback. `_have_systemctl` is PATH presence only —
# "can this box supervise a session at all" — and says yes on a box that has
# systemctl installed and no user bus to reach: a container, a user with no
# lingering and no login, a context with no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. So two
# conjuncts, both required: `systemd-run` on PATH, AND a user manager that
# answers `show-environment` over the bus. The second is the one that tells
# those boxes apart.
#
# THE CALLER EXPORTS THE BUS DEFAULTS FIRST. Nothing between these sentinels
# sets `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`: ccd defaults both at
# source time, below the block, and ccrc does it per function (`_inst_enable`'s
# idiom). Asked without them from a non-interactive context, this answers "no
# manager" on a box that has one, and the caller is handed the nohup arm.
#
# DARWIN ALWAYS ANSWERS 1. launchd has no transient service short of a plist
# written, bootstrapped and reaped per start — the trade `_svc_run_detached`
# declines for the same reason — so the nohup arm below IS the Darwin arm.
#
# ITS OWN FUNCTION so a harness can stub it by name, which is also why
# `_have_systemctl` is one.
_svc_have_user_manager() {   # -> 0 iff a transient user service can be started now
  if [ "$CCD_OS" = darwin ]; then return 1; fi
  command -v systemd-run >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl --user show-environment >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# `_svc_run_supervised` — start a LONG-LIVED process as one named transient
# user service (a slice, a restart policy, a log), or, where
# `_svc_have_user_manager` finds no manager, as a `nohup` child writing the
# same log. A sibling of `_svc_run_detached`, not an extension of it: that one
# fires a two-second job and takes none of those four things, and its argv is
# pinned as it stands (spec §7.1).
#
# SECRETS NEVER RIDE ARGV. A `--setenv=NAME=value` becomes the unit's
# `Environment=` property, which `systemctl --user show` prints to anyone who
# asks — measured 2026-09-23 on a live lane run by another launcher, whose
# gateway key sat in both tier units' `Environment=`. So a NAME whose LAST
# `_`-segment ENDS WITH KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD or PASSWD, in any case,
# is REFUSED, 64, and its value travels in <envfile>: systemd records only
# that file's PATH (`EnvironmentFiles=`), and the nohup arm sources it inside
# the child. The rule reads the TAIL, so `CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR` — LiteLLM's own
# name, which says where a credential lives — passes, and so does a secret
# word that is not last (`SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `…_TOKEN_FILE`). None of the five
# words contains `_`, so "the last segment ends with W" is the same test as
# "the NAME ends with W", which is how the `case` below spells it. A refusal
# names the NAME and never a value — not even for an argument it could not
# parse, which may be a value passed by mistake.
# The grammar is ENUMERATED bracket lists, never `[A-Z]`. A range is ASCII
# only while `globasciiranges` is on — bash 5's default, not the 4.4 floor's;
# with it off, en_US.UTF-8 lets `[!A-Za-z0-9_]` pass `É` (measured). A list can't.
#
# 64 IS A SHAPE, 1 IS A STATE. Shape: fewer than three leading arguments, an
# empty unit, a log or envfile that is not absolute (systemd takes neither
# relative, so neither arm does), a pair that is not NAME=value, no `--`, or
# nothing after it. State: an envfile that is not a readable file, a log that
# cannot be opened for append, a command the nohup arm cannot find. Every
# state is PROBED BEFORE ANYTHING STARTS, because neither arm can report it
# afterwards: a backgrounded child answers 0 whatever happens next, and
# `systemd-run` reports that the UNIT WAS CREATED, not that its process could
# start — the promise `_svc_run_detached`'s probe keeps, kept the same way.
#
# ONE CONTRACT, TWO ARMS. A unit's environment is the MANAGER's plus its
# pairs plus its file, never the caller's, so the nohup child starts from
# `env -i` as well: HOME, PATH, LANG when the caller has one, then the pairs,
# and nothing else the caller exported — an `ANTHROPIC_*`, `CHATGPT_*` or
# `CLAUDE_*` from a session pane cannot reach a tier. The file is sourced by
# a `sh` INSIDE that clean environment, after the pairs, because systemd
# documents `EnvironmentFile=` overriding `Environment=`. Listing its lines
# as `env` arguments instead would put the key in that process's argv, which
# `ps` shows to every user on the box. The child runs in `$HOME`, as
# `--working-directory` does, and its stdin is `/dev/null` explicitly,
# because a block sourced into an interactive shell has job control on,
# where an async job keeps the terminal. The envfile is read by two parsers —
# systemd's and the shell's — so its lines must be plain `NAME=value` with
# nothing to quote, which is the one shape its writer produces. What the
# nohup arm cannot give is the restart policy or a cgroup of its own: the
# child stays in the CALLER's, so a caller that forgot the bus defaults above
# loses the process with the pane that started it (spec §7.2).
#
# THE ANSWER IS ONE LINE ON STDOUT: `systemd <unit>`, or `nohup <pid>` where
# <pid> is the COMMAND's own — the child is a subshell that `exec`s `env`,
# which execs the `sh` that sources the file, which `exec`s `nohup`, which
# execs the command — so a later identity check reads the right
# `ps -o args=`. The redirect sits on that subshell, so a caller's `$(…)`
# returns at once instead of waiting on a pipe the child inherited.
_svc_run_supervised() {   # <unit> <log> <envfile|-> [NAME=value ...] -- <cmd> [args...]
  local use='_svc_run_supervised: usage: <unit> <log> <envfile|-> [NAME=value ...] -- <cmd> [args...]'
  if [ "$#" -lt 3 ]; then printf '%s — fewer than three arguments\n' "$use" >&2; return 64; fi
  local unit="$1" log="$2" envfile="$3" kv name n=3
  local -a pairs=()
  shift 3
  if [ -z "$unit" ]; then printf '%s — the unit name is empty\n' "$use" >&2; return 64; fi
  case "$log" in
    /*) ;;
    *) printf '%s — the log must be an absolute path\n' "$use" >&2; return 64 ;;
  esac
  case "$envfile" in
    -|/*) ;;
    *) printf '%s — the envfile must be - or an absolute path\n' "$use" >&2; return 64 ;;
  esac
  while [ "$#" -gt 0 ] && [ "$1" != -- ]; do
    kv="$1"; shift; n=$((n + 1))
    case "$kv" in *=*) name="${kv%%=*}" ;; *) name="" ;; esac
    case "$name" in
      ''|[0123456789]*|*[!ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_]*)
        printf '%s — argument %s is not NAME=value (not echoed: it may be a value)\n' "$use" "$n" >&2
        return 64 ;;
    esac
    case "$name" in
      *[Kk][Ee][Yy]|*[Tt][Oo][Kk][Ee][Nn]|*[Ss][Ee][Cc][Rr][Ee][Tt]|*[Pp][Aa][Ss][Ss][Ww][Oo][Rr][Dd]|*[Pp][Aa][Ss][Ss][Ww][Dd])
        printf '_svc_run_supervised: %s: refused %s — a secret travels in the envfile, never in argv or unit metadata\n' \
          "$unit" "$name" >&2
        return 64 ;;
    esac
    pairs+=("$kv")
  done
  if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then printf '%s — no -- before the command\n' "$use" >&2; return 64; fi
  shift
  if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then printf '%s — nothing to run after --\n' "$use" >&2; return 64; fi
  if [ "$envfile" != - ] && ! { [ -f "$envfile" ] && [ -r "$envfile" ]; }; then
    printf '_svc_run_supervised: %s: envfile %s is not a readable file — nothing was started\n' "$unit" "$envfile" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! { : >>"$log"; } 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '_svc_run_supervised: %s: log %s cannot be opened for append — nothing was started\n' "$unit" "$log" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if _svc_have_user_manager; then
    local -a sr=(--user --collect --quiet "--unit=$unit" --slice=app.slice "--working-directory=$HOME"
      -p Restart=always -p RestartSec=3 -p StartLimitIntervalSec=300 -p StartLimitBurst=20
      -p "StandardOutput=append:$log" -p "StandardError=append:$log")
    [ "$envfile" = - ] || sr+=(-p "EnvironmentFile=$envfile")
    for kv in ${pairs[@]+"${pairs[@]}"}; do sr+=("--setenv=$kv"); done
    systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1
    systemd-run "${sr[@]}" -- "$@" || return $?
    printf 'systemd %s\n' "$unit"
    return 0
  fi
  if ! command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '_svc_run_supervised: %s: %s is not a command here — nothing was started\n' "$unit" "$1" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  (
    cd -- "$HOME" || exit 1
    exec env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" ${LANG:+LANG="$LANG"} ${pairs[@]+"${pairs[@]}"} \
      sh -c 'if [ "$1" != - ]; then set -a; . "$1" || exit 1; set +a; fi; shift; exec nohup "$@"' \
      sh "$envfile" "$@"
  ) </dev/null >>"$log" 2>&1 &
  printf 'nohup %s\n' "$!"
  return 0
}
```

Notes an implementer needs about this text:
- **No top-level statement.** The insert is two definitions and comments. `runBlock`, the forced-Darwin describe,
  and every `source` of ccd or ccrc execute the region (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement). A top-level line would run in all of
  them.
- **Both definitions start at column 0 as `name() {`.** The membership regex `^(?:_plat_|_svc_)[a-z0-9_]+\(\)` sees
  nothing else. A `function _svc_x {` form, or an indented definition, would be invisible to it, so a misplaced
  copy would red neither check.
- **Loop exit and `--`.** The `while` exits only on `$# = 0` or on `$1 = --`. So `[ "$#" -eq 0 ]` right after it
  is exactly the "no `--`" test. A `[ "${1-}" != -- ]` there would be the same test spelled twice.
- **The empty-array idiom `${pairs[@]+"${pairs[@]}"}`** is the one ccd already uses (`grep -c '\[@\]+"\${' ccd/ccd`
  → 6). Both files run `set -uo pipefail` and never `-e` (`grep -n '^set -' ccd/ccd ccd/ccrc`). So the unchecked
  `systemctl --user reset-failed` cannot abort a caller.
- **GNU corpus:** the platform region is cut out of the scanned text for both files (`executableText`), so nothing
  here is scanned. Nothing here needs to be, either: `command -v`, `nohup`, `env -i`, `sh -c`, `printf` and `ps` are
  POSIX.
- **Why a `sh -c` inside `env -i` (ruling R2), and not the file's lines as `env` arguments.** Both give the child
  the same environment, with the file after the pairs. Listed as arguments, though, the gateway key would sit in
  `env`'s argv, which `ps` shows to every user on the box, for the life of that process. No case can catch that window
  (mutation row 43), so this sentence and the comment above the arm are the only guard on it. `env`, `sh` and
  `nohup` are all found on the caller's `PATH`, the same `PATH` the scrub keeps. The wrapper `sh` adds `PWD` to the
  child's environment (and, where `/bin/sh` is bash, `SHLVL`). Those are the shell's own variables, not the
  caller's.
- **Checked before writing this plan**, by running the definitions with shell-function stubs for `systemd-run` and
  `systemctl` (in memory, nothing written). **Re-checked on the text above after rulings R1 and R2**: bash 5.2.21,

**The rules, from S6-R11, in force for every sub-step:**
- **README first.** README is REPAIRED, never counted: its case is an equality with empty. It is re-pointed by
  content BEFORE anything is measured. A census measured first describes a tree that is about to change.
- **Everything else is RE-MEASURED from a dump, never retyped.** Each moved pin gets a `RE-MEASURED (Plan 2b-2
  Task 2)` paragraph naming its composition and its one cause.
- **Never widen a rule.** No function, regex, floor, exemption, `TOUCHED` entry or `CORPUS` entry in the describe
  changes. Neither frozen corpus document (the graphify spec, its plan-a) is edited. 6e checks this mechanically.
- **A gate that stops is reported, never argued past.** The gates are:
  - a corpus floor below its bound;
  - a non-empty FACT TWO `weak` set, or a moved FACT ONE set;
  - a moved RANGE BOUND list;
  - a `byFile` key other than `ccd/ccd` moving.

  None of those is a census re-measurement. Lowering a floor takes the argument that block's own comment demands
  ("a RE-MEASUREMENT of a floor, never a rule change"), and that is the controller's call.

**6b. Repair README by content.** The script reads README's two anchors FROM THE FILE with
`grep -o 'ccd/ccd:[0-9-]*' README.md` (ruling R41), never from this text. For each anchor, it first ASSERTS that
the lines it names at `BASE` hold the bytes its sentence quotes. Only then does it map those bytes into the working
file:
1. **The contended arm (`genrc == 1`)**, a three-line range. Its three lines at `BASE` must contain `genrc == 1`,
   and they must stand exactly once in the working file.
2. **`cmd_ensure`'s mint (`_reg_generation_init "$id"`)**, one line. That line at `BASE` must contain
   `_reg_generation_init "$id"`. The call's own line also stands outside `cmd_ensure` (at `36d62a1d`: `:10193`, and
   `:10348` after the insert), so the script matches the line together with its continuation line. It also requires
   the match to sit inside `cmd_ensure` at both trees, which is what the sentence says.

History, for the reader of an older draft. At `aed80210` the mint's anchor named a comment line inside
`cmd_ensure` that was green only through sub-rule A, so this step once carried a referent correction. CCR-15 wave 1
(#175) re-pointed it onto the call itself, and at `36d62a1d` both anchors are pure shifts. On a base where either
assertion fails, the script prints `STOP:` and exits 1. It never maps. Report the line to the controller. At
`36d62a1d`, this exact script STOPs when either anchor is put back to its old `aed80210` number
(`ccd/ccd:19776-19778` now names an unrelated comment, and `:20970` the first comment line of `cmd_ensure`'s body).
At the same base, the old literal-number script printed a unique but wrong mapping: `ccd/ccd:19776-19778 ->
ccd/ccd:19931-19933`.

```bash
BASE="$BASE" node --input-type=module <<'LOCATE'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
const BASE = process.env.BASE ?? '';
if (!/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(BASE)) throw new Error("set BASE to Step 0's sha first");
const stop = (why) => { console.error(`STOP: ${why}`); process.exit(1); };
const base = execFileSync('git', ['show', `${BASE}:ccd/ccd`], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 1 << 26 }).split('\n');
const tip = readFileSync('ccd/ccd', 'utf8').split('\n');
const readme = readFileSync('README.md', 'utf8').split('\n');
// every 1-based start where `blk` stands byte-identically in the working file
const at = (blk) => tip.flatMap((_, i) => (blk.every((l, k) => tip[i + k] === l) ? [i + 1] : []));
// a bash function's body, 1-based and inclusive: the audit's own `funcBody` rule
const body = (ls, name) => {
  const i = ls.findIndex((l) => new RegExp(`^${name}\\(\\)\\s*\\{`).test(l));
  if (i < 0) stop(`${name} is not defined`);
  let j = i + 1; while (!ls[j].startsWith('}')) j++;
  return [i + 1, j + 1];
};
// README's anchors, READ FROM THE FILE (ruling R41), never typed
const anchors = execFileSync('grep', ['-o', 'ccd/ccd:[0-9-]*', 'README.md'], { encoding: 'utf8' }).split('\n').filter(Boolean);
if (anchors.length !== 2) stop(`README carries ${anchors.length} ccd/ccd anchors, not the two this step repairs: ${anchors}`);
const QUOTES = ['genrc == 1', '_reg_generation_init "$id"'];
for (const a of anchors) {
  const where = readme.filter((l) => l.includes('`' + a + '`'));
  const q = QUOTES.filter((s) => where.length === 1 && where[0].includes(s));
  if (q.length !== 1) stop(`${a}: its README sentence must quote exactly one of ${QUOTES.join(' / ')}`);
  const [from, to = from] = a.slice('ccd/ccd:'.length).split('-').map(Number);
  const blk = base.slice(from - 1, to);
  // THE ASSERTION BEFORE THE MAPPING: the anchor names the bytes its sentence quotes, AT BASE
  if (!blk.some((l) => l.includes(q[0]))) stop(`${a} does not hold \`${q[0]}\` at ${BASE.slice(0, 8)}: ${JSON.stringify(blk)}`);
  // a one-line anchor is matched with its continuation line: the call's own line occurs twice in ccd/ccd
  const key = to > from ? blk : base.slice(from - 1, from + 1);
  const hit = at(key);
  if (hit.length !== 1) stop(`${a}: its bytes stand ${hit.length} times in the working file (${hit})`);
  if (q[0].startsWith('_reg_generation_init')) {
    const [b0, b1] = body(base, 'cmd_ensure'), [t0, t1] = body(tip, 'cmd_ensure');
    if (from < b0 || from > b1 || hit[0] < t0 || hit[0] > t1) stop(`${a}: the call is not inside cmd_ensure (${b0}-${b1} at BASE, ${t0}-${t1} now)`);
  }
  console.log(`${a} -> ccd/ccd:${hit[0]}${to > from ? `-${hit[0] + (to - from)}` : ''}   (${q[0]})`);
}
LOCATE
```

```bash
// node census-probe.mjs <path/to/session-hook.test.ts>
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
const f = process.argv[2];

const start = L.findIndex((l) => l.startsWith("describe('the compaction card — every line citation is anchored"));
if (start < 0) throw new Error('the describe is not in this file');
const put = [
  ["expect(resolved, 'references into tracked source that the walk resolved')",
    "DUMP('facts', { resolved, anchored, accepted: [...accepted].sort(), weak });"],
  ["expect(byFile, 'the citation debt moved",
    "DUMP('debt', { byFile, total: Object.values(byFile).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0), sites: r.failures.map((f) => `${f.doc}:${f.line} ${refKey(f)}`) });"],
  ["expect(r.failures.filter((f) => f.doc === 'readme')",
    "{ const ro = audit([['readme', fs.readFileSync(path.join(REPO, 'README.md'), 'utf8')]]); DUMP('readme', { inCorpus: r.failures.filter((f) => f.doc === 'readme').map(refKey), resolved: ro.resolved, checked: ro.checked }); }"],
  ["expect(set, 'a **Files:** reference stopped",

  ["expect(r.failures.map(refKey), 'a `|` row stopped",

  ["expect(r.failures.filter((f) => !(f.doc === 'plan' && f.line >= ledgerLine))",
    "DUMP('eof', r.failures.map(refKey));"],
];
for (const [marker, code] of put) {
  const hits = L.flatMap((l, k) => (k > start && l.includes(marker) ? [k] : []));
  if (hits.length !== 1) throw new Error(`${hits.length} matches for: ${marker}`);
  L.splice(hits[0], 0, '    ' + code);
}
L.splice(start + 1, 0, "  const DUMP = (n: string, v: unknown): void => { fs.writeFileSync(path.join(process.env.CENSUS_DUMP_DIR!, n + '.json'), JSON.stringify(v, null, 1)); };");

cat > "$S/census-diff.mjs" <<'DIFF'
// node census-diff.mjs <base-dump-dir> <tip-dump-dir>: the COMPOSITION of every set, and the gates
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
const [base, tip] = process.argv.slice(2);
const d = (dir, n) => JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(dir, n + '.json'), 'utf8'));
const ms = (a, b) => {
  const c = new Map(); for (const x of a) c.set(x, (c.get(x) ?? 0) + 1);
  const enter = []; for (const x of b) { if ((c.get(x) ?? 0) > 0) c.set(x, c.get(x) - 1); else enter.push(x); }
  const leave = []; for (const [x, n] of c) for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) leave.push(x);
  return { enter, leave };
};
const stop = (why) => { console.error(`STOP: ${why}`); process.exitCode = 1; };
const fB = d(base, 'facts'), fT = d(tip, 'facts');
console.log('facts: anchored', fB.anchored, '->', fT.anchored, '(floor 100); resolved', fB.resolved, '->', fT.resolved, '(floor 400)');
if (fT.anchored < 100 || fT.resolved < 400) stop('a corpus floor fell below its bound — that is not a census re-measurement');
if (JSON.stringify(fT.weak) !== '[]') stop(`FACT TWO: weak = ${JSON.stringify(fT.weak)}`);
if (JSON.stringify(fT.accepted) !== JSON.stringify(fB.accepted)) stop(`FACT ONE moved: ${JSON.stringify(fT.accepted)}`);
const r = d(tip, 'readme');
if (r.inCorpus.length || r.resolved !== 9 || r.checked !== 9) stop(`README is not repaired: ${JSON.stringify(r)} — repair README FIRST, then dump`);
const bB = d(base, 'debt'), bT = d(tip, 'debt');
const moved = Object.keys({ ...bB.byFile, ...bT.byFile }).filter((k) => bB.byFile[k] !== bT.byFile[k]);
console.log('byFile moved:', moved.map((k) => `${k} ${bB.byFile[k] ?? 0} -> ${bT.byFile[k] ?? 0}`).join(', ') || 'nothing');
console.log('total', bB.total, '->', bT.total);
if (moved.some((k) => k !== 'ccd/ccd')) stop('a key other than ccd/ccd moved, so "one cause" is not yet shown — measure it separately');
console.log('debt sites:', JSON.stringify(ms(bB.sites, bT.sites), null, 1));
const sB = d(base, 'files'), sT = d(tip, 'files');
console.log('**Files:** set', sB.set.length, '->', sT.set.length, JSON.stringify(ms(sB.set, sT.set)), 'only:', JSON.stringify(ms(sB.only, sT.only)));
const wB = d(base, 'rows'), wT = d(tip, 'rows');
console.log('|-row set', wB.set.length, '->', wT.set.length, JSON.stringify(ms(wB.sites, wT.sites), null, 1));
console.log('site twin', wB.twin.length, '->', wT.twin.length, JSON.stringify(ms(wB.twin, wT.twin), null, 1));
if (JSON.stringify(d(base, 'eof')) !== JSON.stringify(d(tip, 'eof'))) stop('THE RANGE BOUND ratchet moved');
DIFF
cat > "$S/census-repin.mjs" <<'REPIN'
// node census-repin.mjs <path/to/session-hook.test.ts> <tip-dump-dir> <para-dir>
// Rewrites the moved pins FROM THE DUMP, in the instrument's order, each after
// its RE-MEASURED paragraph (<para-dir>/{debt,total,rows,twin}.txt, already
// indented). It touches values and comments, never code.
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
const [file, dump, paraDir] = process.argv.slice(2);
const d = (n) => JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(dump, n + '.json'), 'utf8'));
const para = (n) => readFileSync(path.join(paraDir, n + '.txt'), 'utf8').replace(/\n$/, '').split('\n');
const L = readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n');
const one = (pred, what) => {
  const ix = L.flatMap((l, i) => (pred(l) ? [i] : []));
  if (ix.length !== 1) throw new Error(`${what}: ${ix.length} matches`);
  return ix[0];
};
const list = (marker) => {
  let a = one((l) => l.includes(marker), marker);
  while (!L[a].includes('toEqual([')) a++;
  let z = a + 1; while (!/^\s*\]\);$/.test(L[z])) z++;
  return { a, z, entries: L.slice(a + 1, z).filter((l) => /^\s*'[^']*',$/.test(l)).map((l) => l.trim().slice(1, -2)) };
};
const debt = d('debt'), rows = d('rows'), files = d('files');
// The **Files:** set and its complement are COMPARED, never rewritten here: the
// set carries a comment BETWEEN its entries, so a moved set is edited by hand,
// from the dump, in its order, with its own paragraph.
const FILES = "'a **Files:** reference stopped naming what its clause quotes — re-measure";
const ONLY = "'the stale references only this pass can see'";
if (JSON.stringify(list(FILES).entries) !== JSON.stringify(files.set)) throw new Error('the **Files:** set moved: edit it by hand from files.json');
if (JSON.stringify(list(ONLY).entries) !== JSON.stringify(files.only)) throw new Error('its only-this-pass list moved: edit it by hand from files.json');
// 1. the map's `ccd/ccd` entry
const e = one((l) => /^      'ccd\/ccd': \d+,$/.test(l), "'ccd/ccd' entry");
L.splice(e, 1, ...para('debt'), `      'ccd/ccd': ${debt.byFile['ccd/ccd']},`);
// 2. the headline
const t = one((l) => l.includes("expect(total, 'the narrated headline is the sum of the census, and this is it').toBe("), 'total');
L.splice(t, 1, ...para('total'), L[t].replace(/toBe\(\d+\);$/, `toBe(${debt.total});`));
// 3. the `|`-row set, then 4. its site-level twin: the leading comments kept,
// the paragraph appended after them, the entry block replaced from the dump.
const relist = (marker, entries, pname) => {
  const { a, z } = list(marker);
  let s = a + 1; while (/^\s*\/\//.test(L[s])) s++;
  let y = s; while (/^\s*'[^']*',$/.test(L[y])) y++;
  if (y !== z) throw new Error(`${marker}: its entries are not one contiguous block`);
  L.splice(s, y - s, ...para(pname), ...entries.map((x) => `        '${x}',`));
};
relist("'a `|` row stopped naming what the ROW quotes — re-measure'", rows.set, 'rows');
relist("'the rows this pass reads that another pass already reaches'", rows.twin, 'twin');
writeFileSync(file, L.join('\n'));
console.log(`repinned: ccd/ccd ${debt.byFile['ccd/ccd']}, total ${debt.total}, |-row ${rows.set.length}, twin ${rows.twin.length}`);
REPIN
```

**What this task deliberately does NOT do** (a reviewer rejects any of these as scope creep):

  the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement found in it), and not its callers.
- It adds no caller. Nothing in `ccd/ccd` or `ccd/ccrc` calls either new helper after this task. `_codex_start_tier`
  and `_codex_stop_tier` are later tasks.
- It exports no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` default, inside or outside the region.
- It creates no log directory. The caller `mkdir -p`s it; the helper only probes that the log opens.
- It adds no `_svc_*` stop, status or is-active helper for transient units. The lane library uses the existing
  `_svc_stop`/`_svc_is_active` or raw `systemctl`, as its own task decides.
- It adds no launchd arm (no plist, no `_svc_launchctl`) and edits no install, update, uninstall or doctor
  harness. No spine path reaches the helper yet, so none needs a recorder yet.
- Its citation repair stops at S6-R11's reach. In README it changes only the two `ccd/ccd:` anchors. In

**Hazards a later task must respect:**
1. **Callers export the bus defaults first.** Use ccrc's per-function idiom (`grep -n 'XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:=/run/user'
   ccd/ccrc`), or ccd's source-time defaults. A caller that forgets gets the nohup arm on a box that HAS a manager.
   Its tier then lives in the caller's cgroup (a pane scope) and dies with the pane. That is exactly what spec §7.2
   moved the tiers to `app.slice` to avoid.
2. **The nohup child gets ONLY what it is given.** Resolved by ruling R2: the nohup arm starts from `env -i` with
   `HOME`, `PATH` and `LANG` when set, then the pairs, then the envfile, so a caller's `ANTHROPIC_*`/`CHATGPT_*`/
   `CLAUDE_*` (or `OPENAI_*`, `LITELLM_*`, `DATABASE_URL`-shaped settings) cannot reach a tier from the caller, on
   either arm. The
   other side of that: everything else is gone too. That includes `TMPDIR`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `LC_*` and any proxy
   variable, and the child sees only the shells' own `PWD` besides. A tier that needs a variable gets it as a pair,
   or in the envfile if it is a secret. The two arms still differ in the base: the systemd arm's `PATH`, and
   anything the user manager imported, are the MANAGER's, while the nohup arm's `PATH` and `LANG` are the caller's.
   `_codex_start_tier` passes `HOME` as a pair anyway, so both arms agree on it.
3. **`runtime.env` must stay one plain `NAME=value` line.** It is parsed by systemd's `EnvironmentFile=` and by the
   `.` of the `sh` the nohup arm runs inside `env -i`. Quoting, spaces, `$` or a `export` prefix means the two arms
   read different values. `_codex_runtime_env_ensure`'s `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-<48 hex>` is inside the
   intersection. Keep it there.
4. **Any NAME a caller passes is subject to the refusal, and the refusal reads only the tail** (ruling R1). A NAME
   whose last `_`-segment ends with `KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` or `PASSWD` is refused (64). Everything
   else passes: `…_TOKEN_FILE`, `…_KEY_PATH` and `SECRET_KEY_BASE` all pass. So the name rule is a net for the
   usual spellings, not a gate. A secret passed under a name whose tail is innocent reaches `Environment=` in
   unit metadata. The contract that matters is the caller's: a secret ALWAYS goes in the envfile.
5. **Parse the answer line; never assume the arm.** `systemd <unit>` means no pid is known, so `_codex_tier_ours`
   reads `MainPID`. `nohup <pid>` is the command's own pid, so `ps -o args=` identity works on it. `<tier>.pid` is
   written only on the `nohup` answer.
6. **A `systemd-run` rc ≠ 0 prints no answer line.** On the systemd arm the helper relays `systemd-run`'s rc
   unchanged (a name collision on an active unit is systemd's `already exists` refusal). `_codex_start_tier` must
   treat any non-zero as "not started". Only `_codex_tier_ours` decides adoption, before the call.
7. **Every harness whose spine can now reach `systemd-run` needs a recorder IN THE SAME COMMIT** (design contract Global
   Constraints). The ccrc install, update, uninstall and doctor harnesses contain no `systemd-run` today
   (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement). `makeCcdHarness`'s rc-97 poisons make `_svc_have_user_manager` answer 1, so any ccd-side
   call there takes the nohup arm and REALLY runs its command in the background (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement). Stub
   `_svc_run_supervised` by name in such suites.
8. **The in-flight update-management W4 branch** asserts `systemd-run`'s exact argv in `ccrc-update.test.ts`
   (`[ "$1 $2 $3" = "--user --collect --quiet" ]`). This helper starts with the same three words. A spine step that
   reaches it inside `updateEnv` would satisfy that prefix check and add lines to W4's exact `systemd-run-argv`
   lists (the 2026-09-23 platform-layer measurement).
9. **The tier start limit (20 in 300 s) is a separate policy** from `claude-session@.service`'s and from ccd's
   `SUPERVISE_START_LIMIT_*` pair. `the start limit is one policy, not two` does not cover it, so do not "unify" the
   two by editing either.
10. **The line tax.** This is the plan's only ccd/ccd edit, which is why Step 6 repairs the census here (ruling
    R35, amending R15). Any LATER `ccd/ccd` or `ccd/ccrc` edit re-opens Step 6's numbers, whether it lands in this
