```bash
# ── `ccrc codex` — a Codex lane's two tiers, RUN (Plan 2b-2 Task 5) ────────
# The lane library above this block ANSWERS questions (Task 4). What follows
# ACTS on them, and redefines none of them (ruling R5):
#   - `_codex_ready_secs`: the one parse of CCRC_CODEX_READY_S (ruling R27);
#   - `_codex_lock` / `_codex_unlock`: the one per-lane lock (ruling R11), and
#     its only release (ruling R19);
#   - `_codex_start_tier` / `_codex_stop_tier` / `_codex_stop_lane`: the
#     design contract's interfaces, which the models op (Task 6), account removal's
#     codex arms (Task 8), the install spine (Task 10) and uninstall (Task 11)
#     also call;
#   - `cmd_codex` and its three verbs, and the `login` arm that routes to
#     `_codex_login` (ruling R18).
#
# IDENTITY BEFORE ACTION, both ways (spec §7.4; ruling R8, D-3488):
#   - start never adopts, and never kills, a listener or unit it cannot
#     identify as this lane's — the dated incident of one lane attaching to
#     another's gateway;
#   - stop stops a tier ONLY when `_codex_tier_ours` proves it this lane's
#     (0 running, 4 starting), and only through the handle that proved it.
#     Anything else is left running and named: on the fleet box the other
#     repository's live tiers run under these same unit names;
#   - a pidfile naming a live process that does not prove this lane is STALE,
#     not foreign (ruling R34): start deletes it, stop removes it, and neither
#     ever signals its pid.
#
# Refusals print through `_codex_say`. The code `usage` exits 2 (this file's
# EXIT CODES table; ruling R3); every other code exits 1.

# The readiness bound `start` waits for both tiers inside, in whole seconds:
# `CCRC_CODEX_READY_S`, default 90, and a value that is empty or not all
# digits falls back to 90. The lane lock's wait is this plus 30, because the
# longest holder is a start waiting out its own bound. PUBLIC (ruling R27):
# the install spine's restart (Task 10) waits on the same bound, so it asks
# this function and never parses the variable itself. Prints the number with
# no newline; always rc 0.
_codex_ready_secs() {
  local s="${CCRC_CODEX_READY_S:-90}"
  case "$s" in ''|*[!0-9]*) s=90 ;; esac
  printf '%s' "$(( 10#$s ))"
}

# `ccrc codex`'s two dependencies, proven before any lane is read (ruling R22).
# jq reads every lane's roster row, lane.json and tier records; node runs
# deploy/models-op.mjs, lane.json's one writer. Without this probe a missing
# jq reads as `roster-invalid` (Task 4's hazard 9), naming the wrong remedy.
# `_models_deps` is NOT reused: it dies through `_ccrc_die` as `ccrc: … is
# required by 'ccrc models' …`, which is neither this verb's refusal shape nor
# its name.
_codex_deps() {   # -> rc 0; rc 1 + one missing-dependency line naming each tool that is absent
  local t miss='' verb=is
  for t in jq node; do
    command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || miss="${miss:+$miss and }$t"
  done
  [ -z "$miss" ] && return 0
  case "$miss" in *' and '*) verb=are ;; esac
  _codex_say missing-dependency "$miss $verb not on PATH, and 'ccrc codex' needs both: jq reads every lane's roster row and lane.json, and node runs ${CCRC_HERE%/*}/deploy/models-op.mjs, lane.json's one writer. Install what is missing, or put it on PATH, then re-run. Nothing was read, started or stopped."
  return 1
}

# `_codex_lock <id>` — THE ONE PER-LANE LOCK (ruling R11): an exclusive
# `flock` on `~/.ccrc/codex/<id>/.lock`, held by THIS shell until
# `_codex_unlock` or exit. Every path that starts or stops a tier takes it
# before it asks `_codex_tier_ours` anything: `ccrc codex start|stop`,
# `_acct_remove`'s codex arms, `_models_litellm_lane`, `_inst_codex_tiers`,
# `_uninst_codex`. A tier is provable only once its handle exists, so without
# the lock two starters can both read "not running" and both start it, and a
# stop can stop the tier a start is waiting on.
# - THE CONTRACT (ruling R19). rc 0 with the lock HELD and CX_LOCK_FD set
#   (CX_LOCK_ID = <id>); rc 0 with CX_LOCK_FD EMPTY where `flock` is missing;
#   rc 1 (one refusal line) and rc 2 (usage) with CX_LOCK_FD empty.
#   `_codex_unlock` is the ONLY release: no caller closes CX_LOCK_FD itself,
#   because a closed fd left in CX_LOCK_FD would read, to the next call in
#   this shell, as this lane's lock still held.
# - ONE LEVEL. flock attaches to the open file description, so a second open
#   of this path in this shell is a stranger to the first and would wait on a
#   lock this very process holds (`_acct_marker_lock` says the same of its
#   own). The functions the entry points call — `_codex_start_tier`,
#   `_codex_stop_tier`, `_codex_stop_lane` — take none. A second call for the
#   lane this shell already holds is a no-op; a call for another lane releases
#   the first through `_codex_unlock` (one lane's lock per shell).
# - THE FD MUST NOT REACH A TIER. A process forked while the lock is held
#   inherits the fd and holds the lock for its whole life (measured), so
#   `_codex_start_tier` closes CX_LOCK_FD inside each spawn's substitution,
#   and any new spawn path must do the same. That close drops a subshell's
#   copy only; it is not a release.
# - Where `flock` is missing, rc 0 with nothing held and CX_LOCK_FD empty:
#   starts and stops then run unserialised, which is this race's behaviour
#   without the lock and no worse. install requires flock on macOS, and
#   util-linux ships it on Linux.
_codex_lock() {   # <id> -> rc 0 held (CX_LOCK_FD set) or no flock (CX_LOCK_FD empty); rc 1 + one refusal line; rc 2 usage
  local id="${1:-}" d fd bound
  _codex_shape || return 1
  if ! [[ "$id" =~ $WRAPPER_ID_RE ]]; then
    _codex_say usage "'$id' is not an account id, so no lane lock is built from it."
    return 2
  fi
  if [ -n "${CX_LOCK_FD:-}" ]; then
    [ "${CX_LOCK_ID:-}" = "$id" ] && return 0
    _codex_unlock
  fi
  command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  d="$(_codex_lane_dir "$id")"
  if ! { [ -d "$d" ] || ( umask 077 && mkdir -p -- "$d" ); } 2>/dev/null \
     || ! { exec {fd}>>"$d/.lock"; } 2>/dev/null; then
    _codex_say lane-unwritable "$d/.lock could not be opened, so this start or stop cannot be serialised against another on lane $id. Fix $d, then re-run. Nothing was started or stopped."
    return 1
  fi
  bound=$(( $(_codex_ready_secs) + 30 ))
  if ! flock -w "$bound" "$fd"; then
    exec {fd}>&-   # never held and never published, so this is no release
    _codex_say tier-not-ready "another 'ccrc codex' start or stop has held lane $id's lock ($d/.lock) for ${bound}s without finishing. 'ccrc codex status $id' shows the lane; re-run once that has ended. Nothing was started or stopped."
    return 1
  fi
  CX_LOCK_FD="$fd"; CX_LOCK_ID="$id"
  return 0
}

# THE ONLY RELEASE of `_codex_lock` (ruling R19): closes CX_LOCK_FD when set
# and clears CX_LOCK_FD and CX_LOCK_ID both. A no-op when nothing is held.
_codex_unlock() {   # always rc 0
  if [ -n "${CX_LOCK_FD:-}" ]; then exec {CX_LOCK_FD}>&-; fi
  CX_LOCK_FD=''; CX_LOCK_ID=''
  return 0
}

# Names what a 2 from `_codex_tier_ours` found, for start's refusal and
# stop's notice alike, so the two say the same thing about one fact. Call it
# DIRECTLY, right after that 2: it reads CX_TIER_WHY and `_codex_row`'s CX_*,
# and it sets CX_FOREIGN_CODE, CX_FOREIGN_WHAT and CX_FOREIGN_FIX.
#   - A live unit of this tier's name, whatever else answers: `unit-foreign`.
#     Asked first because it is the fleet box's incident shape, the other
#     repository's tier under this lane's unit name (m-livebox §3). Ruling R34
#     keeps it foreign: that unit is not ccrc's to call stale.
#   - Anything else holding the port: `port-foreign`.
# A pidfile naming a live process that does not prove this lane is never a 2
# (ruling R34): it is a stale pidfile, which `_codex_tier_ours` reads past, so
# it has no sentence here.
_codex_foreign_what() {   # <id> <tier>
  local id="$1" tier="$2" unit port
  CX_FOREIGN_CODE=''; CX_FOREIGN_WHAT=''; CX_FOREIGN_FIX=''
  if [ "$tier" = litellm ]; then port="$CX_LITELLM"; else port="$CX_PROXY"; fi
  if unit="$(_codex_unit "$id" "$tier")" && _svc_have_user_manager; then
    case "$(_svc_is_active "$unit")" in
      active|activating|deactivating|reloading|refreshing)
        CX_FOREIGN_CODE=unit-foreign
        CX_FOREIGN_WHAT="the unit $unit is active but is not $id's $tier tier: its MainPID's command line does not prove this lane"
        CX_FOREIGN_FIX="If another tool runs a lane under this name, stop that lane with that tool first."
        return 0 ;;
    esac
  fi
  CX_FOREIGN_CODE=port-foreign
  case "${CX_TIER_WHY:-}" in
    listener-answers-other-lane)
      CX_FOREIGN_WHAT="port $port ($id's $tier tier) is held by a listener that is not this lane's: it answers as another lane" ;;
    listener-unresponsive)
      CX_FOREIGN_WHAT="port $port ($id's $tier tier) is held by a listener that is not this lane's: it completes no connection inside the probe bound" ;;
    *)
      CX_FOREIGN_WHAT="port $port ($id's $tier tier) is held by a listener that is not this lane's: its identity check failed" ;;
  esac
  CX_FOREIGN_FIX="Stop whatever holds port $port, or give $id other ports in ~/.ccrc/accounts.json."
  return 0
}

# `_codex_start_tier <id> <tier>` — start ONE tier through the platform layer's
# supervised helper. It never re-checks identity and takes no lock: its callers
# hold `_codex_lock` and asked `_codex_tier_ours` first, and this runs only on
# a 1.
# - ONE MEASUREMENT names both the interpreter and the record. The argv's
#   python is the generation `_codex_started_json` resolved (D-3480:
#   resolved, never `current`, because a process started through the symlink
#   keeps the unresolved path as sys.prefix and would load a later
#   generation's files). `<tier>.started` is that function's output and
#   nothing else, so `_codex_tier_stale` compares like with like.
# - The argv is built from Task 4's helpers, so it is exactly what
#   `_codex_pid_is_tier` proves: litellm's `--config <lane dir>/litellm.yaml`
#   as two words, and the shim's `<shim file> --ccrc-lane=<id>` (ruling R6 —
#   the shim reads no argv, so the word is inert to it, and it is the only
#   lane-specific thing the shim's command line can carry).
# - LITELLM RUNS ISOLATED, `-I -m` (ruling R45), as the shim already does.
#   Both arms start a tier in $HOME, and `-m` without `-I` puts the working
#   directory first on sys.path, so a `~/litellm/` would load instead of the
#   generation's litellm, the one `ccgpt-runtime`'s own `-I` probe proved.
# - The gateway key reaches LiteLLM ONLY as `runtime.env`, an EnvironmentFile
#   (spec §5.4). The shim gets no env file, because it is value-blind
#   (m-tiers §5).
# - THE LOCK FD IS CLOSED INSIDE EACH SPAWN'S SUBSTITUTION. A tier forked while
#   the caller holds the lane's flock would inherit the fd and hold the lock
#   for its whole life, so every later start and stop would wait out its bound
#   (measured: the control kept the lock after its parent exited). The close
#   happens in the `$( … )` subshell only, so the caller keeps its lock.
# - A PIDFILE HERE IS STALE (ruling R34). This runs only on a 1, so a
#   `<tier>.pid` names no live process, or a live one whose command line does
#   not prove this lane (pid reuse, or a hand edit). It goes BEFORE the spawn,
#   on both arms, and its pid is never signalled: that process is somebody
#   else's. On the unit arm nothing else would remove the file, and on either
#   arm a failed spawn would otherwise leave it behind.
_codex_start_tier() {   # <id> <tier> -> rc 0 + "systemd <unit>" | "nohup <pid>" on stdout; rc 1 + one refusal line; rc 2 usage
  local id="${1:-}" tier="${2:-}" d unit rec gen py log ans rc p
  _codex_row "$id" || return $?
  if ! _codex_tier_ok "$tier"; then
    _codex_say usage "a tier is one of: $CODEX_TIERS (got '$tier')."
    return 2
  fi
  d="$(_codex_lane_dir "$id")"
  if ! unit="$(_codex_unit "$id" "$tier")"; then
    _codex_say lane-unwritable "$d/lane.json names no usable $tier unit, so there is no name to run $id's $tier tier under. 'ccrc codex start $id' re-renders it; if it still names none, run 'ccrc models $id init codex'."
    return 1
  fi
  if ! "$(_codex_runtime_cli)" python >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _codex_say runtime-absent "no LiteLLM runtime is current on this box, so $id's $tier tier has no interpreter to start from. Build one with 'ccgpt-runtime build' (or 'ccrc update', which builds it), then re-run."
    return 1
  fi
  if ! rec="$(_codex_started_json "$tier")"; then
    if [ "$tier" = shim ]; then
      _codex_say runtime-absent "the lane shim $(_codex_shim_file) is missing or unreadable, so $id's shim tier has nothing to run. 'ccrc update' places it; re-run after."
    else
      _codex_say runtime-absent "the current runtime generation carries no readable stamp (.ccrc-runtime.json), so what $id's litellm tier would run cannot be recorded. Rebuild it with 'ccgpt-runtime build --force', then re-run."
    fi
    return 1
  fi
  gen="$(printf '%s' "$rec" | jq -r '.generation // empty' 2>/dev/null)" || gen=''
  py="$gen/bin/python"
  if [ -z "$gen" ] || [ ! -x "$py" ]; then
    _codex_say runtime-absent "the current runtime's interpreter ${gen:+$py }is not executable, so $id's $tier tier cannot start. Rebuild it with 'ccgpt-runtime build --force', then re-run."
    return 1
  fi
  log="$HOME/.ccrc/logs/codex/$id/$tier.log"
  # 0700: a tier's log can carry request fragments on an error path.
  if ! ( umask 077; mkdir -p -- "${log%/*}" ) 2>/dev/null; then
    _codex_say lane-unwritable "${log%/*} could not be created, so $id's $tier tier would have nowhere to log. Fix that directory, then re-run."
    return 1
  fi
  if ! rm -f -- "$d/$tier.pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    _codex_say lane-unwritable "$d/$tier.pid is a stale pidfile (it names no running tier of $id's) and could not be removed. Fix $d, then re-run. Nothing was started."
    return 1
  fi
  _codex_bus_defaults
  if [ "$tier" = litellm ]; then
    ans="$( [ -z "${CX_LOCK_FD:-}" ] || exec {CX_LOCK_FD}>&-
      _svc_run_supervised "$unit" "$log" "$d/runtime.env" \
        "CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR=$HOME/$CX_AUTH" LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True "HOME=$HOME" \
        -- "$py" -I -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config "$d/litellm.yaml" --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$CX_LITELLM" )"; rc=$?
  else
    ans="$( [ -z "${CX_LOCK_FD:-}" ] || exec {CX_LOCK_FD}>&-
      _svc_run_supervised "$unit" "$log" - \
        "CCGPT_ACCOUNT_ID=$id" "CCGPT_PROXY_PORT=$CX_PROXY" "CCGPT_LITELLM_PORT=$CX_LITELLM" "HOME=$HOME" \
        -- "$py" -I "$(_codex_shim_file)" "--ccrc-lane=$id" )"; rc=$?
  fi
  ans="${ans##*$'\n'}"
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    _codex_say tier-not-ready "$id's $tier tier could not be started: the platform helper answered rc $rc (its reason is the line above). Read $log; 'ccrc codex status $id' shows what is running."
    return 1
  fi
  case "$ans" in
    "systemd $unit")
      # The unit is the handle. Any stale pidfile went before the spawn.
      : ;;
    "nohup "*)
      p="${ans#nohup }"
      case "$p" in ''|*[!0-9]*) p='' ;; esac
      if [ -z "$p" ] || ! { printf '%s\n' "$p" > "$d/$tier.pid.$$" && mv -f -- "$d/$tier.pid.$$" "$d/$tier.pid"; }; then
        rm -f -- "$d/$tier.pid.$$"
        _codex_say lane-unwritable "$id's $tier tier was started under nohup (\"$ans\"), but its pid could not be recorded in $d/$tier.pid, and without it nothing can stop it by verified identity. Stop it by hand, fix $d, then re-run."
        return 1
      fi ;;
    *)
      _codex_say tier-not-ready "the platform helper answered \"$ans\" for $id's $tier tier, which names neither its unit nor a pid. Read $log."
      return 1 ;;
  esac
  if ! { printf '%s\n' "$rec" > "$d/$tier.started.$$" && mv -f -- "$d/$tier.started.$$" "$d/$tier.started"; }; then
    rm -f -- "$d/$tier.started.$$"
    _codex_say lane-unwritable "$id's $tier tier IS running, but $d/$tier.started could not be written, so the next update will read that tier as stale and restart it. Fix $d."
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$ans"
}

# `_codex_stop_tier <id> <tier>` — stop ONE tier, IDENTITY FIRST (ruling R8,
# D-3488, which departs from spec §7.4's "by exact unit, then by
# verified identity"). It takes no lock: its callers hold `_codex_lock`.
#   1. It stops the tier ONLY when `_codex_tier_ours` answers 0 (ours,
#      running) or 4 (ours, starting), and only through the handle that proof
#      came through: the unit, by the exact name lane.json gives it, when the
#      proof was the unit's MainPID (CX_TIER_VIA=systemd); the verified pid
#      when it was the pidfile's (nohup). A unit is never stopped for its NAME,
#      because on the fleet box the other repository's live tiers run under
#      these same names (m-livebox §3). A service-owned pid is never killed
#      around its unit, because `Restart=always` would race the kill.
#   2. A 2 (foreign: a listener on the port, or a same-named unit whose
#      MainPID is not this lane's) is LEFT RUNNING and named on stderr, and the
#      word is `foreign`. A 3 stops nothing and is stop-failed, because "down"
#      cannot be claimed over a tier nobody measured.
#   3. MEASURED AGAIN. The answer is what runs now, not what was asked: this
#      lane's tier still answering (0 or 4) is stop-failed. Otherwise the
#      tier's `.pid`/`.started` go. They describe no running tier of this
#      lane. A pidfile naming a live process that does not prove this lane is
#      ccrc's own STALE file (ruling R34): `_codex_tier_ours` read past it, the
#      word is `not running`, and the file goes WITHOUT its pid ever being
#      signalled.
_codex_stop_tier() {   # <id> <tier> -> rc 0 + "stopped" | "not running" | "foreign" on stdout; rc 1 + one stop-failed line; rc 2 usage
  local id="${1:-}" tier="${2:-}" d unit q pid did='not running' n note=''
  _codex_row "$id" || return $?
  if ! _codex_tier_ok "$tier"; then
    _codex_say usage "a tier is one of: $CODEX_TIERS (got '$tier')."
    return 2
  fi
  d="$(_codex_lane_dir "$id")"
  _codex_tier_ours "$id" "$tier"; q=$?
  case "$q" in
    0|4)
      pid="$CX_TIER_PID"
      case "$CX_TIER_VIA" in
        systemd)
          if unit="$(_codex_unit "$id" "$tier")" && _svc_stop "$unit"; then did=stopped; fi ;;
        nohup)
          kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null
          n=0
          while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && [ "$n" -lt 10 ]; do sleep 1; n=$(( n + 1 )); done
          if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null
            n=0
            while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && [ "$n" -lt 5 ]; do sleep 1; n=$(( n + 1 )); done
          fi
          did=stopped ;;
      esac ;;
    3)
      _codex_say stop-failed "$id's $tier tier could not be measured, so nothing was stopped and it cannot be called down. 'ccrc codex status $id' shows what answers."
      return 1 ;;
  esac
  _codex_tier_ours "$id" "$tier"; q=$?
  case "$q" in
    0|4)
      if [ -z "$CX_TIER_VIA" ]; then
        _codex_say stop-failed "$id's $tier tier answers as this lane, but neither a unit nor a pidfile of this lane's holds it, so there is no verified handle to stop it by: it was started outside ccrc and must be stopped by hand."
      else
        _codex_say stop-failed "$id's $tier tier is still running after the stop ($CX_TIER_VIA${CX_TIER_PID:+, pid $CX_TIER_PID}). 'ccrc codex status $id' shows it; re-run the stop, or stop it by hand."
      fi
      return 1 ;;
    3)
      _codex_say stop-failed "$id's $tier tier could not be measured after the stop, so it cannot be called down. 'ccrc codex status $id' shows what answers."
      return 1 ;;
    2)
      _codex_foreign_what "$id" "$tier"
      note="$CX_FOREIGN_WHAT — ccrc left it running"
      [ "$did" = stopped ] || did=foreign ;;
  esac
  rm -f -- "$d/$tier.pid" "$d/$tier.started"
  [ -z "$note" ] || printf '%s codex: %s: %s.\n' "$PROG" "$id" "$note" >&2
  printf '%s\n' "$did"
}

# `_codex_stop_lane <id>` — both tiers, the FRONT one first: the shim closes
# before the gateway behind it (the live launcher's own order, m-tiers §3).
# Both are always attempted, so one tier that will not stop never leaves the
# other running. It takes no lock: its callers hold `_codex_lock`. It RETURNS,
# never exits, because account removal's codex arm (Task 8, ruling R16) calls
# it between `_codex_lock` and `_codex_unlock`, BEFORE the roster drop (the
# stop reads the row's ports and lane.json's unit names), and must still print
# its envelope; that arm reaps the files with Task 4's `_codex_reap_files`
# only AFTER the drop.
_codex_stop_lane() {   # <id> -> rc 0 + "litellm <word>, shim <word>" on stdout; rc 1 when a tier of this lane still runs (its line is on stderr); rc 2 usage
  local s l rc=0
  _codex_row "${1:-}" || return $?
  s="$(_codex_stop_tier "$CX_ID" shim)" || rc=1
  l="$(_codex_stop_tier "$CX_ID" litellm)" || rc=1
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || return 1
  printf 'litellm %s, shim %s\n' "$l" "$s"
}

# `ccrc codex start <id>` — the idempotent ensure the launcher runs on every
# session start.
# - EVERY REFUSAL LANDS BEFORE ANYTHING IS SPAWNED: login, runtime, config and
#   BOTH tiers' identity are all decided first. A refusal here is a session that
#   dies at once, and ccd parks one that dies five times in 120 s as FAILED
#   (m-ccd-launcher §3); a half-started lane would be a second problem on top.
# - It holds the lane lock (ruling R11) from before the key is minted until it
#   exits, so a second start waits and then adopts, and a stop waits for this
#   start to finish.
# - 0 (ours, running) and 4 (ours, starting: ruling R7) are adopted, never
#   started over; 1 is started; 2 is refused by name; 3 has already said why.
#   Then it waits, bounded, until both tiers answer as this lane (0).
# - A KEY MINTED OR REPLACED UNDER THIS LANE'S LITELLM (ruling R21) restarts
#   that tier: stopped, identity-gated, after every refusal has been decided,
#   then started from the new runtime.env, under this start's lock, before the
#   readiness wait.
_codex_cmd_start() {   # <id>
  local id d py tier q lq=1 sq=1 lv='' lp='' sv='' sp='' via pid out h hl='' hs='' limit t0 rekey=0
  _codex_row "${1:-}" || exit $?
  id="$CX_ID"
  _codex_lane_json_ensure "$id" || exit 1
  d="$(_codex_lane_dir "$id")"
  if [ ! -f "$HOME/$CX_AUTH/auth.json" ]; then
    _codex_say not-logged-in "$id has no OAuth login: ~/$CX_AUTH holds no auth.json (existence is all ccrc checks; it never reads one). Log the lane in with 'ccrc codex login $id', then re-run. Nothing was started."
    exit 1
  fi
  py="$("$(_codex_runtime_cli)" python 2>/dev/null)" || py=''
  if [ -z "$py" ] || [ ! -x "$py" ]; then
    _codex_say runtime-absent "no LiteLLM runtime is current on this box ('ccgpt-runtime python' answered none). Build one with 'ccgpt-runtime build' (or 'ccrc update', which builds it), then re-run. Nothing was started."
    exit 1
  fi
  _codex_lock "$id" || exit 1
  _codex_runtime_env_ensure "$id" || exit 1
  # Read at once, in this shell (Task 4's hazard 3): the ensure's own answer.
  case "$CX_ENV_ACTION" in created|replaced) rekey=1 ;; esac
  if [ ! -f "$d/litellm.yaml" ]; then
    _codex_say litellm-unrendered "$id has no LiteLLM config at $d/litellm.yaml, so its gateway would start with no model list. Render it with 'ccrc models litellm $id', then re-run. Nothing was started."
    exit 1
  fi
  for tier in $CODEX_TIERS; do
    _codex_tier_ours "$id" "$tier"; q=$?
    case "$q" in
      0|1|4) ;;
      2)
        _codex_foreign_what "$id" "$tier"
        _codex_say "$CX_FOREIGN_CODE" "$CX_FOREIGN_WHAT. ccrc never adopts or stops what it cannot identify. $CX_FOREIGN_FIX Nothing was started."
        exit 1 ;;
      *) exit 1 ;;   # 3: `_codex_tier_ours` has printed why
    esac
    if [ "$tier" = litellm ]; then lq="$q"; lv="$CX_TIER_VIA"; lp="$CX_TIER_PID"
    else sq="$q"; sv="$CX_TIER_VIA"; sp="$CX_TIER_PID"; fi
  done
  # A KEY THAT CHANGED UNDER A RUNNING LITELLM (ruling R21; Task 4's hazard
  # 4). LiteLLM reads LITELLM_MASTER_KEY from runtime.env once, when it
  # starts, and the launcher reads runtime.env on every session start. So a
  # file the ensure above created or replaced while this lane's LiteLLM runs
  # (0) or is starting (4) would hand the session a key its gateway refuses.
  # That tier is stopped here, through `_codex_stop_tier` (identity-gated, so
  # it stops only what proves this lane's), and the loop below starts it from
  # the new file. `kept` and `rechmod` are the key it already holds. The shim
  # holds no key (m-tiers §5) and is never restarted for one. Whatever takes
  # the port between this stop and that start is never adopted or killed: the
  # start then fails by name, `tier-not-ready`.
  if [ "$rekey" -eq 1 ] && [ "$lq" -ne 1 ]; then
    _codex_stop_tier "$id" litellm >/dev/null || exit 1
    lq=1
  fi
  for tier in $CODEX_TIERS; do
    if [ "$tier" = litellm ]; then q="$lq"; via="$lv"; pid="$lp"; else q="$sq"; via="$sv"; pid="$sp"; fi
    if [ "$q" -eq 1 ]; then
      out="$(_codex_start_tier "$id" "$tier")" || exit 1
      h="started ($out)"
    else
      case "$via" in
        systemd) h="adopted (systemd $(_codex_unit "$id" "$tier"))" ;;
        nohup)   h="adopted (nohup $pid)" ;;
        *)       h="adopted (a listener answering as $id that no unit or pidfile of this lane's holds)" ;;
      esac
    fi
    if [ "$tier" = litellm ]; then hl="$h"; else hs="$h"; fi
  done
  limit="$(_codex_ready_secs)"
  t0=$SECONDS
  while :; do
    _codex_tier_ours "$id" litellm; lq=$?
    _codex_tier_ours "$id" shim; sq=$?
    [ "$lq" -eq 0 ] && [ "$sq" -eq 0 ] && break
    if [ $(( SECONDS - t0 )) -ge "$limit" ]; then
      tier=litellm; [ "$lq" -eq 0 ] && tier=shim
      _codex_say tier-not-ready "$id's $tier tier did not answer as this lane within ${limit}s. Read $HOME/.ccrc/logs/codex/$id/$tier.log. What was started was left under its unit or pid: 'ccrc codex status $id' reports it, and 'ccrc codex stop $id' stops it."
      exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$PROG codex: $id: litellm $hl, shim $hs"
}

# `ccrc codex stop <id>` — both tiers, identity-gated (ruling R8), under the
# lane lock (ruling R11). Exit 0 whenever no tier of this lane still runs,
# including when a foreign one was left running and named.
_codex_cmd_stop() {   # <id>
  local out
  _codex_row "${1:-}" || exit $?
  _codex_lock "$CX_ID" || exit 1
  out="$(_codex_stop_lane "$CX_ID")" || exit 1
  printf '%s\n' "$PROG codex: $CX_ID: $out"
}

# `ccrc codex status <id> [--json]` — READ-ONLY (no lock, no ensure), and exit
# 0 whatever it finds. A tier is `running` (this lane's, answering, and how it
# is held), `starting` (this lane's proven handle, its port not answering
# yet: ruling R7), `stopped` (a stale pidfile included: ruling R34),
# `foreign` (something answers on its port or holds its unit, and is not this
# lane's), or `unknown` (it could not be asked, which is never folded into
# `foreign`).
_codex_cmd_status() {   # <id> <1 = --json>
  local id json="$2" d py gen='' lane tier q state via pid sg port
  local ls='' lv='' lp='' ss='' sv='' sp=''
  # A variable, not the literal, as the `${via:-…}` default below: bash reads
  # an apostrophe inside a double-quoted `${…:-word}` as a quote (measured,
  # bash 5.2: `unexpected EOF while looking for matching`).
  local nohandle="held by no unit or pidfile of this lane's"
  _codex_row "${1:-}" || exit $?
  id="$CX_ID"
  d="$(_codex_lane_dir "$id")"
  py="$("$(_codex_runtime_cli)" python 2>/dev/null)" || py=''
  if [ -n "$py" ]; then gen="${py%/bin/python}"; gen="${gen##*/}"; fi
  lane="$(_codex_lane_json_state "$id")" || lane=''
  for tier in $CODEX_TIERS; do
    _codex_tier_ours "$id" "$tier"; q=$?
    via=''; pid=''
    case "$q" in
      0) state=running;  via="$CX_TIER_VIA"; pid="$CX_TIER_PID" ;;
      4) state=starting; via="$CX_TIER_VIA"; pid="$CX_TIER_PID" ;;
      1) state=stopped ;;
      2) state=foreign ;;
      *) state=unknown ;;
    esac
    if [ "$tier" = litellm ]; then ls="$state"; lv="$via"; lp="$pid"; else ss="$state"; sv="$via"; sp="$pid"; fi
  done
  if [ "$json" -eq 1 ]; then
    jq -cn --arg id "$id" --arg ls "$ls" --arg lv "$lv" --arg lp "$lp" \
      --arg ss "$ss" --arg sv "$sv" --arg sp "$sp" --arg gen "$gen" --arg lane "$lane" '
      def s: if . == "" then null else . end;
      def n: if . == "" then null else tonumber end;
      {id: $id,
       tiers: {litellm: {state: $ls, via: ($lv | s), pid: ($lp | n)},
               shim:    {state: $ss, via: ($sv | s), pid: ($sp | n)}},
       runtime: {generation: ($gen | s)},
       lane: {json: ($lane | s)}}'
    return 0
  fi
  for tier in $CODEX_TIERS; do
    if [ "$tier" = litellm ]; then state="$ls"; via="$lv"; pid="$lp"; else state="$ss"; via="$sv"; pid="$sp"; fi
    if [ "$tier" = litellm ]; then port="$CX_LITELLM"; else port="$CX_PROXY"; fi
    case "$state" in
      running)
        sg="$(jq -r '.generation // empty' "$d/$tier.started" 2>/dev/null)" || sg=''
        printf '%s\n' "$PROG codex: $id: $tier running (${via:-$nohandle}${pid:+, pid $pid}${sg:+, started from ${sg##*/}})" ;;
      starting)
        printf '%s\n' "$PROG codex: $id: $tier starting ($via${pid:+, pid $pid}) — this lane's, and port $port does not answer yet" ;;
      stopped)
        printf '%s\n' "$PROG codex: $id: $tier stopped" ;;
      foreign)
        printf '%s\n' "$PROG codex: $id: $tier FOREIGN — port $port or its unit answers, but not as this lane's $tier; ccrc will neither adopt nor stop it" ;;
      *)
        printf '%s\n' "$PROG codex: $id: $tier UNKNOWN — its state could not be measured" ;;
    esac
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$PROG codex: $id: runtime ${gen:-absent}; lane.json ${lane:-unknown}"
}

# `ccrc codex {start|stop|status|login} <id>` — the lane's lifecycle verb (D-3479).
# The usage parse comes first and reads nothing. The role gate comes next: a
# server-role box runs no sessions, so it runs no lanes, and it is refused
# before any lane is read or locked. Then the dependency probe (ruling R22),
# so no subcommand reads a lane without jq and node. `login` rides the same
# parse and the same two gates (ruling R18), and its body, Task 8's
# `_codex_login`, takes the one parsed id and re-checks no arity.
cmd_codex() {
  case "${1:-}" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
  esac
  local sub="${1:-}" id json=0
  case "$sub" in
    start|stop|status|login) shift ;;
    '') _codex_say usage "ccrc codex needs a subcommand: ccrc codex {start|stop|status|login} <id> (status also takes --json)."; exit 2 ;;
    *)  _codex_say usage "ccrc codex has no subcommand \"$sub\" in this build; it implements start, stop, status and login."; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  id="${1:-}"
  case "$id" in
    ''|-*) _codex_say usage "ccrc codex $sub needs a lane id: ccrc codex $sub <id>. 'ccrc status' lists this box's accounts."; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
  if [ "$sub" = status ] && [ "${1:-}" = --json ]; then json=1; shift; fi
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    _codex_say usage "ccrc codex $sub takes one lane id$([ "$sub" = status ] && printf ' and an optional --json'), and got \"$1\"."
    exit 2
  fi
  if [ -f "$BOX_ENV_FILE" ] && [ -r "$BOX_ENV_FILE" ] \
      && [ "$(_box_env_value "$BOX_ENV_FILE" CCRC_ROLE)" = server ]; then
    _codex_say server-role "this box records CCRC_ROLE=server in $BOX_ENV_FILE, and a server box runs no sessions, so no Codex lane either. Run 'ccrc codex $sub $id' on the fleet box."
    exit 1
  fi
  _codex_deps || exit 1
  _codex_bus_defaults
  case "$sub" in
    start)  _codex_cmd_start "$id" ;;
    stop)   _codex_cmd_stop "$id" ;;
    status) _codex_cmd_status "$id" "$json" ;;
    login)  _codex_login "$id" ;;
  esac
}
```

  The `login` arm's function, `_codex_login`, is Task 8's (ruling R18), placed by Task 8 directly above `cmd_codex`.
  Until that commit, `ccrc codex login <id>` on a box that passes both gates reaches an undefined function (bash's
  `_codex_login: command not found`, exit 127). The plan is squash-merged, so that interval never reaches `main`, and
  no case in this task runs `login` past the role gate and the probe.

  No Task 4 function is edited (ruling R5). Task 4's `_codex_lane_json_ensure` already asks `_codex_lane_json_state`
  before it writes, and `status` asks the same function, so lane.json's one comparison exists once.

```bash
git add ccd/ccrc server/test/codexLaneFixture.ts server/test/ccrc-codex.test.ts server/test/ccrc-cli.test.ts
# ONLY if Step 5's citation census redded and was repaired here (ruling R35):
#   git add README.md server/test/session-hook.test.ts   — and say why in the message below
git commit -m "feat(gpt-lane): ccrc codex start|stop|status — the lane runs, in fixtures

cmd_codex runs a codex lane's two tiers through _svc_run_supervised:
transient units where a user manager answers, nohup where none does.
start refuses before it spawns (login, runtime, config, and both tiers'
identity), adopts what already answers as this lane or is still
starting, and waits, bounded, until both answer. The shim's argv carries
--ccrc-lane=<id>, so its pid is provable, and LiteLLM runs under -I, so
no directory in \$HOME can shadow the generation's litellm. stop stops a
tier only once it is proven this lane's, through the handle that proved
it, and leaves anything else running, named: a same-named unit that is
not this lane's is never stopped. A pidfile naming a live process that
proves no lane is stale, not foreign: start deletes it, stop removes it, and neither
signals its pid. A gateway key minted or replaced under a running
LiteLLM restarts that tier before readiness. status reads, never writes.
Every start and stop takes the per-lane _codex_lock, whose fd no tier
inherits, and _codex_unlock is its only release. cmd_codex proves jq
and node before it reads any lane, and routes the login subcommand,
whose function lands with the login door.

The fixture's systemd-run now RUNS what it is handed, with a manager's
environment, inside codexLaneFixture.ts' one state layout, so the census
asserts argv and process facts together. The fixture also exports the
stand-in LiteLLM (fakeLitellmSource, spawnFakeLitellm), a rendered lane
config (plantLaneConfig) and the port, wait and process helpers, so
later suites import them instead of declaring their own. The usage-line
pin in ccrc-cli.test.ts moved to name codex.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

**Why:**

*A codex lane cannot run on today's `_models_litellm`.*
- The config path is one box-global line. `grep -n '^_models_litellm_path()' ccd/ccrc` finds
  `${CCGPT_CONFIG:-$HOME/.handoff/litellm-config.yaml}`, the file the other repository's live LiteLLM reads
  (m-verbs §4).
- The "is it running" check is `pgrep -f "litellm .*<that path>"`. On the live box that pattern matches the other
  repository's process.
- The stop is a bare `ccgpt stop`. `grep -n 'command -v ccgpt' ccd/ccrc` finds it; with no id it acts on the live
  launcher's first lane, whichever lane changed (m-ccd-launcher §5).
- A ccrc-owned tier is started with `--config $HOME/.ccrc/codex/<id>/litellm.yaml` (design contract, `_codex_start_tier`).
  Without this task, nothing ever writes that file.

*The fix is all in `ccd/ccrc`* (spec §8). The op takes its destination from the caller and computes no path of its own:
`grep -n "litellm: { keys" deploy/models-op.mjs` finds `['file','id','template','out','commit']`.

*The external arm must not move a byte.*
- The live lanes are `external` rows (D-3169).
- OpenClaw's LiteLLM reads the box-global file.
- Plan 3 retires this arm at cutover (D-3482).

So the external body of `_models_litellm` stays verbatim, behind a one-line dispatch, and so does
`_models_litellm_running`. The existing external cases already pin the box-global path, `calls('ccgpt') ==
['stop']`, the refusal, and the "never reaches a real pgrep" poison. This task adds two characterisation pins:
- the exact `pgrep` argv;
- that `CCGPT_CONFIG` still redirects the external arm, and that the lane library is never asked.

*The kind predicate has one legitimate reader.*
- `grep -n 'exec\.kind' ccd/ccrc | grep -c jq` returns 0: there is no bash reader of `exec.kind` in this file today.
- `accounts.sh`'s `CCRC_CODEX_BACKEND` is keyed on `telemetry`, so it names today's external live lanes (m-spine H8).
- Therefore the dispatch asks Task 4's `_codex_lanes`, which reads `exec.kind` off `accounts.json`.
- An unreadable roster makes `_codex_lanes` answer rc 1 with no ids (Task 4), and the predicate reads that as "not
  codex", discarding the library's `ccrc codex: roster-invalid:` line, which would be the wrong verb's prefix in a
  `ccrc models` run. That sends the call to the external arm, but nothing can be written there: phase 1 hands the
  same file to the op, and `readRoster` refuses before rendering, with its own sentence
  (`grep -n 'const r = readRoster(a.file)' deploy/models-op.mjs`).

*Why the codex arm does not go through `_models_litellm_running`.*
- `_codex_tier_ours` answers five ways (ruling R7). `_models_litellm_running` is boolean-by-nonzero, and the
  poisoned-`pgrep` case (`grep -n "never reaches a real pgrep or ccgpt" server/test/ccrc-models.test.ts`) pins that an
  rc of 97 reads as "not running".
- Folding the five answers into that boolean would collapse "foreign" or "cannot ask" into one of their neighbours,
  which is the overloaded-return defect CLAUDE.md names.
- So the arm asks `_codex_tier_ours` directly, with one arm per answer:
  - 0 (ours, running) and 4 (ours, starting): stop, write, start. R7 makes a starting tier ours, so it is stopped like
    a running one. A tier still importing litellm may already have read the old bytes, and it is this lane's to stop.
  - 1: write;
  - 2: refuse `tier-foreign`, with nothing written. ccrc can neither prove that the foreign process does not hold the
    old bytes nor stop it (design contract: "never kill").
  - 3, or any code outside the five (a library that is not there answers 127): refuse `tier-unmeasured`, with
    nothing written, carrying the library's own sentence. That sentence names the remedy, such as a row
    `_codex_row` refused. Reporting it as `tier-foreign` would name a listener that may not exist.
- Only 0 and 4 reach `_codex_stop_tier` (ruling R8, `D-3488`). A 2 or a 3 is LEFT RUNNING and named in the
  refusal. The stop itself is by exact unit name or verified pid, which is `_codex_stop_tier`'s own gate (Task 5).

*The lane lock (ruling R11).* Every path that starts or stops a tier takes the lane's `_codex_lock`, and this arm is
one of them.
- **What it covers.** It is taken BEFORE phase 1, so one critical section holds the whole decision: compare, ask
  the tier, stop, write, start. It is serialised against `ccrc codex start|stop`, the install spine and another
  render. Taken only after "changed", the lock would let two renders both see "changed", and the second would stop
  the tier the first had just started, to write the same bytes. An unchanged render takes it too. That costs one
  `flock`, and at worst an hourly refresh waits behind a start's readiness wait.
- **Its scope is one render.** `_models_litellm_lane` takes it inside a subshell around the body, so the lock is
  released the moment the render ends. Its fd, too, never outlives that render in the calling shell. A caller that
  renders two lanes in one shell therefore holds each lane's lock only for that lane's render. Otherwise the first
  lane's fd would stay open under the second lane's work, and a tier started there would inherit it for its whole
  life. `_models_refuse` still ends the render with its one JSON object on stdout, because the subshell's stdout is
  the caller's.
- **One level.** `_codex_litellm_ensure` runs inside `ccrc codex start` (`_codex_cmd_start`), which already holds
  this lane's lock. It therefore calls the body, `_models_litellm_lane_held`, and never `_models_litellm_lane`.
  `_codex_lock` is RE-ENTRANT in the holding shell (ruling R38): a second call there returns 0 at once, because
  `CX_LOCK_ID` already names the lane, so nothing here would deadlock or wait out the bound — a deadlock arises
  only through a second RAW open of `.lock`, bypassing that check. The one-level rule holds anyway, because it
  keeps one render's lock scope to exactly one `_models_litellm_lane` call and keeps the fake's call log
  (`laneCalls()`) honest about which call actually took the lock.
- **Called in the arm's own shell.** `_codex_lock` is the one library call made OUTSIDE a `( … )`, with stdout
  discarded, because a lock taken in a subshell is released as that subshell exits. The arm therefore relies on its
  contract of returning, which the install spine needs as well.

*Why START follows the write here and not in the external arm.* This arm stopped a tier that live sessions were using.
The external arm never owned its tier, and it leaves the restart to whatever session starts that lane next (R40:
paraphrased — the shipped external-arm log line this restates names the live lane by its live id, which no line this
plan adds may spell). If a write fails after
the stop, the tier starts again on the bytes still on disk: the box is back where it was, and the next run sees the
same difference and retries, which is the doctrine's own property.

*The directory mode.* The op's `grep -n "mkdirSync(path.dirname(a.out)" deploy/models-op.mjs` carries no mode, and
`runtime.env` lives in that directory. Carry-forward 9 already explains why a later `mkdir` cannot tighten it. The
directory is absent when a lane was `external` at `init` and is later flipped to `codex` (the Plan 3 cutover): the
registry exists, but `lane.json` and its directory do not. In that state `ccrc models litellm <id>` is the first
writer, so this arm creates the directory `umask 077` first. It does so before the lane lock, whose file lives in
that directory.

*`.remedy` (carry-forward 10).*
- m-spine §8 measured that the fix site is `_models_answer`, not `_models_summary`, which serves only `show`, whose
  bodies never carry `.remedy`.
- `grep -n "answer.remedy" deploy/models-op.mjs` finds exactly 2 sites: `init` with an unseeded probe, and
  `HAIKU_UNASSIGNED_REMEDY` in the mutation tail.
- `_models_answer` has no human line today, so both reach only stdout JSON.

*Why this suite fakes the library by name, not with `plantSystemd`.* `ccrc-models.test.ts`'s `env()` rewrites its
`systemctl` poison unconditionally on EVERY `run()` (`grep -n "poison('systemctl'" server/test/ccrc-models.test.ts`),
so a functional `systemctl` planted by `plantSystemd` would be clobbered before it answered. What is claimed here is
what the models arm DOES with each answer the library can give, and a fake that holds one answer still measures
exactly that. `ccd/ccrc` is sourced, which is what the `BASH_SOURCE` guard at its foot is for (`grep -n 'BASH_SOURCE\[0\]}" == "${0}"' ccd/ccrc`,
the `sourceCall` idiom of `ccrc-account.test.ts`). The named functions are redefined, and one call is made. Three
cases still run REAL library code:
- A: an idle lane must answer 1 in this box, through the real `_codex_tier_ours` and the real `_codex_lock`;
- M: the real `_codex_start_tier`'s `--config` must be the path this arm wrote, on a runtime planted by Task 4's
  `plantFakeRuntime` and named by the real `ccgpt-runtime` (ruling R28);
- real-lock: Task 5's real `_codex_lock` must be held at the tier question, the stop and the start, and released
  when the render returns. The fakes probe it from outside with `flock -n`, which opens the lock file afresh. That
  is a new open file description, which a held lock refuses, so "held" is a measured fact about the lock and not
  about a variable.

These three are the cross-task seams that the fakes cannot see.

  ```ts
  // ── Task 6 (D-3482): the lane library, faked BY NAME ──────────
  // The codex arm of `_models_litellm` asks four bash FUNCTIONS (the lane
  // library and its lock), not two binaries on PATH, so the `pgrep`/`ccgpt` PATH stubs this
  // file uses for the external arm cannot reach it. It is faked the way
  // `ccrc-account.test.ts`'s `sourceCall` reaches a function: `ccd/ccrc` is
  // SOURCED (the `BASH_SOURCE` guard at its foot exists for this), the named
  // functions are redefined, and one call is made. Not `plantSystemd`
  // (codexLaneFixture.ts): `env()` above re-plants its `systemctl` poison on
  // EVERY `run()`, so a functional systemctl would be overwritten before it
  // answered — and the claim here is what the models arm DOES with each
  // answer, which a fake holding one answer still measures directly.
  //
  // A knob is `<home>/fake/<fn>-<id>` holding a code; absent → the fake's
  // default. A NON-ZERO knob EXITS rather than returns, the way a `ccrc codex`
  // refusal does, and every fake prints a stray line on STDOUT: a call site
  // that forgot its subshell, or its `>/dev/null`, breaks the one-object
  // envelope and reds, instead of passing on a fake that behaved politely.
  // ONE EXCEPTION, `_codex_lock`: its knob RETURNS. A lock taken
  // in a subshell is released as the subshell exits, so the arm calls it in
  // its own shell and relies on its contract of returning — which the
  // install spine's callers need as well.
  //
  // `_fk_probe` measures the REAL lock from OUTSIDE, only when
  // `<home>/fake/probe-lock` exists: `flock -n` opens the lock file afresh,
  // a new open file description, which a held flock refuses. It is off by
  // default so no fake case creates a `.lock` file of its own.
  const LANE_FAKE_PRELUDE = [
    '_fk_log() { printf \'%s\\n\' "$1" >> "$HOME/lane-calls"; }',
    // what the lane's config held AT THE MOMENT of the call: a STOP must see
    // the old bytes and a START the new ones — the ordering is the claim
    '_fk_cfg() { local f="$HOME/.ccrc/codex/$1/litellm.yaml"; if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then echo absent; elif grep -q "model_name:" "$f"; then echo new; else echo old; fi; }',
    '_fk_rc() { local k="$HOME/fake/$1-$2" rc="$3"; [ -f "$k" ] && rc="$(cat "$k")"; [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && return 0; exit "$rc"; }',
    '_fk_probe() { [ -f "$HOME/fake/probe-lock" ] || return 0; if flock -n "$HOME/.ccrc/codex/$1/.lock" true 2>/dev/null; then echo "$2 free"; else echo "$2 held"; fi >> "$HOME/lock-probe"; }',
  ].join('\n');
  const LANE_FAKES = {
    // The library's own sentence goes to STDERR, the way a `_codex_row`
    // refusal behind a 3 does: the arm must carry it, not discard it.
    ours: '_codex_tier_ours() { _fk_log "ours $1 $2"; _fk_probe "$1" ours; echo "stray library stdout"; echo "fake library sentence for $1" >&2; _fk_rc ours "$1" 1; }',
    stop: '_codex_stop_tier() { _fk_log "stop $1 $2 cfg=$(_fk_cfg "$1")"; _fk_probe "$1" stop; echo "stray library stdout"; _fk_rc stop "$1" 0; }',
    start: '_codex_start_tier() { _fk_log "start $1 $2 cfg=$(_fk_cfg "$1")"; _fk_probe "$1" start; echo "stray library stdout"; _fk_rc start "$1" 0; }',
    lock: '_codex_lock() { _fk_log "lock $1"; echo "stray library stdout"; local k="$HOME/fake/lock-$1"; [ -f "$k" ] && return "$(cat "$k")"; return 0; }',
    // Only for the one case that runs the REAL `_codex_start_tier`: records the
    // argv it is handed, one word per line, and answers as the systemd arm does.
    svc: '_svc_run_supervised() { printf \'%s\\n\' "$@" > "$HOME/svc-argv"; printf \'systemd %s\\n\' "$1"; }',
  } as const;
  type LaneFake = keyof typeof LANE_FAKES;

  /** `ccd/ccrc` sourced, `fakes` redefined over the real library, then `call`
   *  (e.g. `cmd_models litellm codex-a`). `umask 022` first, so a directory
   *  mode this file asserts is this code's and not the runner's. */
  function sourced(call: string, fakes: LaneFake[], extra: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {}): Result {
    const script = ['umask 022', `. "${join(home, 'ccrc', 'ccd', 'ccrc')}"`, LANE_FAKE_PRELUDE,
      ...fakes.map((f) => LANE_FAKES[f]), call].join('\n');
    const r = spawnSync(BASH, ['-c', script], { env: env(home, extra), encoding: 'utf8', input: '' });
    return { code: r.status ?? -1, stdout: r.stdout ?? '', stderr: r.stderr ?? '' };
  }

  const laneCalls = (): string[] => {
    const p = join(home, 'lane-calls');
    return fs.existsSync(p) ? fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : [];
  };

  /** What `_fk_probe` saw of the lane lock, one `<fake> held|free` per call. */
  const lockProbe = (): string[] => {
    const p = join(home, 'lock-probe');
    return fs.existsSync(p) ? fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : [];
  ```

  ```ts
      // `plantFakeRuntime` (Task 4's rule). Never hand-write a generation here,
      // and never weaken the assertions.
      plantCodexBins(home);
      plantFakeRuntime(home);
      // Generated, never asserted by value (global constraint).
      fs.writeFileSync(join(laneDir('codex-a'), 'runtime.env'),
        `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-${randomBytes(24).toString('hex')}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
      const r = sourced('cmd_models litellm codex-a', ['lock', 'ours', 'stop', 'svc']);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      const argv = fs.readFileSync(join(home, 'svc-argv'), 'utf8').split('\n');
      expect(argv[0]).toBe('ccgpt-codex-a-litellm.service');
      const at = argv.indexOf('--config');
      expect(at, argv.join(' ')).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
      expect(argv[at + 1]).toBe(lanePath('codex-a'));
      expect(argv[at + 1]).toBe(String(oneObject(r)['path']));
      expect(fs.readFileSync(argv[at + 1]!, 'utf8')).toContain('model_name:');
    });

    it('a runner\'s own lane-library bounds never reach the child, and `extra` still sets one (ruling R23)', () => {
      // A runs the REAL `_codex_tier_ours`, whose probe bound is
      // `CCRC_CODEX_PROBE_S`, and A and real-lock run the REAL `_codex_lock`,
      // whose wait derives from `CCRC_CODEX_READY_S`. The knobs are planted on
      // THIS process for two calls and then restored, so the pin measures
      // env()'s deletion and not a runner that happens to be clean.
      const knobs = ['CCRC_CODEX_PROBE_S', 'CCRC_CODEX_READY_S'] as const;
      const saved = knobs.map((k) => process.env[k]);
      const show = 'printf \'%s|%s\\n\' "${CCRC_CODEX_PROBE_S-unset}" "${CCRC_CODEX_READY_S-unset}"';
      const seen = (() => {
        for (const k of knobs) process.env[k] = '1';
        try {
          return { inherited: sourced(show, []), passed: sourced(show, [], { CCRC_CODEX_READY_S: '7' }) };
        } finally {
          knobs.forEach((k, i) => {
            const v = saved[i];
            if (v === undefined) delete process.env[k]; else process.env[k] = v;
          });
        }
      })();
      expect(seen.inherited.stdout).toBe('unset|unset\n');
      // The control: only the INHERITED value is dropped, so a case that
      // wants a bound still passes one.
      expect(seen.passed.stdout).toBe('unset|7\n');
    });

    describe('_codex_litellm_ensure — `ccrc codex start` renders an ABSENT config through the same arm', () => {
      it('absent: rendered through the codex arm, with NOTHING on stdout (ccrc codex prints its own line), and the lane lock is NOT taken again', () => {
        const r = sourced('_codex_litellm_ensure codex-a', ['lock', 'ours', 'stop', 'start']);
        expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
        expect(r.stdout).toBe('');
        expect(fs.readFileSync(lanePath('codex-a'), 'utf8')).toContain('model_name:');
        // No `lock` line: the one caller, `ccrc codex start`, already holds
        // this lane's lock, and `_codex_litellm_ensure` never calls
        // `_codex_lock` again — the real lock is RE-ENTRANT there and would
        // return 0 at once rather than deadlock (R38), but a second call
        // here would still blur one render's lock scope across two levels
        // and add a spurious `lock` line to the fake's call log.
        expect(laneCalls()).toEqual(['ours codex-a litellm']);
      });

      it('present: left alone, whatever it holds — staleness is refresh\'s question, not start\'s', () => {
        fs.writeFileSync(lanePath('codex-a'), OLD);
        const r = sourced('_codex_litellm_ensure codex-a', ['lock', 'ours', 'stop', 'start']);
        expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
        expect(fs.readFileSync(lanePath('codex-a'), 'utf8')).toBe(OLD);
        expect(laneCalls()).toEqual([]);
      });

      it('a render that refuses is ONE `ccrc codex: litellm-unrendered:` line carrying the op\'s own remedy, rc 1', () => {
        fs.rmSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'models', 'codex-a.json'));   // never probed
        const r = sourced('_codex_litellm_ensure codex-a', ['lock', 'ours', 'stop', 'start']);
        expect(r.code).toBe(1);
        expect(r.stdout).toBe('');
        const lines = r.stderr.split('\n').filter(Boolean);
        expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
        expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^ccrc codex: litellm-unrendered: /);
        expect(lines[0]).toContain("'ccrc models refresh codex-a'");
        expect(fs.existsSync(lanePath('codex-a'))).toBe(false);
      });

      it('never takes the EXTERNAL arm, even handed an id that is not a codex lane', () => {
        // `_codex_cmd_start` gates on `_codex_row` first, so this is belt and braces —
        // but the external arm's failure mode is the live box's box-global
        // file and a bare `ccgpt stop`, so the braces are measured. R40: the
        // non-codex id here is `router2`, the tree's existing external row —
        // never a live lane id.
        writeCatalogue('router2');
        expect(run(['models', 'router2', 'init', 'codex']).code).toBe(0);
        sourced('_codex_litellm_ensure router2', ['lock', 'ours', 'stop', 'start']);
        expect(fs.existsSync(boxGlobal())).toBe(false);
        for (const name of ['pgrep', 'ccgpt']) expect(poisonLog(name), name).toEqual([]);
      });

      it('`ccrc codex start` asks for it under the lane lock, after the gateway key and before any tier is adopted or started', () => {
        // A behavioural pin needs Task 5's whole start harness (auth, runtime,
        // readiness), which this file does not build; that START reaches this
        // step is pinned on the start sequence's own text. START_FN is
        // `_codex_cmd_start` (ruling R17), the function whose body runs `ccrc
        // codex start`'s sequence. `cmd_codex` only parses, gates and
        // dispatches `start` to it.
        const START_FN = '_codex_cmd_start';
        const src = fs.readFileSync(CCRC_SRC, 'utf8');
        const m = new RegExp(`^${START_FN}\\(\\) \\{[^\\n]*\\n([\\s\\S]*?)\\n\\}$`, 'm').exec(src);
        expect(m, `ccd/ccrc has no ${START_FN}`).toBeTruthy();
        const code = m![1]!.split('\n').filter((l) => !l.trim().startsWith('#'));
        const at = (fn: string): number[] =>
          code.flatMap((l, i) => (new RegExp(`(?:^|[\\s;&|(])${fn}\\s`).test(l) ? [i] : []));
        const ensure = at('_codex_litellm_ensure');
        expect(ensure, `${START_FN} calls _codex_litellm_ensure exactly once`).toHaveLength(1);
        // The ensure runs the arm's body WITHOUT taking the lane lock, so the
        // lock must already be held — taken by this function, earlier.
        expect(at('_codex_lock').some((i) => i < ensure[0]!),
          'the lane lock is taken before the config is rendered').toBe(true);
        // The interim absent-config refusal this call replaces is gone.
        expect(code.filter((l) => l.includes('litellm-unrendered')),
          `${START_FN} no longer spells the interim litellm-unrendered refusal`).toEqual([]);
        const key = at('_codex_runtime_env_ensure').filter((i) => i < ensure[0]!);
        expect(key.length, 'the gateway key is ensured before the config').toBeGreaterThan(0);
        const tiers = [...at('_codex_tier_ours'), ...at('_codex_start_tier')];
        expect(tiers.filter((i) => i > key[key.length - 1]! && i < ensure[0]!),
          'no tier is adopted or started between the gateway key and the config').toEqual([]);
        expect(tiers.some((i) => i > ensure[0]!), 'and the tier loop follows it').toBe(true);
      });
    });
  });
  ```

  Old (unique, because `PROG=ccrc` follows it once):

  ```bash
      *) _models_refuse no-answer 1 "deploy/models-op.mjs exited $rc, outside this build's 0/1/2 contract, after printing a JSON object — its own exit code broke, not yours. ccrc and deploy/models-op.mjs ship together and must be one build.   New:
  ```

  ```bash
      *) _models_refuse no-answer 1 "deploy/models-op.mjs exited $rc, outside this build's 0/1/2 contract, after printing a JSON object — its own exit code broke, not yours. ccrc and deploy/models-op.mjs ship together and must be one build. Re-run the install (or redeploy), then re-run this. Nothing was written." ;;
    esac
    # THE REMEDY reaches the human stream too (carry-forward 10). The op puts
    # a `.remedy` on exactly two answers — `init` of an unseeded probe, and a
    # mutation that leaves a codex lane's haiku null — and before this line
    # both reached only the JSON a person never reads: mutations have no
    # summary, and `_models_summary` serves `show`, whose bodies carry none
    # (m-spine §8 — this is the site, not that function). STDERR, the stream
    # `_models_refuse` already uses for its sentence; stdout keeps its one
    # object. Keyed on the field being a string, so an answer without one
    # prints nothing here.
    printf '%s' "$body" \
      | jq -r --arg p "$PROG" 'if (.remedy | type) == "string" then "\($p): \(.remedy)" else empty end' >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$body"
    return "$rc"
  ```

- [ ] **Step 4: The per-lane path, the kind predicate, the codex arm, and the dispatch.**

  (a) Replace the path helper. Old:

  ```bash
  # Where a box keeps LiteLLM's config, and the template it is rendered from. The
  # destination is the ONE thing `ccgpt` and this verb must agree about
  # (`infra/handoff/ccgpt:20` reads `${CCGPT_CONFIG:-$HOME/.handoff/litellm-config.yaml}`),
  # so the same override is honoured here.
  _models_litellm_path()     { printf '%s' "${CCGPT_CONFIG:-$HOME/.handoff/litellm-config.yaml}"; }
  _models_litellm_template() { printf '%s' "$CCRC_HERE/../deploy/litellm-config.template.yaml"; }
  ```

  New:

  ```bash
  # Where a box keeps LiteLLM's config, and the template it is rendered from.
  # TWO ARMS, and the CALLER picks (spec §8, D-3482):
  #   - no argument: the EXTERNAL lane's box-global file — byte for byte what
  #     this helper answered before it took one. The destination is the ONE
  #     thing `ccgpt` (another repository's live launcher) and this verb must
  #     agree about (`infra/handoff/ccgpt:20` reads
  #     `${CCGPT_CONFIG:-$HOME/.handoff/litellm-config.yaml}`), so the same
  #     override is honoured here.
  #   - an id: that CODEX-kind lane's own file, the one ccrc's own tier is
  #     started against (`_codex_start_tier`'s --config). UNCONDITIONAL, on
  #     purpose: this helper never reads the roster, so no caller holding an id
  #     — a reap after the roster row is gone included — can ever be answered
  #     with the box-global path, which an identity check would then match
  #     against the OTHER repository's live LiteLLM. And CCGPT_CONFIG, that
  #     repository's variable, never redirects a lane ccrc owns. Which arm a
  #     lane takes is `_models_litellm_codex`'s question, not this helper's.
  _models_litellm_path() {   # [<codex accountId>] -> the LiteLLM config file
    [ $# -eq 0 ] || { printf '%s' "$(_codex_lane_dir "$1")/litellm.yaml"; return 0; }
    printf '%s' "${CCGPT_CONFIG:-$HOME/.handoff/litellm-config.yaml}"
  }
  _models_litellm_template() { printf '%s' "$CCRC_HERE/../deploy/litellm-config.template.yaml"; }
  ```

  (b) Above the existing comment that begins `# "Is LiteLLM up against this config?"`, add ONE comment line.
  Leave the `_models_litellm_running()` line itself byte-identical:

  ```bash
  # The EXTERNAL arm's question only — a codex-kind lane asks `_codex_tier_ours` (`_models_litellm_lane_held`, below).
  ```

  (c) Insert the three new functions after the `_models_litellm_running()` line and its blank line, immediately above
  `# STOP-THEN-WRITE (fix round 1, this task's controller ruling). Restart is`:

  ```bash
  # WHICH ARM (D-3482): `exec.kind == "codex"` read off
  # ~/.ccrc/accounts.json by the lane library's ONE reader of that question
  # (`_codex_lanes`) — never accounts.sh's CCRC_CODEX_BACKEND, which is keyed
  # on `telemetry` and names today's EXTERNAL live lanes. An unreadable roster
  # (`_codex_lanes` rc 1, no ids) answers "not codex" here and still cannot
  # write through the external arm: that arm's PHASE 1 hands the same file to
  # the op, whose `readRoster` refuses before anything is rendered, in its own
  # sentence. The library's `ccrc codex: roster-invalid:` line is discarded,
  # because it would be the wrong verb's prefix in a `ccrc models` run.
  _models_litellm_codex() {   # <accountId> -> 0 iff the roster row is exec.kind "codex"
    local l
    while IFS= read -r l; do [ "$l" = "$1" ] && return 0; done < <(_codex_lanes 2>/dev/null)
    return 1
  }

  # THE CODEX ARM of `_models_litellm` (spec §8, D-3482): the lane's
  # LOCK, then the body (`_models_litellm_lane_held`, below).
  # THE LANE LOCK: every ccrc path that starts or stops a tier
  # takes `_codex_lock <id>`, and this arm does both. It is taken BEFORE the
  # compare, so the whole decision — compare, ask, stop, write, start — is one
  # critical section against `ccrc codex start|stop`, the install spine and
  # another render; taken after "changed", two renders could both see a
  # difference, and the second would stop the tier the first had just started
  # to write the same bytes.
  # IN A SUBSHELL, so the lock's scope is exactly this render: it is released
  # as the render ends, and its fd never outlives the render in the caller's
  # shell. A caller that renders two lanes in one shell would otherwise still
  # hold the first lane's fd under the second, and a tier started there would
  # inherit it for its whole life. The subshell's stdout is the caller's, so
  # `_models_refuse` still ends the render with its one JSON object.
  # `_codex_lock` is the one library call made OUTSIDE a `( … )` — a lock
  # taken in a subshell is released as that subshell exits — so this relies
  # on its contract of RETURNING, which the install spine needs as well.
  # The directory comes first because the lock's file lives in it. The op's
  # own `mkdir -p` carries no mode, and `runtime.env` lives here too: create
  # it 0700 when absent (a later mkdir cannot tighten it — carry-forward 9).
  # A failure here surfaces as the lock's refusal, or as the op's own
  # `config-unwritable`, which names the path.
  _models_litellm_lane() {   # <codex accountId> -> prints exactly one JSON object, as `_models_litellm` does
    local out
    out="$(_models_litellm_path "$1")"
    ( umask 077; mkdir -p "${out%/*}" ) 2>/dev/null || :
    (
      _codex_lock "$1" >/dev/null \
        || _models_refuse lock-failed 1 "lane $1's lock could not be taken: another ccrc command holds it (a start, a stop, an install or another render), or its lock file could not be opened. Re-run once that command has finished — 'ccrc codex status $1' shows the lane. Nothing was written."
      _models_litellm_lane_held "$1"
    )
  }

  # THE BODY of the codex arm, for a caller that ALREADY HOLDS `_codex_lock
  # <id>`: `_models_litellm_lane` above, and `_codex_litellm_ensure` (`ccrc
  # codex start` holds the lock when it asks). It never takes the lock itself —
  # not because a second `_codex_lock` in the holding shell would deadlock (it
  # is RE-ENTRANT there and returns 0 at once, R38), but because taking it
  # here would blur one render's lock scope across two levels and hide that
  # from the fake's call log. The lane directory exists by that precondition:
  # the lock's file is in it.
  # The STOP-THEN-WRITE doctrine below is preserved verbatim — a stop that
  # fails writes NOTHING, so the next run sees the same difference and
  # retries — with all three of "the bytes", "the tier" and "the stop" named
  # per lane:
  #   - the bytes: `_models_litellm_path <id>`, this lane's own file;
  #   - the tier: `_codex_tier_ours <id> litellm`, which answers FIVE ways,
  #     and each has its own arm. 0 (ours, running) and 4 (ours,
  #     starting — a live handle whose args prove this lane before its port
  #     answers) are this lane's own: stop, write, start. 1 is not running:
  #     write. 2 is FOREIGN — something holds this lane's port or unit that is
  #     not provably this lane's tier — and refuses `tier-foreign`. 3 is CANNOT
  #     ASK (a row `_codex_row` refused, with its sentence) and refuses
  #     `tier-unmeasured`, carrying that sentence; so does any code outside the
  #     five (a library that is not there answers 127) — fail closed. Folding
  #     2 or 3 into a neighbour is the defect: into 0 would stop what ccrc
  #     cannot identify, into 1 would write under a process that may hold the
  #     old bytes, and 3 read as 2 would name a listener that may not exist.
  #   - the stop AND the start: ccrc's own `_codex_stop_tier`/
  #     `_codex_start_tier` for exactly this id — never `ccgpt`, which on a
  #     live box is another repository's launcher and, called bare, acts on
  #     ITS first lane. ONLY a 0 or a 4 reaches the stop
  #     (D-3488); a 2 or a 3 is LEFT RUNNING and named in the refusal,
  #     and the stop itself is by exact unit name or verified pid, which is
  #     `_codex_stop_tier`'s own gate.
  # START follows the write because this arm stopped a tier live sessions were
  # using; the external arm leaves that to the next session because it never
  # owned its tier. "Started" is the promise `_svc_run_supervised` keeps — the
  # job was created — not readiness, which is `ccrc codex start`'s question.
  # A write that fails after the stop starts the tier again on the bytes still
  # on disk, so the box is back where it was and the next run retries.
  # Every library call runs in a SUBSHELL with stdout discarded: this verb's
  # contract is one JSON object on stdout on every path, and the library is
  # written for `ccrc codex`'s own stdout — a stray line or an `exit` inside
  # it must not reach this envelope. The tier question keeps its STDERR,
  # captured, because a 3's reason is there.
  _models_litellm_lane_held() {   # <codex accountId> -> prints exactly one JSON object; the caller holds `_codex_lock <id>`
    local file out check crc ours said held=0
    file="$(_models_roster_path)"
    out="$(_models_litellm_path "$1")"
    # PHASE 1 — render and compare; never write.
    check="$(_models_answer litellm --file "$file" --id "$1" \
               --template "$(_models_litellm_template)" --out "$out")"; crc=$?
    [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] || { printf '%s\n' "$check"; return "$crc"; }
    if [ "$(printf '%s' "$check" | jq -r '.changed')" != "true" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$check"
      return 0
    fi
    # THE TIER — asked only now, when the bytes differ, as the external arm asks.
    said="$( _codex_tier_ours "$1" litellm 2>&1 >/dev/null )"; ours=$?
    said="${said##*$'\n'}"
    case "$ours" in
      0|4) held=1
           ( _codex_stop_tier "$1" litellm ) >/dev/null 2>&1 \
             || _models_refuse restart-failed 1 "lane $1's LiteLLM tier is running (or still starting) on the PREVIOUS config and could not be stopped. Run 'ccrc codex stop $1', then re-run this command — until then this lane serves the old model list. Nothing was written." ;;
      1) : ;;
      2) _models_refuse tier-foreign 1 "something holds lane $1's LiteLLM port or unit that ccrc cannot identify as this lane's own tier, so ccrc cannot tell whether it is serving the previous rendering — and ccrc never stops what it cannot identify, so it was left running. Run 'ccrc codex status $1' to see what holds it, then re-run this command. Nothing was written." ;;
      *) _models_refuse tier-unmeasured 1 "ccrc could not ask whether lane $1's LiteLLM tier is running (the lane library answered $ours${said:+: $said}), so whatever holds it was left running and nothing was stopped — ccrc never stops what it cannot identify. Fix what that names, then re-run this command. Nothing was written." ;;
    esac
    # PHASE 2 — the write.
    local body
    body="$(_models_answer litellm --file "$file" --id "$1" \
              --template "$(_models_litellm_template)" --out "$out" --commit true)"; crc=$?
    if [ "$crc" -ne 0 ]; then
      if [ "$held" -eq 1 ]; then
        if ( _codex_start_tier "$1" litellm ) >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "$PROG: started lane $1's LiteLLM tier again on the previous rendering — the new one could not be written." >&2
        else
          local why
          why="$(printf '%s' "$body" | jq -r '.detail // "no reason given"' 2>/dev/null)"
          _models_refuse start-failed 1 "the new model list could not be written ($why), and lane $1's LiteLLM tier — stopped to take it — did not start again on the previous one, so this lane has no LiteLLM tier until it does. Run 'ccrc codex start $1' (every session launched on this lane runs it too)."
        fi
      fi
      printf '%s\n' "$body"
      return "$crc"
    fi
    # START — this arm stopped a tier sessions were using, so it owes them one.
    local restarted=false
    if [ "$held" -eq 1 ]; then
      ( _codex_start_tier "$1" litellm ) >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        || _models_refuse start-failed 1 "the new model list WAS written to $out, but lane $1's LiteLLM tier — stopped to take it — did not start again, so this lane has no LiteLLM tier until it does. Run 'ccrc codex start $1' (every session launched on this lane runs it too)."
      restarted=true
      echo "$PROG: restarted lane $1's LiteLLM tier — it was holding the previous rendering, and it now reads $out." >&2
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$body" | jq -c --argjson r "$restarted" '. + {restarted: $r}')"
    return 0
  }

  ```

  (d) The dispatch. In `_models_litellm`, old:

  ```bash
  _models_litellm() {   # <accountId> -> prints exactly one JSON object: the op's final answer, or a refusal
    local file check crc
  ```

  New:

  ```bash
  _models_litellm() {   # <accountId> -> prints exactly one JSON object: the op's final answer, or a refusal
    # A codex-kind lane takes its own arm (`_models_litellm_lane`, above).
    # Everything below is the EXTERNAL arm, unchanged byte for byte
    # (D-3482): the live lanes are external, and another
    # repository's LiteLLM reads that arm's file. Plan 3 retires it at cutover.
    if _models_litellm_codex "$1"; then _models_litellm_lane "$1"; return $?; fi
  ```

**What this task deliberately does NOT do** (reject any of these as scope creep):
- **The external arm.** It changes no byte of the external arm's behaviour: the box-global path, `CCGPT_CONFIG`, the
  `pgrep -f` pattern, the bare `ccgpt stop`, and the `restart-failed` sentence naming `ccgpt stop`. Plan 3 retires
  that arm at cutover.
- **The op and its renderer.** It does not touch `deploy/models-op.mjs`, `shared/litellm.mjs` or
  `deploy/litellm-config.template.yaml`. The op already takes `--out`, and spec §8 says the fix is all in `ccd/ccrc`.
- **The lane library (Tasks 4 and 5, ruling R5).** It does not edit `_codex_tier_ours`, `_codex_lanes`, `_codex_say`
  (Task 4), `_codex_stop_tier`, `_codex_start_tier` or `_codex_lock` (Task 5), and it defines none of them again. It
  does not repoint their inline spellings of the per-lane path either. Case M measures that the spellings agree. Such
  a repoint would be safe later, because `_models_litellm_path <id>` is unconditional.
- **The stop's own identity gate.** The arm decides WHETHER to stop: only on 0 or 4 (ruling R8). How the stop proves
  identity, by exact unit name or verified pid, is `_codex_stop_tier`'s (Task 5), and this task does not re-check it.
- **The shim tier.** Only LiteLLM reads `litellm.yaml`.
- **Readiness.** It adds no readiness wait after the START. "Started" means the job was created, and readiness is
  `ccrc codex start`'s own bounded wait.
- **The probe.** It does not touch `ccd/ccrc-models-probe` (the `CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR` default, and re-supplying
  `authDir`). Plan 2a's wave table gives that to Plan 3 (m-verbs §5).
- **`_models_summary`, usage text, README, `ccrc-models.service`.** It does not change `_models_summary`, which is not
  the remedy's site (m-spine §8). Nor does it touch the usage text ("restarts the proxy only if it is holding the
  previous rendering" is true of both arms), the README, or `ccrc-models.service`.
- **The reap.** It does not touch the reap list. Ruling R10 puts `litellm.yaml.prev` on Task 4's `_codex_reap_files`,
  and ruling R11 adds `.lock`.
- **Staleness.** `_codex_litellm_ensure` asks only whether the file is present. Keeping it current is refresh's job.
- **Task 5's `ccrc-codex.test.ts`.** L3 unchanged: no edit to that file is owed. Its `litellm-unrendered` row's
  assertions (`remedy` matching `/ccrc models litellm codex-a/`, the `^ccrc codex: litellm-unrendered: ` prefix)
  still match the ensure's sentence, which keeps both substrings; `lifeBox` plants no catalogue, so the ensure's
  render fails the same way the interim check did and refuses with the same code (confirmed against Task 5's own
  text, which states this row is expected to stay green through this commit).

**Hazards a later task must respect:**
1. **A STARTING tier (ruling R7's 4) is this arm's to stop.** This arm stops a 4 and starts it again on the new
   bytes, so a catalogue change that lands during a cold start costs that start's import again (LiteLLM's import
   alone measured 7.8–9.9 s, m-runtime-probe §2.5). It cannot interleave with `ccrc codex start`'s own window,
   because both hold the lane lock (ruling R11). So a 4 this arm sees is a tier nobody is waiting on: its own
   previous START, which has no readiness wait, or `Restart=always` bringing a crashed tier back. The arm refuses
   every code outside 0, 1, 2 and 4 as `tier-unmeasured`, so a code a later task adds fails closed here until it
   gets an arm.
2. **`_models_litellm_path <id>` must stay unconditional.** Never make it read the roster. After an account's row is
   removed, a kind-dispatching helper would answer the box-global path. An identity check built on that answer would
   then match the other repository's live LiteLLM (`--config` on that path) and stop it.
3. **After `start-failed` that follows a successful write, the next refresh reads "unchanged" and never retries the
   START.** The lane stays down until the next `ccrc codex start`, which every session launch runs. Plan 3's
   `_check_codex` should report a stopped litellm tier on a lane that has live sessions.
4. **The hourly `ccrc-models.service` (a oneshot user unit) can now START a tier.** Under a user unit,
   `_svc_have_user_manager` is true, so it reaches the systemd arm: a separate transient unit in `app.slice`. The
   `nohup` arm must never be reachable from inside a systemd unit, because the child would die with the oneshot's
   cgroup.
5. **Two `_codex_lanes` with opposite predicates.** `ccd/ccd` already defines `_codex_lanes`
   (`grep -n '^_codex_lanes()' ccd/ccd`), keyed on `telemetry` through `CCRC_CODEX_BACKEND`. Task 4's `ccd/ccrc`
   function of the same name is keyed on `exec.kind`. Nothing sources both files today, and no test forbids the pair.
   Moving either function into a shared file, or copying one across, would silently switch predicates (H8).
6. **`_models_answer` now prints any string `.remedy` on stderr, including from internal captures.** That covers
   `showbody=`, `lanes=` and `_models_litellm*`'s `check=`/`body=`. Measured today, only the `init` answer and the
   mutation-tail answer carry one. An op that later adds `.remedy` to a `show`, `lanes` or `litellm` answer will print
   it once per internal call.
7. **`litellm.yaml.prev`** now lands in `~/.ccrc/codex/<id>/`. Ruling R10 puts it on Task 4's `_codex_reap_files`
   list. A reap list that later drops it leaves one lane's previous model list for a re-added id.
8. **Case A runs the REAL `_codex_tier_ours` in a box whose `systemctl` is poisoned.** It pins that an idle lane with
   no user manager answers 1. If Task 4's function treats a failing `systemctl` as "unknown → foreign", A reds, and
   every codex render on a manager-less box would refuse `tier-foreign`. That is a defect to fix in the library, not
   in A. A also runs the REAL `_codex_lock` on a fresh lane. If that lock refuses where nothing holds it, A reds
   `lock-failed`, and every codex render would refuse. That, too, is the library's defect.
9. **The lane lock is taken at ONE level (ruling R11).** `_models_litellm_lane` takes it, in a subshell, for exactly
   one render. `_models_litellm_lane_held` never takes it. Its callers are that wrapper and `_codex_litellm_ensure`,
   whose caller, `ccrc codex start` (`_codex_cmd_start`), already holds it. So:
   - a new caller of `_models_litellm_lane` that already holds the lane's lock must not add one anyway: the real
     `_codex_lock` is RE-ENTRANT in the holding shell and would return 0 at once rather than deadlock (R38), but
     the second call would still blur that render's lock scope across two levels and add a spurious `lock` line to
     a fake's call log — report it, never rely on the re-entrant return to excuse it;
   - a new caller of `_models_litellm_lane_held` or `_codex_litellm_ensure` MUST hold it;
   - the install spine's `_inst_codex_tiers` (Task 10) must not call `_models_litellm_lane` while it holds a lane's
     lock, for the same reason.
10. **An hourly `ccrc models refresh` can now wait behind a `ccrc codex start`.** The render takes the lane lock
    before its compare, even when nothing changed, so a refresh that lands during a start's readiness wait waits up
    to `_codex_lock`'s bound. Then it either renders or refuses `lock-failed`, and that lane's row reads `ok: false`
    naming the lock. The next hourly run retries. A doctor check (Plan 3) should not read one such row as a broken
    lane.
11. **This file's `env()` drops exactly two knobs (ruling R23): `CCRC_CODEX_PROBE_S` and `CCRC_CODEX_READY_S`.** A
    bound the lane library gains later must join that list here, and in every other harness whose verb reaches the
    library. Otherwise a runner's value steers this file's real-library cases (A and real-lock). Knobs pins the
    two names it knows, and no case can pin a knob that does not exist yet.
