- [ ] Insert directly above `# ── _inst_enable — ask systemd to read them, then prove one stayed up ─────`:

```bash
# ── _inst_codex_runtime — the Codex lanes' LiteLLM runtime (spec §5.2) ────
# `ccgpt-runtime` owns ~/.ccrc/runtime/codex/ whole — generations, the
# behaviour probe, the stamp, the `current` swap, the pruning (D-3480,
# D-3481, D-3487). This step only asks it, and reports what it
# RE-MEASURES afterwards: the generation named on the transcript is what
# `ccgpt-runtime python` resolves, never a parse of the builder's own prose,
# which is why the builder's stdout is not relayed. Its failure sentence is
# on stderr, uncaptured, verbatim.
#
# IT DEGRADES, IT NEVER DIES — `_inst_graphify_engine` is fatal on the same
# three failures and this step departs from it on purpose (spec §5.2): a
# LiteLLM environment is orders of magnitude heavier than one wheel, and an
# unreachable package index must not turn an update of a box whose Anthropic
# lanes are healthy into a failed one. A failed build leaves the previous
# runtime current, is counted in INST_DEGRADED (`codex-runtime`), and the
# spine runs on to `_inst_installed`, so `cmd_update` reads "spine completed".
#
# THE GATE IS `exec.kind`, READ FROM accounts.json by `_codex_lanes` — never
# accounts.sh's `CCRC_CODEX_BACKEND`, which is keyed on telemetry and names
# today's EXTERNAL lanes (m-spine H8). A box with no codex lane does the cheap
# part only. A roster `_codex_lanes` cannot read (rc 1, its own
# `roster-invalid` sentence on stderr) is NOT a box with no codex lane: this
# step says so, builds nothing, and degrades — "none" printed over a file
# nobody read would be an overloaded empty. A server-role box converges
# nothing per account (D-3111), and `_inst_bins` places no builder there.
#
# IT SAYS THE BUILD IS RUNNING BEFORE IT RUNS: a pip build can take minutes,
# and an install that goes silent that long reads as hung. The requirement it
# names is READ from the placed builder's own `LITELLM_REQUIREMENT='…'` line,
# its one home (D-3487) — single-definition forbids this file to spell it,
# comments included. The line is said even when the builder then finds the
# runtime current: only the build can tell, and the result line says which.
#
# POSITION: after `_inst_bins` (the builder) and immediately before
# `_inst_enable`, whose `ccrc-models.timer` refresh can stop and start a codex
# lane's tiers through the functions that resolve `ccgpt-runtime python`, and
# before `_inst_codex_tiers`, which measures staleness against what this step
# made current (m-spine H4). The cmd_install pin states both reasons.
_inst_codex_runtime() {
  [ "$INST_ROLE" = server ] && return 0
  local rt lanes n req before after gen why prev rc=0
  rt="$(_codex_runtime_cli)"
  if ! lanes="$(_codex_lanes)"; then
    echo "install: codex runtime: NOT BUILT — \$HOME/.ccrc/accounts.json could not be read as a roster (the ccrc codex: roster-invalid line above says why), so this step cannot tell whether any codex lane needs a runtime. This install continues. Fix the roster (ccrc wrappers prints the validator's sentence), then re-run: ccrc install"
    INST_DEGRADED+=(codex-runtime)
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -z "$lanes" ]; then
    echo "install: codex runtime: none — no codex lane in the roster"
    return 0
  fi
  n="$(printf '%s\n' "$lanes" | grep -c .)"
  if [ ! -x "$rt" ]; then
    echo "install: codex runtime: NOT BUILT — $rt is not on this box, so $n codex lane(s) have no runtime to start from; re-run ccrc install from a complete tree"
    INST_DEGRADED+=(codex-runtime)
    return 0
  fi
  before="$("$rt" python 2>/dev/null)" || before=""
  req="$(sed -n "s/^LITELLM_REQUIREMENT='\([^']*\)'\$/\1/p" "$rt" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
  [ -n "$req" ] || req="(the requirement $rt declares could not be read)"
  echo "install: codex runtime: building $req — pip may take minutes"
  "$rt" build >/dev/null || rc=$?
  after="$("$rt" python 2>/dev/null)" || after=""
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$after" ]; then
    # TWO failures, one outcome, two sentences: a build that said no, and a
    # build that said yes while nothing resolves — an overloaded success this
    # step refuses to report as one.
    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
      why="ccgpt-runtime build exited $rc (its reason is the ccgpt-runtime line on stderr)"
    else
      why="ccgpt-runtime build exited 0 but no runtime resolves (ccgpt-runtime python answers nothing)"
    fi
    # What is current NOW, re-measured after the failure — not assumed.
    if [ -n "$after" ]; then
      prev="${after%/bin/python}"; prev="the previous runtime ${prev##*/} stays current"
    else
      prev="there is no runtime at all, so no codex lane can start until a build passes"
    fi
    echo "install: codex runtime: NOT BUILT — $why; $prev. This install continues. Re-run: ccgpt-runtime build"
    INST_DEGRADED+=(codex-runtime)
    return 0
  fi
  gen="${after%/bin/python}"; gen="${gen##*/}"
  if [ "$after" = "$before" ]; then
    echo "install: codex runtime: $gen already current (requirement, probe and litellm version re-measured unchanged) for $n codex lane(s)"
  else
    echo "install: codex runtime: $gen built, probed and current for $n codex lane(s)"
  fi
}

# identity-gated (D-3488), and only `_codex_tier_ours` = 0 is ever
# stopped here. A lazy lane stays lazy (1 is never started). A port or unit
# that answers as something else (2) — on the fleet box a same-named unit of
# another repository is live today (m-livebox §3) — is left alone and said

# tier of this lane's that is still STARTING (4: its handle proves the lane,
# its port does not answer yet) is never restarted: that would kill it
# mid-import and start it again. It is named with its remedy. Stale means
# `<tier>.started` differs from `_codex_started_json`'s answer now: a new
# generation, or new shim code — a running Python keeps its old code after

# ONE LOCK PER LANE, `_codex_lock`, held from the lane's first question to its
# last act and released through `_codex_unlock`, its ONLY release, before the
# next lane's is taken. `ccrc-models.timer`'s refresh and a session's `ccrc
# codex start` stop and start tiers through the same functions and take the
# same lock; a question asked outside it would be a check-then-act race. It is
# taken HERE, once — the tier functions never take it again. `_codex_lock` is
# re-entrant in this shell (a call for the lane CX_LOCK_ID already names
# returns 0 at once, and a subshell inherits that), so a nested call would add
# nothing; a deadlock comes only through a second RAW open of `.lock`, which
# flock counts as a second locker. A lane whose lock cannot be taken is not
# touched at all. A box with no `flock` answers 0 with CX_LOCK_FD empty: that
# is not a refusal, and the lane is handled unserialised, as Task 5's own
# verbs handle it there.
#
# STOP, THEN START — NEVER `systemctl restart`: a transient unit's argv was
# fixed at `systemd-run` time and carries the RESOLVED generation path
# (D-3480), so a restart re-runs the OLD one. And never STOP what this
# step could not START again: with no runtime resolving, a stale tier stays up
# on the old code and is reported, rather than taken down.
#
# "RESTARTED" IS A MEASUREMENT: after the start, the tier must answer as this
# lane (`_codex_tier_ours` = 0; a 4 is still starting, so the wait goes on)
# within `_codex_ready_secs` — the verb's own bound, and the ONE parse of
# CCRC_CODEX_READY_S (default 90), which this step never parses itself — or it
# is a FAILED restart. Every failure is its own line on stderr and one
# `codex-tiers` in INST_DEGRADED — a per-lane capability degrades; it is not
# the guardrail `_inst_enable` is. An unreadable roster (`_codex_lanes` rc 1)
# is a failure too, never "no codex lane".
_inst_codex_tiers() {
  [ "$INST_ROLE" = server ] && return 0
  local lanes id tier ours stale py ready deadline back
  local restarted=0 kept=0 failed=0
  local -a ids=()
  if ! lanes="$(_codex_lanes)"; then
    echo "install: codex tiers: NOT measured — \$HOME/.ccrc/accounts.json could not be read as a roster (the ccrc codex: roster-invalid line above says why), so no codex lane's tiers were checked or restarted; fix the roster, then re-run: ccrc install" >&2
    INST_DEGRADED+=(codex-tiers)
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -z "$lanes" ]; then
    echo "install: codex tiers: none — no codex lane in the roster"
    return 0
  fi
  mapfile -t ids <<<"$lanes"
  _codex_bus_defaults
  py="$("$(_codex_runtime_cli)" python 2>/dev/null)" || py=""
  ready="$(_codex_ready_secs)"
  for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
    [ -n "$id" ] || continue
    # rc 0 is the lock held, or no `flock` on this box (CX_LOCK_FD empty):
    # both go on. Only a non-zero answer is a refusal.
    if ! _codex_lock "$id"; then
      echo "install: codex tiers: $id: NOT measured — its lane lock could not be taken (the line above says why), so neither of its tiers was checked or restarted; re-run ccrc install once it is free (read: ccrc codex status $id)" >&2
      for tier in $CODEX_TIERS; do failed=$((failed + 1)); done
      continue
    fi
    for tier in $CODEX_TIERS; do
      _codex_tier_ours "$id" "$tier"; ours=$?
      case "$ours" in
        0) ;;
        1) continue ;;
        2)
          echo "install: codex tiers: $id $tier: left alone — its port or unit answers as something that is not this lane, and this step never stops what it cannot prove it started (read: ccrc codex status $id)"
          kept=$((kept + 1)); continue ;;
        4)
          echo "install: codex tiers: $id $tier: left alone — it is this lane's own tier and still starting (its port does not answer yet), and this step never restarts a tier mid-start; if it runs code this install replaced, restart it once it answers: ccrc codex stop $id, then ccrc codex start $id"
          kept=$((kept + 1)); continue ;;
        *)
          echo "install: codex tiers: $id $tier: left alone — whether it is this lane's could not be measured, and this step never stops what it cannot prove it started (read: ccrc codex status $id)"
          kept=$((kept + 1)); continue ;;
      esac
      _codex_tier_stale "$id" "$tier"; stale=$?
      case "$stale" in
        0) ;;
        1) kept=$((kept + 1)); continue ;;
        *)
          # 2 is "cannot tell" — no runtime to start on, or a code file that
          # cannot be read — and so is any answer that is not a clean 0 or 1:
          # a tier nobody can prove stale is never restarted.
          echo "install: codex tiers: $id $tier: left alone — whether it runs code this install replaced could not be measured (no runtime resolves, or its code file cannot be read), and a tier nobody can prove stale is never restarted"
          kept=$((kept + 1)); continue ;;
      esac
      # `_codex_tier_stale` already answers 2 when no runtime resolves. This
      # guard is the step's own, against a runtime that vanished between the
      # two questions: a tier it could not start again is never stopped.
      if [ -z "$py" ]; then
        echo "install: codex tiers: $id $tier: NOT restarted — it runs code this install replaced, but no codex runtime resolves (ccgpt-runtime python answers nothing), and a tier this step could not start again is never stopped; it stays up on the old code until: ccgpt-runtime build, then ccrc codex stop $id and ccrc codex start $id" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1)); continue
      fi
      # The stop's one-word answer is the verb's, not this transcript's.
      if ! _codex_stop_tier "$id" "$tier" >/dev/null; then
        echo "install: codex tiers: $id $tier: restart FAILED — it could not be stopped, so it is still running the code this install replaced (read: ccrc codex status $id)" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1)); continue
      fi
      # stdin from /dev/null: `install.sh` is run as `curl … | bash`, and a
      # tier must never inherit the installer's own text as its stdin.
      if ! _codex_start_tier "$id" "$tier" </dev/null >/dev/null; then
        echo "install: codex tiers: $id $tier: restart FAILED — it was stopped and would not start again, so this tier is DOWN; bring it back with: ccrc codex start $id" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1)); continue
      fi
      back=1; deadline=$((SECONDS + ready))
      while :; do
        if _codex_tier_ours "$id" "$tier"; then back=0; break; fi
        [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" ] || break
        sleep 1
      done
      if [ "$back" -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "install: codex tiers: $id $tier: restart FAILED — it was started again and did not answer as this lane within ${ready}s, so this tier is DOWN; read: ccrc codex status $id, then: ccrc codex start $id" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1)); continue
      fi
      echo "install: codex tiers: $id $tier: restarted — it was running code this install replaced"
      restarted=$((restarted + 1))
    done
    # The release is `_codex_unlock`, the lock's ONLY release — never an
    # inline close, which would leave CX_LOCK_ID naming a lock that is gone —
    # so no later spawn, the next lane's tiers included, inherits it.
    _codex_unlock
  done
  [ "$failed" -eq 0 ] || INST_DEGRADED+=(codex-tiers)
  echo "install: codex tiers: ${#ids[@]} codex lane(s) — $restarted restarted, $kept left as they were, $failed not restarted"
}

feat(gpt-lane): install and update build the Codex runtime and restart stale tiers

Two bare spine steps join cmd_install's pinned sequence (D-3485):
_inst_codex_runtime immediately before _inst_enable, and _inst_codex_tiers
immediately after it. The runtime is built before anything _inst_enable arms
could start a tier. Stale tiers are restarted only after the build, and only
when they are running, verified as this lane's, and stale (D-3488).
A foreign tier, an unmeasurable one and one of this lane's that is still
starting are left running and named. Each lane is handled under its own
lane lock, which is released through _codex_unlock before the next lane's
is taken. The runtime step says the build is running before it starts it. The restart is
a stop followed by a start, and the tier is re-measured before the step
reports it. Both steps degrade (codex-runtime, codex-tiers) and never die,
and an unreadable roster is its own line, never "no codex lane". Update gets
both, because it re-runs the staged spine.

The ccrc install/update harnesses reached the real systemd-run. They now
front it with a recorder, adopt Task 4's plantSystemd as the delegate, and
answer the codex-tier systemctl verbs, all in this commit.

- No `_inst_enable`, `_upd_sweep`, `cmd_update` or `_upd_report` edit. Update picks the steps up through the staged spine.
- No doctor check for the runtime or the tiers. Spec §5.2 says "doctor FAILs the lane", and no task in this plan's file table owns that; carry it forward to Plan 3.
- No fix for the `_inst_enable` timer degrades that never reach `INST_DEGRADED` (m-spine H6, measured on bare `aed80210`). This task changes their number by 0: it adds none and fixes none. The stale file-scope sentence "with ONE exception by design, `_inst_linger`" is also left untouched.
- No placement of `ccgpt-runtime` or `ccrc-codex`, no `TREE_FILES` edit, and no bin-list `toEqual` edit. All of that is Task 9.
- No change to `plantSystemd`, `plantFakeRuntime`, `spawnListener`, `freePorts` or any other Task 4 export. The appended block only adds, and it builds on them rather than defining a second copy (ruling R5).
- No second copy of a Task 5 fixture export. `plantLaneConfig`, `fakeLitellmSource`, `portAccepts`, `laneAnswer`, `eventually`, `alive`, `psArgs` and `killIfOurs` are imported and never re-declared (rulings R20, R29, R30), and there is no `FIXTURE_LITELLM_LISTENER`.
- No hand-planted generation (ruling R28). Every runtime these suites run is BUILT by the real `ccgpt-runtime`. The one exception is the `python3` stub's venv template (`plantRuntimeTemplate`, `VACUOUS_RUNTIME_PYTHON`), which models the BUILD, not a built runtime. A case that needs a runtime without a build plants it with Task 4's `plantFakeRuntime`.
- No lock of its own. The lane lock is Task 5's `_codex_lock`, taken here once per lane (ruling R11) and never re-implemented. Its release is Task 5's `_codex_unlock`, never an inline close (ruling R19).
- No parse of `CCRC_CODEX_READY_S`. The bound is Task 5's `_codex_ready_secs` (ruling R27).
- No identity gate inside the library. `_codex_stop_tier`'s own gate is Task 5's (`D-3488`), and this step keeps its own because it must name what it leaves running.
- No containment change to `ccrc-install-graphify.test.ts`'s or `ccrc-cli.test.ts`'s harness. Neither writes a codex row today (`grep -n "kind: 'codex'"` finds none in either), so neither can reach `systemd-run`.
- No codex-lane end-to-end update test. The update case proves the staged spine runs both steps in order, and the install cases prove what the steps do.

**Hazards later tasks must respect:**
1. **Two fakes of the user manager now exist.** Task 4's `plantSystemd` is one. This task's fronts (`adoptPlantedSystemd`, `spineSystemctlArms`, `spineSystemdRun`, accepted by ruling R13) are the other. The fronts own no state: the delegate they forward to reads and writes Task 4's one layout (`<home>/fake-systemd/…`). The fronts add only their own recorders (`manager-calls`, `spine-systemd-run-calls`), because a delegated call already writes `systemd-run-calls` once. `plantSystemd` must keep planting through `harnessBin(home)` = `<home>/.local/bin`, or every spine tier case reds on the delegate assertion. Folding the two fakes into one is a follow-up. The isolation wall (`isolationManagerStubs`, in `<home>/isolation-bin`) is not a third fake: it answers nothing, forwards nothing and only refuses, and only the extraction harnesses (`runStepHarness`, Task 11's `runUninstCodex`) put it on PATH. A later extraction harness that runs a step reaching the manager through a STUBBED seam needs no change; one that runs a real `_svc_*` function must plant the spine fronts instead, because the wall makes it throw.
2. **The install harness's `python3` stub still refuses every argv except `-m venv <path>`.** If Task 3's builder hashes or does anything else with `python3 -c`, that commit must teach the stub the argv, with a new arm that execs the real interpreter. The measured symptom is `fixture python3: unexpected argv` and `build failed at <stage>`.
3. **The template runtime python recognises the probe by the literal `behaviour_probe` in the program text.** A stamp writer whose program text carries that literal would be answered as the probe.
4. **One lock per lane, taken at ONE level (ruling R11), released only through `_codex_unlock` (ruling R19).** `_inst_codex_tiers` holds `_codex_lock <id>` across a lane's questions and acts, and it calls `_codex_stop_tier` and `_codex_start_tier` under it.
   - `_codex_lock`'s rc 0 with `CX_LOCK_FD` empty is a box with no `flock`, where the step runs the lane unserialised. A later reader of `CX_LOCK_FD` must not take that empty value for a refusal.
   - Neither tier function takes the lock again, and the reason is Task 5's contract (ruling R38). `_codex_lock` is re-entrant in the holding shell: it returns 0 at once when `CX_LOCK_ID` already names the lane, and a subshell inherits that, so a nested `_codex_lock` would cost nothing and add nothing. A deadlock happens only through a second RAW open of `.lock` that bypasses `_codex_lock` (flock treats two opens of one path in one process as two lockers), and no tier function may make one.
   - A `ccrc codex start` or a `ccrc models refresh` that holds the lane's lock delays this step for that lane, for as long as the holder's own bound allows. A lock that is refused degrades `codex-tiers`.
   - If Task 5's `_codex_lock` refuses a lane whose directory does not exist yet, every never-started lane degrades the install. The real lazy case pins that it does not.
5. **A crash-looping own unit reads as 4, "ours, starting" (ruling R7).** Its MainPID proves the lane while its port never answers. This step never restarts a 4, so such a tier is left alone and named as "still starting", not as "down". That is bounded by `StartLimitBurst=20`/`StartLimitIntervalSec=300`, Task 2's `_svc_run_supervised` values (read them there, not here). A doctor check (Plan 3) must not read a single sample of 4 as healthy either.
6. **Absent `jq` now reads as `roster-invalid`** (Task 4 hazard 9). Both steps then degrade with the unreadable-roster line, whose remedy ("fix the roster") is the wrong one for a missing tool. `cmd_install` probes only `node` by name.
7. **An update on a box with a codex lane can now take minutes.** It includes a pip build, and m-runtime-probe HR10 measured about 650 MB per generation and about 2 GB at the swap peak (one box's measurement, an example; the requirement Task 3 pins decides the real size). The `building … — pip may take minutes` line (ruling R33) is said first, so a transcript read mid-build names what is running. Each restarted tier can add up to `CCRC_CODEX_READY_S` (90 s) of wait, and each lane can add the wait for its lock. `ccrc rollout`'s timeouts, if any, must allow for all three.
8. **The spine's messages name the lane, never a unit or a log path.** Unit names live in `lane.json` and are never re-derived. Keep it that way in any new message.
9. **`_inst_codex_runtime` reads the placed builder's `LITELLM_REQUIREMENT='…'` line** for its building line (ruling R33), with a BRE `sed` that expects the whole assignment at column 0 in single quotes. If Task 3's builder changes that line's shape, the line says the requirement could not be read, and the real `…a passing runtime: built…` case reds. Task 3's own comment says every reader outside the builder reads the STAMP; the building line is the one reader of the declaration, because before a build the stamp names the previous requirement.

### Task 11: uninstall stops the Codex lanes and removes the runtime

> Resolved by the round-2 rulings (Task 11):
> - R16: `_codex_reap_lane` does not exist. Account removal is `_acct_remove`'s two codex arms, and those are Task 8's.
> - R19: each lane's lock is released only through Task 5's `_codex_unlock`, and Task 10's `lockStub` models both functions, the no-`flock` answer included.
> - R20: `codexUninstallBox` plants every lane's rendered config through Task 5's `plantLaneConfig`, so a case's `ccrc codex start` finds one.
> - R23: `verbEnv` deletes `CCRC_CODEX_PROBE_S` and `CCRC_CODEX_READY_S`.
> - R28: the three runtimes this task used to plant by hand go through Task 4's `plantFakeRuntime`.
> - R30: `laneAnswer`, `portAccepts` and `eventually` are Task 5's exports, with Task 5's shapes (`{status, type, body} | null`, and a wait that throws).
>
> Resolved by the round-4 rulings (Task 11): R40, R41 and R44 as Task 10's header states them; and R46: this task's uninstall half is `D-3490` (Why).

**Files:**
- Modify: `ccd/ccrc`
  - `cmd_uninstall`'s step list (`grep -n '^cmd_uninstall() {' ccd/ccrc`, then `grep -n '^  _uninst_units$' ccd/ccrc`).
  - New function `_uninst_codex`, placed directly above `_uninst_hooks`' header block (`grep -n "^# THE TREE'S OWN installer, in \`--remove\` mode" ccd/ccrc`).
- Modify: `server/test/ccrc-uninstall.test.ts`
  - `verbEnv` (`grep -n "^function verbEnv" server/test/ccrc-uninstall.test.ts`): the transient-unit launcher, the systemctl arms that accept `stop`, and the delete list.
  - Three new describes, appended at the end of the file.
- Modify, CONDITIONAL (ruling R35): `README.md` and `server/test/session-hook.test.ts`, only when Step 4's compaction-card census reds, repaired per S6-R11 in this task's own commit.
- Test: `server/test/ccrc-uninstall.test.ts`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - Task 4 (ruling R5, one definition each):
    - `_codex_lanes`: rc 0 + ids (EMPTY = none), or rc 1 + its own `roster-invalid` sentence. The rc 1 is its own closing line here, never "no codex lane".
    - `_codex_tier_ours`: **0** ours, running · **1** not running · **2** foreign · **3** cannot ask · **4** ours, starting (ruling R7).
    - `_codex_bus_defaults` and `CODEX_TIERS`.
  - Task 5:
    - `_codex_stop_tier`, identity-gated itself under ruling R8 (`D-3488`).
    - `_codex_lock <id>` and `_codex_unlock` (rulings R11 and R19), under Task 5's contract, which Task 10's Interfaces restates:
      - rc 0 with the lock held, `CX_LOCK_FD` and `CX_LOCK_ID` set;
      - rc 0 with `CX_LOCK_FD` EMPTY on a box with no `flock`, where the lane is handled unserialised, and that answer is not a refusal;
      - non-zero with `CX_LOCK_FD` empty and its reason on stderr;
      - `_codex_unlock` is the ONLY release. It closes `CX_LOCK_FD` when set, clears both variables, and answers 0. This step calls it once per locked lane and never closes the descriptor inline.
    - `ccrc codex start`.
    - `codexLaneFixture.ts` exports (rulings R20, R30): `plantLaneConfig(home, id)`, `portAccepts(port)`, `laneAnswer(port)` (`{status, type, body} | null`) and `eventually(pred, what, ms)` (it THROWS on timeout and never resolves false).
  - Task 4's fixture module and its one layout: `codexRoster`, `plantCodexBins`, `plantFakeRuntime`, `plantSystemd`, `spawnListener` and `killLaneProcesses`.
    - `plantFakeRuntime(home, opts?)` takes `version`, `python`, `stamp: false` and `generationName` (ruling R28). It is the test tree's ONE writer of the `gen-…`/`current`/stamp layout, and this task plants every runtime through it, with its defaults.
  - Task 10's fixture exports: `adoptPlantedSystemd`, `spineSystemctlArms`, `spineSystemdRun` (ruling R13), `SPINE_CONTAINMENT_PROBE`, `managerCalls`, `spineRunCalls`, `isolationManagerStubs` and `strayManagerCalls` (the extraction harness's wall), `ccrcFunction`, `ccrcLine`, `recordingStub`, `lockStub` (`_codex_lock` and `_codex_unlock` both), `StubRc`, `freeLanes`, `authDirOf`, `plantLaneAuth`, `laneUnits`.
  - Task 3: `ccd/ccgpt-runtime python`, consumed only INDIRECTLY. `_uninst_codex` never calls it. The real-lane cases' `ccrc codex start` resolves it through Task 5's tier functions, over the real builder `plantCodexBins` places and the generation `plantFakeRuntime` plants.
- Produces:
  - `_uninst_codex`, run in `cmd_uninstall` right after `_uninst_units`.
  - Its lines, all quoted exactly below:
    - per tier on stdout, `uninstall: codex: <id> <tier>: left alone — …`, with one sentence for a foreign tier (2) and another for an unmeasurable one (3);
    - per tier on stderr, `… could not be stopped …`;
    - per lane on stderr, `uninstall: codex: <id>: not stopped — its lane lock could not be taken …`;
    - one closing `uninstall: codex: …` line, which has a third form for an unreadable roster.

**Why:**
- **Why this plan, and not Plan 3 (`D-3490`, ruling R46).** Plan 2a's wave table gave "uninstall behaviour" to Plan 3 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-gpt-lane-ownership-2a-request-path.md`, its Plan 3 row). This task pulls the uninstall half forward: it stops the tiers and removes `~/.ccrc/runtime/codex/`. Task 10 installs that runtime and restarts tiers from it, and the release that can place them must be able to remove them. What stays Plan 3's is the usage-unit instance sweep and everything after the cutover (see What Task 11 deliberately does NOT do). This departs from Plan 2a, so it carries the slug, not only this paragraph.
- **What spec §13 removes and keeps.**
  - Removed: "the isolated runtime under `~/.ccrc/runtime/codex/`, and any transient tier still running".
  - Kept, "deliberately and stated so nobody has to infer it": "OAuth directories … `~/.ccrc/logs/codex/*`, and `~/.ccrc/codex/<id>/` itself".
- **This is the first plain-uninstall venv removal.** Graphify's venv survives until `--purge` (m-spine §4, H11: "No precedent exists"). Spec §13 departs from that on purpose, because the runtime is regenerable and heavy (m-runtime-probe HR10: about 650 MB per generation).
- **`--purge` is unchanged.** `_uninst_purge` takes `~/.ccrc` whole except `memory`, which already includes `~/.ccrc/codex/<id>/` and the runtime. `authDir` is never under `~/.ccrc` (the roster refuses that, spec §4.1), so a purge cannot reach a credential.
- **Why right after `_uninst_units`.** `_uninst_units`' `disable --now` loop names `ccrc-models.timer ccrc-models.service` (measured, `grep -n 'ccrc-models.timer ccrc-models.service; do' ccd/ccrc`). With that timer disabled first, its refresh can no longer stop and start a lane's tiers (D-3482) between this step's stop and the runtime removal.
- **Why before `_uninst_tree_bins`.** That step removes the lane executables (Task 9's census), so the tier functions still find everything they could need.
- **Why the per-tier identity gate (ruling R8, `D-3488`).** Same-named transient units of another repository are live on the fleet box right now (the 2026-09-23 live-box census). `_uninst_units`' own rule is "An uninstall removes only what ccrc placed" (D-3172). So this step stops a tier only when `_codex_tier_ours` answers 0 or 4, and leaves a 2 or a 3 running, each named in its own sentence. This departs from spec §7.4's "stopping is by exact unit, then by verified identity". `_codex_stop_tier` carries the same gate inside the library (Task 5). This step asks first anyway, because it must name what it leaves running.
- **A 4 is stopped (ruling R7).** A tier that is still starting is ccrc's own. Its handle proves this lane while its port does not answer yet. Leaving it would leave ccrc's own process running over a removed runtime.
- **Why the lane lock (ruling R11).** `_uninst_units` has already taken `ccrc-models.timer` down, but a session's `ccrc codex start` can still start a tier between this step's identity check and its stop. So each lane is measured and stopped under Task 5's `_codex_lock <id>`, which is released before the next lane's is taken. A lock that cannot be taken stops nothing in that lane and names it.
  - The release is Task 5's `_codex_unlock`, the lock's ONLY release (ruling R19). An inline close would leave `CX_LOCK_ID` naming a lane whose lock is gone.
  - On a box with no `flock`, `_codex_lock` answers 0 with `CX_LOCK_FD` empty (ruling R19). That is not a refusal: the step measures and stops the lane unserialised there, as Task 5's own verbs do. Reading the empty descriptor as a failed lock would leave every tier of such a box running over a removed runtime.
- **Why an unreadable roster is its own line.** `plantInstalledBox`'s `accounts.json` is `{"fixture":"roster"}`, which is not a roster. Task 4's `_codex_lanes` answers rc 1 there, with `roster-invalid`. Saying "no codex lane in the roster" over a file nobody read would be an overloaded empty. The step says it could not read the roster, stops nothing, and still removes the runtime (§13). Every existing uninstall case on that fixture therefore gains one `roster-invalid` stderr line and this closing line. None of those cases asserts either stream whole. Measured with `grep -n "stderr).toBe(\|stdout).toBe(" server/test/ccrc-uninstall.test.ts` (at `aed80210`, and again at `bbb5e714`, where #174 and #175 left the file untouched; re-run it at Step 0): every hit is `expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0)` or its `r2` twin, which uses stderr as a failure message, except the darwin `logs` case, which runs no uninstall. The file's `stderr).toMatch` cases name refusals that end the verb before any step runs.
- **Why the harness change must land with the step.**
  - `verbEnv`'s `systemctl` stub accepts only `daemon-reload` and `disable --now` (m-platform §3.3). A codex lane's stop would exit 90.
  - Its `systemd-run` resolves to the real one (m-platform §3.2). `_uninst_codex` never starts a unit, but `_svc_have_user_manager` resolves the name, and the containment rule covers every name a spine path can reach.
  - Its delete list gains both codex knobs (ruling R23). `ccrc uninstall` now reaches the lane library, which reads `CCRC_CODEX_PROBE_S` (Task 4's per-probe bound, through `_codex_tier_ours`) and `CCRC_CODEX_READY_S` (Task 5's bound, through `_codex_lock`'s wait). A case that needs a bound passes it explicitly (`READY`).
- **`install-census.test.ts` does not read `_uninst_codex`.** Its STATED SCOPE reads `rm -f` in `_uninst_tree_bins` and the systemd arm of `_uninst_units` only. `rm -rf` is a verb it deliberately does not read, and `~/.ccrc/runtime/codex` is not a census directory. So the census neither needs nor gains an entry.

/** `_uninst_codex` alone: its two lane-library seams stubbed by table, Task 5's
 *  `_codex_lock` and `_codex_unlock` by `lockStub` (ruling R19), Task 4's
 *  `CODEX_TIERS` and the real `PROG`/`_ccrc_die` read out of ccd/ccrc, and a
 *  HOME holding what §13 removes (a runtime from Task 4's `plantFakeRuntime`,
 *  ruling R28) and keeps. */
function runUninstCodex(c: {
  lanes?: string[]; lanesRc?: number; ours?: Record<string, StubRc>; stopRc?: Record<string, StubRc>;
  runtime?: boolean; lockRefuse?: string[]; lockNoFlock?: string[];
}): {
  code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string; calls: string[]; home: string; kept: Record<string, string>;
  /** `CX_LOCK_FD` and `CX_LOCK_ID` after the step returned: empty unless a
   *  lane's lock was never released through `_codex_unlock`. */
  lockAfter: string;
} {
  const home = mkTmp('ccrc-uninst-codex-step-');
  const lanes = c.lanes ?? ['codex-a'];
  const kept: Record<string, string> = {};
  const keep = (rel: string, text: string): void => {
    mkdirSync(join(home, path.dirname(rel)), { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(join(home, rel), text);
    kept[rel] = text;
  };
  for (const id of lanes) {
    for (const f of ['lane.json', 'runtime.env', 'litellm.yaml']) keep(`.ccrc/codex/${id}/${f}`, `fixture ${f} for ${id}\n`);
    keep(`.ccrc/logs/codex/${id}/shim.log`, 'fixture log\n');
    keep(`.local/share/ccrc/codex/${id}/auth.json`, '{"fixture": "test-token-not-a-secret"}\n');
  }
  if (c.runtime !== false) plantFakeRuntime(home);
  const lanesDef = (c.lanesRc ?? 0) === 0
    ? `_codex_lanes() { ${lanes.length === 0 ? ':' : `printf '%s\\n' ${lanes.join(' ')}`}; }`
    : `_codex_lanes() { echo "ccrc codex: roster-invalid: fixture: the roster could not be read" >&2; return ${c.lanesRc}; }`;
  const harness = [
    'set -uo pipefail',
    ccrcLine(/^PROG=.*$/m, 'PROG='),
    ccrcLine(/^_ccrc_die\(\) \{.*\}$/m, '_ccrc_die'),
    ccrcLine(/^CODEX_TIERS=.*$/m, 'CODEX_TIERS='),
    lanesDef,
    '_codex_bus_defaults() { :; }',
    lockStub(c.lockRefuse ?? [], c.lockNoFlock ?? []),
    recordingStub('_codex_tier_ours', c.ours, 1),
    recordingStub('_codex_stop_tier', c.stopRc, 0),
    ccrcFunction('_uninst_codex'),
    '_uninst_codex; rc=$?',
    'printf \'%s\\n\' "${CX_LOCK_FD:-}" "${CX_LOCK_ID:-}" > "$HOME/lock-after"',
    'exit "$rc"',
  ].join('\n');
  // Task 10's isolation wall, FIRST on PATH (the containment rule): the step
  // stops tiers only through the stubbed `_codex_stop_tier`, so a direct
  // `systemctl` or `systemd-run` from its body is a thrown, named red, never
  // the real binary.
  const wall = isolationManagerStubs(home);
  const p = spawnSync(BASH, ['-c', harness],
    { env: { PATH: `${wall}:${process.env['PATH'] ?? ''}`, HOME: home }, encoding: 'utf8' });
  const stray = strayManagerCalls(home);
  if (stray.length > 0) {
    throw new Error(`_uninst_codex reached the user manager directly, not through the stubbed lane library:\n${stray.join('\n')}\n${p.stderr ?? ''}`);
  }
  const lines = (f: string): string[] =>
    (existsSync(join(home, f)) ? readFileSync(join(home, f), 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : []);
  return {
    code: p.status ?? -1, stdout: p.stdout ?? '', stderr: p.stderr ?? '', calls: lines('calls'), home, kept,
    lockAfter: lines('lock-after').join('\n'),
  };
}

describe('ccrc uninstall: the codex step, measured in isolation (_uninst_codex)', () => {
  const RT = '$HOME/.ccrc/runtime/codex';
  const KEPT = 'kept: $HOME/.ccrc/codex/<id>/, $HOME/.ccrc/logs/codex/ and every lane\'s authDir';
  const LOCK_A = '_codex_lock codex-a';
  const LOCK_B = '_codex_lock codex-b';
  // `lockStub`'s record of Task 5's `_codex_unlock`, the lock's ONLY release
  // (ruling R19): an inline close leaves no such line.
  const UNLOCK_A = '_codex_unlock codex-a';
  const UNLOCK_B = '_codex_unlock codex-b';
  const keptIntact = (r: ReturnType<typeof runUninstCodex>): void => {
    for (const [rel, text] of Object.entries(r.kept)) {
      expect(readFileSync(join(r.home, rel), 'utf8'), `${rel} was removed or changed`).toBe(text);
    }
  };

  it('no codex lane: nothing is asked, the runtime is removed, and one line says both', () => {
    const r = runUninstCodex({ lanes: [] });
    expect(r.code).toBe(0);
    expect(r.calls).toEqual([]);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe(`uninstall: codex: no codex lane in the roster — nothing to stop; the runtime at ${RT} removed\n`);
    expect(existsSync(join(r.home, '.ccrc', 'runtime', 'codex'))).toBe(false);
  });

  it('no runtime on the box: the line says it was not installed, never that it was removed', () => {
    const r = runUninstCodex({ lanes: [], runtime: false });
    expect(r.stdout).toBe(`uninstall: codex: no codex lane in the roster — nothing to stop; the runtime at ${RT} was not installed\n`);
  });

  it('a roster that cannot be read: no lane is asked or stopped, it is said in its own line, and the runtime still goes', () => {
    // `ours: 0` is the CONTROL: a step that read rc 1 as a lane list, or
    // guessed one, would ask and stop.
    const r = runUninstCodex({ lanesRc: 1, ours: { 'codex-a litellm': 0, 'codex-a shim': 0 } });
    expect(r.code).toBe(0);
    expect(r.calls).toEqual([]);
    expect(r.stderr).toMatch(/^ccrc codex: roster-invalid: /m);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe(`uninstall: codex: the roster could not be read (the ccrc codex: roster-invalid line above says why), so no codex lane's tier was measured or stopped; the runtime at ${RT} removed; ${KEPT}\n`);
    expect(existsSync(join(r.home, '.ccrc', 'runtime', 'codex'))).toBe(false);
    keptIntact(r);
  });

  it('a running lane of ours: each tier is identity-checked under the lane lock, then stopped; the runtime goes; everything §13 keeps is byte-identical', () => {
    const r = runUninstCodex({ ours: { 'codex-a litellm': 0, 'codex-a shim': 0 } });
    expect(r.calls).toEqual([LOCK_A, '_codex_tier_ours codex-a litellm', '_codex_stop_tier codex-a litellm',
      '_codex_tier_ours codex-a shim', '_codex_stop_tier codex-a shim', UNLOCK_A]);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe(`uninstall: codex: 1 codex lane(s) in the roster — stopped: codex-a litellm, codex-a shim; left alone: none; not stopped: none; the runtime at ${RT} removed; ${KEPT}\n`);
    expect(existsSync(join(r.home, '.ccrc', 'runtime', 'codex'))).toBe(false);
    expect(r.lockAfter).toBe('');
    keptIntact(r);
  });

  it('a tier of ours that is still STARTING (4) is stopped too — it is ccrc\'s own, and would outlive its runtime', () => {
    const r = runUninstCodex({ ours: { 'codex-a litellm': 4 } });
    expect(r.calls).toEqual([LOCK_A, '_codex_tier_ours codex-a litellm', '_codex_stop_tier codex-a litellm',
      '_codex_tier_ours codex-a shim', UNLOCK_A]);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/— stopped: codex-a litellm; left alone: none; not stopped: none; /);
  });

  it('a tier whose port or unit answers as something else is NEVER stopped — an uninstall stops only what ccrc started', () => {
    // `codex-a shim` at rc 1 is the CONTROL for the next mutation row: a
    // step that stopped every non-zero tier would stop it too.
    const r = runUninstCodex({ ours: { 'codex-a litellm': 2 } });
    expect(r.calls).toEqual([LOCK_A, '_codex_tier_ours codex-a litellm', '_codex_tier_ours codex-a shim', UNLOCK_A]);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^uninstall: codex: codex-a litellm: left alone — its port or unit answers as something that is not this lane, and an uninstall stops only what ccrc started$/m);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/— stopped: none; left alone: codex-a litellm; not stopped: none; /);
    keptIntact(r);
  });

  it('an identity answer the step cannot read is left alone too, in its own sentence', () => {
    const r = runUninstCodex({ ours: { 'codex-a shim': 3 } });
    expect(r.calls).toEqual([LOCK_A, '_codex_tier_ours codex-a litellm', '_codex_tier_ours codex-a shim', UNLOCK_A]);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^uninstall: codex: codex-a shim: left alone — whether it is this lane's could not be measured, and an uninstall stops only what it can prove ccrc started$/m);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/left alone: codex-a shim;/);
  });

  it('a stop that fails is its own stderr line and is not counted as stopped; the runtime is still removed', () => {
    const r = runUninstCodex({ ours: { 'codex-a litellm': 0 }, stopRc: { 'codex-a litellm': 1 } });
    expect(r.code).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stderr).toMatch(/^uninstall: codex: codex-a litellm: could not be stopped — it is still running/m);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/— stopped: none; left alone: none; not stopped: codex-a litellm; the runtime at \$HOME\/\.ccrc\/runtime\/codex removed; /);
  });

  it('two lanes: only the running one is stopped, each under its own lock, released through _codex_unlock before the next is taken', () => {
    // `LOCK-STILL-HELD` is the stub's record of a lock entered while the
    // previous one was never released; `lockAfter` is the last lane's
    // `CX_LOCK_FD` and `CX_LOCK_ID`, which an inline close leaves naming a lane.
    const r = runUninstCodex({ lanes: ['codex-a', 'codex-b'], ours: { 'codex-a litellm': 0, 'codex-a shim': 0 } });
    expect(r.calls.filter((l) => l.startsWith('_codex_stop_tier'))).toEqual(['_codex_stop_tier codex-a litellm', '_codex_stop_tier codex-a shim']);
    expect(r.calls.filter((l) => /^(_codex_lock|_codex_unlock|LOCK-STILL-HELD) /.test(l))).toEqual([LOCK_A, UNLOCK_A, LOCK_B, UNLOCK_B]);
    expect(r.calls.indexOf(UNLOCK_A)).toBeGreaterThan(r.calls.indexOf('_codex_stop_tier codex-a shim'));
    expect(r.lockAfter).toBe('');
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^uninstall: codex: 2 codex lane\(s\) in the roster — stopped: codex-a litellm, codex-a shim; /m);
  });

  it('a lane whose lock cannot be taken is not asked or stopped: named as not stopped, and the next lane still runs', () => {
    const r = runUninstCodex({
      lanes: ['codex-a', 'codex-b'], lockRefuse: ['codex-a'],
      ours: { 'codex-a litellm': 0, 'codex-b litellm': 0 },
    });
    expect(r.code).toBe(0);
    expect(r.calls).toEqual([LOCK_A, LOCK_B, '_codex_tier_ours codex-b litellm', '_codex_stop_tier codex-b litellm',
      '_codex_tier_ours codex-b shim', UNLOCK_B]);
    expect(r.stderr).toMatch(/^uninstall: codex: codex-a: not stopped — its lane lock could not be taken/m);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/— stopped: codex-b litellm; left alone: none; not stopped: codex-a litellm, codex-a shim; the runtime at \$HOME\/\.ccrc\/runtime\/codex removed; /);
    expect(r.lockAfter).toBe('');
  });

  it('a box with no flock: the lock answers 0 with nothing held, and the lane is still measured and stopped, unserialised', () => {
    // Task 5's contract (ruling R19): rc 0 with CX_LOCK_FD EMPTY means "no
    // flock on this box", never a refusal. A step that read the empty
    // descriptor as a failed lock would leave every tier of such a box running
    // over a removed runtime. `_codex_unlock -` is the release of nothing.
    const r = runUninstCodex({ lockNoFlock: ['codex-a'], ours: { 'codex-a litellm': 0, 'codex-a shim': 0 } });
    expect(r.calls).toEqual([LOCK_A, '_codex_tier_ours codex-a litellm', '_codex_stop_tier codex-a litellm',
      '_codex_tier_ours codex-a shim', '_codex_stop_tier codex-a shim', '_codex_unlock -']);
    expect(r.stderr).not.toMatch(/its lane lock could not be taken/);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/— stopped: codex-a litellm, codex-a shim; left alone: none; not stopped: none; /);
    expect(r.lockAfter).toBe('');
  });
});

// PLATFORM-ONLY: stopping a tier by its exact unit is the user-manager arm,
// faked by Task 4's `plantSystemd`; on Darwin `_svc_have_user_manager` is
// always false and the nohup arm (Task 5's subject) is the only one.
describeLinux('ccrc uninstall: the codex lanes on a real lane (Plan 2b-2 Task 11)', () => {
  const homes: string[] = [];
  // `killLaneProcesses` ends every child Task 4's fixture tracked for a home
  // (the foreign `spawnListener` included) and, by Task 5's extension, every
  // pid its fake `systemd-run` recorded.
  afterEach(async () => {
    for (const h of homes.splice(0)) await killLaneProcesses(h);
  });

  /** An installed box whose roster carries `ids` as codex lanes, with the
   *  shipped shim and builder on PATH (Task 4's `plantCodexBins`: copies, 0755),
   *  every lane's rendered config (Task 5's `plantLaneConfig`, ruling R20: a
   *  case's `ccrc codex start` refuses `litellm-unrendered` without one), and
   *  Task 4's fake runtime and fake user manager. */
  async function codexUninstallBox(prefix: string, ids: string[]): Promise<{ home: string; lanes: LanePorts[] }> {
    const lanes = await freeLanes(ids);
    const home = mkTmp(prefix);
    homes.push(home);
    plantInstalledBox(home);
    codexRoster(home, lanes);
    for (const l of lanes) plantLaneConfig(home, l.id);
    plantCodexBins(home);
    plantFakeRuntime(home, { version: '1.101.0' });
    plantSystemd(home, { userManager: true });
    return { home, lanes };
  }
  const initLane = (home: string, id: string): void => {
    const init = runVerb(home, 'models', [id, 'init', 'codex']);
    if (init.code !== 0) throw new Error(`ccrc models ${id} init codex:\n${init.stderr}`);
  };
  const stops = (home: string): string[] => managerCalls(home).filter((l) => /^systemctl --user stop\b/.test(l));

  it('a running lane is stopped by its exact units, the runtime goes, and the lane state, logs and credential stay', async () => {
    const { home, lanes: [lane] } = await codexUninstallBox('ccrc-uninst-codex-running-', ['codex-a']);
    initLane(home, 'codex-a');
    plantLaneAuth(home, 'codex-a');
    const s = runVerb(home, 'codex', ['start', 'codex-a'], READY);
    expect(s.code, `ccrc codex start codex-a:\n${s.stdout}\n${s.stderr}`).toBe(0);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, '.local', 'bin', '.codex-systemctl')),
      'plantSystemd did not plant into ~/.local/bin, so this harness cannot adopt it (Task 10 Interfaces)').toBe(true);
    const units = laneUnits(home, 'codex-a');
    const ans = await laneAnswer(lane!.proxyPort);   // Task 5's {status, type, body} (ruling R30)
    expect(ans?.type).toMatch(/^application\/json/);
    expect(JSON.parse(ans!.body)).toEqual({ lane: 'codex-a' });
    const r = runVerb(home, 'uninstall', ['--force']);
    expect(r.code, `stderr: ${r.stderr}\nstdout: ${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    for (const u of [units.litellm, units.shim]) {
      expect(stops(home).some((l) => l.includes(u)), `${u} was not stopped by name:\n${managerCalls(home).join('\n')}`).toBe(true);
    }
    // Task 5's `eventually` THROWS on timeout and never resolves false (ruling R30).
    await eventually(async () => !(await portAccepts(lane!.proxyPort)), 'the shim to stop listening', 5000);
    await eventually(async () => !(await portAccepts(lane!.litellmPort)), 'litellm to stop listening', 5000);
    expect(existsSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'runtime', 'codex'))).toBe(false);
    for (const f of ['lane.json', 'runtime.env', 'litellm.yaml']) {
      expect(existsSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'codex', 'codex-a', f)), `${f} was removed`).toBe(true);
    }
    expect(existsSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'logs', 'codex', 'codex-a'))).toBe(true);
    expect(existsSync(join(authDirOf(home, 'codex-a'), 'auth.json')), 'the credential was removed').toBe(true);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^uninstall: codex: 1 codex lane\(s\) in the roster — stopped: codex-a litellm, codex-a shim; left alone: none; not stopped: none; the runtime at \$HOME\/\.ccrc\/runtime\/codex removed; kept: /m);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^uninstall: done — /m);
  }, 120_000);

  it('a foreign listener on the lane port survives the uninstall', async () => {
    // The OTHER repository's shim shape (`text/plain`, the bare id — m-tiers
    // §1) on this lane's shim port: Task 4's `spawnListener`, bound when it
    // resolves. The lane was never materialised (no lane.json). Its directory
    // exists only because `codexUninstallBox` planted its config, so the lock's
    // missing-directory behaviour is Task 10's lazy case's to pin, not this one's.
    const { home, lanes: [lane] } = await codexUninstallBox('ccrc-uninst-codex-foreign-', ['codex-a']);
    const foreign = await spawnListener(home, { answer: 'text', lane: 'codex-a', port: lane!.proxyPort });
    const r = runVerb(home, 'uninstall', ['--force']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^uninstall: codex: codex-a shim: left alone — its port or unit answers as something that is not this lane/m);
    expect(stops(home)).toEqual([]);
    expect(() => process.kill(foreign.pid, 0)).not.toThrow();
    expect(await portAccepts(lane!.proxyPort)).toBe(true);
  }, 120_000);

  it('a same-named ACTIVE unit that is not this lane is never stopped', async () => {
    // The fleet box's shape (m-livebox §3): a transient unit with the lane's
    // own unit name, active, holding the litellm port — owned by another
    // repository. Identity, not the name, decides.
    const { home, lanes: [lane] } = await codexUninstallBox('ccrc-uninst-codex-namesake-', ['codex-a']);
    initLane(home, 'codex-a');   // lane.json, so the unit name is read, not re-derived
    const units = laneUnits(home, 'codex-a');
    const env = verbEnv(home);
    const root = join(home, 'foreign-unit-root');
    mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
    const log = join(home, 'foreign-unit.log');
    const sd = spawnSync(join(home, '.local', 'bin', 'systemd-run'), ['--user', '--collect', '--quiet',
      `--unit=${units.litellm}`, '-p', `StandardOutput=append:${log}`, '-p', `StandardError=append:${log}`,
      '--', realPy(), '-m', 'http.server', String(lane!.litellmPort), '--bind', '127.0.0.1', '--directory', root],
    { env, encoding: 'utf8' });
    expect(sd.status, `the fake user manager would not start the namesake unit:\n${sd.stderr}`).toBe(0);
    await eventually(() => portAccepts(lane!.litellmPort), 'the namesake to bind', 5000);
    const active = spawnSync(join(home, '.local', 'bin', 'systemctl'), ['--user', 'is-active', units.litellm], { env, encoding: 'utf8' });
    expect(active.stdout.trim(), 'the fixture does not model a same-named ACTIVE unit, so this case would measure nothing').toBe('active');
    rmSync(join(home, 'manager-calls'), { force: true });
    const r = runVerb(home, 'uninstall', ['--force']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(/^uninstall: codex: codex-a litellm: left alone — /m);
    expect(stops(home).filter((l) => l.includes(units.litellm))).toEqual([]);
    expect(await portAccepts(lane!.litellmPort)).toBe(true);
  }, 120_000);
});
```

- [ ] Insert directly above `# THE TREE'S OWN installer, in \`--remove\` mode — never the INSTALLED copy at`:

```bash
# ── _uninst_codex — stop the Codex lanes' tiers, remove their runtime ─────
# Spec §13. REMOVED: the isolated runtime (~/.ccrc/runtime/codex, every
# generation and `current`) and every tier of a rostered codex lane that is
# RUNNING OR STARTING AND VERIFIED THIS LANE'S, stopped through the lane
# library — by exact unit where a user manager exists, by verified pid where
# not. KEPT, stated so nobody has to infer it: ~/.ccrc/codex/<id>/ (diagnosis
# material, and every byte of it regenerable), ~/.ccrc/logs/codex/, and every
# lane's authDir — ccrc never obtained that credential, and removing it would
# end a subscription session it did not start. `--purge` takes ~/.ccrc whole
# as before; authDir is never under ~/.ccrc (the roster refuses it), so a
# purge cannot reach a credential either.
#
# A PLAIN UNINSTALL REMOVES A VENV, which no step did before: graphify's venv
# survives until `--purge`. That departure is spec §13's own — the runtime is
# hundreds of MB per generation and rebuilt by the next install.
#
# IDENTITY, NOT THE NAME, DECIDES WHAT STOPS (D-3488). Only a tier
# `_codex_tier_ours` answers 0 (ours, running) or 4 (ours, still starting —
# ccrc's own, which would otherwise outlive its runtime) is stopped. A tier it
# calls foreign (2), or cannot ask about (3, or anything else), is LEFT
# RUNNING and named, each in its own sentence: on the fleet box a transient
# unit with a lane's exact tier name is live today and belongs to another
# repository (m-livebox §3), and an uninstall removes only what ccrc placed
# (`_uninst_units`' own rule, D-3172). A tier that is not running (1) has
# nothing to stop. A stop that fails is its own stderr line; the runtime is
# removed regardless, as §13 says.
#
# ONE LOCK PER LANE, `_codex_lock`, held from the lane's first identity
# question to its last stop and released through `_codex_unlock`, its ONLY
# release, before the next lane's is taken: a session's `ccrc codex start`
# takes the same lock, and a check made outside it would be a check-then-act
# race. A lane whose lock cannot be taken is not asked or stopped, and is
# named. A box with no `flock` answers 0 with CX_LOCK_FD empty: that is not a
# refusal, and the lane is measured and stopped unserialised, as Task 5's own
# verbs handle it there. A roster `_codex_lanes` cannot read (rc 1,
# its `roster-invalid` sentence on stderr) is NOT a roster with no codex lane:
# nothing is stopped, and the closing line says the roster could not be read.
#
# POSITION: right after `_uninst_units`, whose `disable --now` takes
# `ccrc-models.timer` down first — its refresh stops and starts a codex lane's
# tiers — and before `_uninst_tree_bins` removes the lane's executables.
_uninst_codex() {
  local lanes id tier rc rt="$HOME/.ccrc/runtime/codex" rt_word roster=read
  local stopped="" left="" nostop=""
  local -a ids=()
  if lanes="$(_codex_lanes)"; then
    [ -z "$lanes" ] || mapfile -t ids <<<"$lanes"
  else
    roster=unreadable
  fi
  _codex_bus_defaults
  for id in ${ids[@]+"${ids[@]}"}; do
    [ -n "$id" ] || continue
    # rc 0 is the lock held, or no `flock` on this box (CX_LOCK_FD empty):
    # both go on. Only a non-zero answer is a refusal.
    if ! _codex_lock "$id"; then
      for tier in $CODEX_TIERS; do nostop="$nostop${nostop:+, }$id $tier"; done
      echo "uninstall: codex: $id: not stopped — its lane lock could not be taken (the line above says why), so neither of its tiers was measured; stop them by hand before any reinstall" >&2
      continue
    fi
    for tier in $CODEX_TIERS; do
      _codex_tier_ours "$id" "$tier"; rc=$?
      case "$rc" in
        0|4)
          # The stop's one-word answer is the verb's, not this transcript's.
          if _codex_stop_tier "$id" "$tier" >/dev/null; then
            stopped="$stopped${stopped:+, }$id $tier"
          else
            nostop="$nostop${nostop:+, }$id $tier"
            echo "uninstall: codex: $id $tier: could not be stopped — it is still running; stop it by hand before any reinstall" >&2
          fi ;;
        1) ;;
        2)
          left="$left${left:+, }$id $tier"
          echo "uninstall: codex: $id $tier: left alone — its port or unit answers as something that is not this lane, and an uninstall stops only what ccrc started" ;;
        *)
          left="$left${left:+, }$id $tier"
          echo "uninstall: codex: $id $tier: left alone — whether it is this lane's could not be measured, and an uninstall stops only what it can prove ccrc started" ;;
      esac
    done
    # The release is `_codex_unlock`, the lock's ONLY release — never an
    # inline close, which would leave CX_LOCK_ID naming a lock that is gone —
    # so nothing started after this, the next lane's lock included, inherits it.
    _codex_unlock
  done
  rt_word="was not installed"
  if [ -e "$rt" ] || [ -L "$rt" ]; then
    rm -rf -- "$rt" || _ccrc_die "removing $rt failed — the codex runtime is still on this box"
    rt_word="removed"
  fi
  if [ "$roster" = unreadable ]; then
    echo "uninstall: codex: the roster could not be read (the ccrc codex: roster-invalid line above says why), so no codex lane's tier was measured or stopped; the runtime at \$HOME/.ccrc/runtime/codex $rt_word; kept: \$HOME/.ccrc/codex/<id>/, \$HOME/.ccrc/logs/codex/ and every lane's authDir"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${#ids[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "uninstall: codex: no codex lane in the roster — nothing to stop; the runtime at \$HOME/.ccrc/runtime/codex $rt_word"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "uninstall: codex: ${#ids[@]} codex lane(s) in the roster — stopped: ${stopped:-none}; left alone: ${left:-none}; not stopped: ${nostop:-none}; the runtime at \$HOME/.ccrc/runtime/codex $rt_word; kept: \$HOME/.ccrc/codex/<id>/, \$HOME/.ccrc/logs/codex/ and every lane's authDir"
}

```

feat(gpt-lane): uninstall stops the Codex lanes and removes their runtime

Plan 2a gave uninstall behaviour to Plan 3. This plan pulls the uninstall
half forward (D-3490), because the release that installs the
runtime must be able to remove it.

_uninst_codex runs right after _uninst_units. Under each lane's lock,
released through _codex_unlock before the next lane's is taken, it stops
each tier of a rostered codex lane that is running or still starting and
verified as this lane's (D-3488). A tier whose port or unit
answers as something else, or whose identity cannot be measured, is left
running and named. An unreadable roster is its own line, never "no codex
lane". It then removes ~/.ccrc/runtime/codex and keeps the lane state, the
logs and the credential (spec §13). The uninstall harness answers the
codex-tier systemctl verbs and contains systemd-run, in this commit.

**What Task 11 deliberately does NOT do:**
- No `_uninst_purge` change. `--purge` already takes `~/.ccrc` whole except `memory`.
- No `_uninst_tree_bins` census, prose or echo edit, and no `_uninst_wrappers` `case` edit. Both are Task 9's.
- No account-removal work. There is no `_codex_reap_lane` (ruling R16): account removal is `_acct_remove`'s two codex arms, which are Task 8's (`_codex_lock` → `_codex_stop_lane` → `_codex_unlock` before the roster drop, then `_codex_reap_files`).
- No change to `_codex_stop_lane`, `_codex_stop_tier`, `_codex_lock` or `_codex_unlock` (Task 5). Under `D-3488` the library gates its own stops. This step asks first anyway, because it must name what it leaves running. It defines no lock of its own (ruling R11) and releases through `_codex_unlock` only (ruling R19).
- No hand-planted runtime (ruling R28). Every generation these cases need is `plantFakeRuntime`'s.
- No sweep of lanes that are no longer rostered (see hazard 1).
- No usage-unit instance sweep. Under `D-3490` only the tier stop and the runtime removal move forward; that sweep and everything after the cutover stay Plan 3's.
- No change to `cmd_uninstall`'s closing `uninstall: done — …` line. Its preserved list names config, roster, identity and memory, never the runtime, so it stays true.

**Hazards later tasks must respect:**
1. **An un-rostered lane's tiers survive uninstall.** A lane removed from `accounts.json` by hand leaves its tiers running, because the library is keyed on `_codex_row`, which refuses `not-rostered`. `~/.ccrc/codex/<id>/lane.json` still names its units. Account removal does reap a lane before its row goes, through `_acct_remove`'s two codex arms, which are Task 8's (ruling R16). A hand edit does not, and Plan 3's cutover should reap a lane before its row goes.
2. **A tier whose stop failed keeps running over a deleted runtime.** The runtime is removed regardless, as spec §13 says. The stderr line tells the operator, and after an uninstall the remedy is by hand, because `ccrc` itself is gone.
3. **Every stop path is identity-gated now (ruling R8, `D-3488`).** `ccrc codex stop`, `_codex_stop_tier`, `_codex_stop_lane`, `_acct_remove`'s codex arms (Task 8, ruling R16), `_models_litellm_lane` and this step all stop a tier only on `_codex_tier_ours` 0 or 4. `_inst_codex_tiers` is narrower: it stops only a 0 and never a 4, because it stops a tier only to restart it, and a 4 is left alone and named (ruling R7). A same-named foreign unit on the fleet box therefore survives every ccrc path. The cutover (Plan 3) must stop the other repository's live units by that repository's own means, because no ccrc verb will stop them.
4. **`plantInstalledBox`'s `accounts.json` is `{"fixture":"roster"}`, which is not a roster.** Task 4's `_codex_lanes` answers rc 1 with `roster-invalid` on it, so every uninstall case on that fixture now prints one `ccrc codex: roster-invalid:` stderr line and the unreadable-roster closing line. A future case that asserts that fixture's stderr or stdout whole must plant a real roster first, with `codexRoster(home, [])`.
5. **The runtime goes after the last lane's lock is released.** A `ccrc codex start` that takes a lane's lock after this step released it, and before `rm -rf`, can start a tier on a runtime about to be removed. An uninstall on a box with live sessions needs `--force`, and the operator's act is the bound, which is the same as hazard 2's.

## Deviations found

Allocator-issued (`ccrc-api ledger allocate`) and defined here in the same act. Each entry: what departs, from which text, the measurement that forced it, and what it costs if wrong.

- **D-3478 — ccrc's common Codex launcher is `ccd/ccrc-codex`, not `ccd/ccgpt`.**
  The spec's name (§5.1, §5.3, §17) collides with a live program.
  - **Measured 2026-09-23, read-only.** On the fleet box, `~/.local/bin/ccgpt` is another repository's 22 KB launcher, carrying no ccrc marker. Both live Codex lanes exec it: one through a symlink, one through a launcher that execs it by path. It backs two running transient tier units.
  - **Why the spec's name fails.** `_inst_atomic` has no ownership check, so placing ccrc's file at that path is a silent cutover done by an installer. Even an ownership-guarded placement forces every lane to cut over in one sitting, because ccrc's launcher serves only lanes the roster declares `codex`. That contradicts spec §15.3's lane-by-lane order.
  - **What changes.** Plan 1's shipped target (`shared/wrapper.mjs`, `TOOLCHAIN_EXECUTABLES`, both roster mirrors' reserved ids, `_check_wrappers`) moves to `ccrc-codex` in Task 1. This is safe because no roster on any box names a `codex` lane, so no generated launcher execs `ccgpt` anywhere.
  - **What stays.** `ccgpt` stays a reserved roster id: a wrapper written at that path would shadow the other repository's launcher. `ccgpt-runtime`, `ccgpt-proxy.py`, `ccgpt-usage.py` and the tier unit names keep their names, because nothing of the other repository's occupies them, or (for the units) the cutover stops the old ones first.
  - **Cost if wrong:** a second name for operators to learn, and one rename commit.
  - Operator decision sought 2026-09-23; this plan is written on it.
- **D-3479 — the lifecycle verbs are `ccrc codex start|stop|status|login <id>`.**
  The spec made the launcher "the common launcher and lifecycle verb — start, stop, status, login, run" (§5.1).
  - **Why they can't live in the launcher.** `_svc_run_supervised` must live in the byte-identical platform region of `ccd/ccd` and `ccd/ccrc` (spec §7.1), and no shipped `ccd/*` executable sources either file (measured). A launcher carrying its own copy would put a third copy outside `macos-platform.test.ts`' identity pin.
  - **Why the launcher never interprets argv.** Every argument belongs to Claude Code. The other repository's launcher treats a first word of `login` or `stop` as a subcommand, and that collides with a prompt.
  - **Cost if wrong:** an operator types `ccrc codex stop <id>` rather than `ccgpt stop`.
- **D-3480 — the runtime is a set of venv generations plus a `current` symlink, and tiers start from the resolved generation.**
  The spec says a passing staged runtime "becomes current, by rename" (§5.2).
  - **Measured.** A renamed venv's console scripts exit 127, because they exec the build-time absolute path. A process started through a symlink keeps the unresolved path as `sys.prefix`, and so would lazily import the *next* generation's files after a swap.
  - **Result.** Generations are built at their final path. `current` is swapped by `ln -s` to a temp name, then one `os.replace` onto `current` (a bare `mv -f` onto a symlink-to-directory follows it). `ccgpt-runtime python` answers the resolved path.
  - **Cost if wrong:** about 650 MB per kept generation on disk.
- **D-3481 — the behaviour probe gates on the shim's folded output; Claude Code's raw shape is a non-gating canary.**
  The spec's probe sentence (§5.2) is only true after the shim's fold.
  - **Measured offline on litellm 1.101.0.** The raw shape still leaks a `{"role":"system"}` input item for a block-list mid-turn system entry, so gating on it would refuse the runtime the box runs today.
  - **Also false.** Spec §1's and §5.2's "`chatgpt` is not a member of `litellm.provider_list`" is false: measured `True`, twice.
  - **Cost if wrong:** a LiteLLM that re-breaks the raw shape passes the gate. The shim still folds it, and the canary reports it.
- **D-3482 — codex-kind lanes get `~/.ccrc/codex/<id>/litellm.yaml` and per-lane stop→write→start in this plan.**
  Plan 2a's wave table gave spec §8's rework to Plan 3.
  - **Why pulled forward.** A lane cannot run without a config, and the box-global path is the one the other repository's live LiteLLM reads.
  - **Scope.** External lanes keep today's behaviour byte-for-byte until Plan 3's cutover retires that arm.
  - **Cost if wrong:** two arms in one function for one plan's lifetime.
- **D-3483 — this plan adds `_svc_have_user_manager`: how a box without a usable user manager is detected.**
  Spec §7.3 says where there is no user manager the helper falls back to `nohup`, probing that the command exists first (the inherited `command -v` probe, which Task 2 keeps). It does not say how the ABSENCE of a user manager is detected.
  - **Measured.** `_svc_run_detached`'s Linux arm never falls back, and no helper in the tree tests for a usable user manager.
  - **The new check.** `command -v systemd-run` and `systemctl --user show-environment`.
  - **Cost if wrong:** on a box with a wedged user manager, the probe waits for systemd's own D-Bus timeout before the helper falls back. No caller adds a tighter bound.
- **D-3484 — every litellm import this plan adds runs with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`.**
  That covers both tiers' LiteLLM, the behaviour probe, `ccrc codex login` and the usage unit. `ccd/ccrc-models-probe`'s import (inside the cut) is Plan 3's, and is carried forward as a precondition of the cutover.
  - **Measured.** Otherwise `import litellm` fetches a mutable remote JSON on every start, with three retries: 11.8 s when the network is denied, and a model map the probe never saw.
  - **This changes live behaviour.** The other repository's tiers fetch today.
  - **Cost if wrong:** model metadata is as old as the installed wheel.
- **D-3485 — restart-after-update is the bare spine step `_inst_codex_tiers`, not code inside `_inst_enable` (spec §7.4).**
  - **Why the spec's reason still holds.** It runs on install and update, and never through `_upd_sweep`.
  - **Why a separate step.** It is visible in the pinned step list, and platform-neutral: Darwin's `_inst_enable` returns before any addition.
  - **How it restarts.** Stop plus start, not `systemctl restart`. A transient unit's restart re-runs the OLD generation's argv. Only tiers that are running, verified ours and stale are restarted.
  - **Cost if wrong:** one more line in the step list.
- **D-3486 — `deploy/systemd/ccgpt-usage@.service` runs `%h/.ccrc/runtime/codex/current/bin/python -I` with the cost map local.**
  This closes D-3164's 2b-2 half. The pair stays unplaced (D-3172); arming it is Plan 3's.
  - **Why `current` is fine here.** A oneshot starts fresh each run, so the symlink resolves anew every time.
  - **Cost if wrong:** none until Plan 3 arms the unit.
- **D-3487 — the LiteLLM requirement is `litellm[proxy]>=1.101.0,<1.110`, declared once in `ccd/ccgpt-runtime`.**
  The spec asks for "a declared, supported range" and names none.
  - **Why this range.** It chooses tolerance over freezing (the operator's standing preference), bounded because the surface is upstream's experimental one. The probe is the acceptance test.
  - **No cross-box drift after a build.** A box rebuilds only when `check` fails: no runtime, the requirement or the probe bytes moved, or the installed litellm no longer matches its stamp. (Corrected by Task 12, ruling PF-6. This sentence used to say "only when the requirement or the probe bytes change", but the builder's own pinned cases rebuild an absent or mutated runtime too.)
  - **Cost if wrong:** a release inside the range that the probe cannot see breaking. The previous generation is the rollback.
- **D-3488 — every ccrc path that stops a tier stops it only when `_codex_tier_ours` proves it ours (running or starting), and only then by exact unit or verified pid.**
  The spec says "stopping is by exact unit, then by verified identity" (§7.4).
  - **Measured.** The other repository's live tiers use the same unit names ccrc's would. An exact-name stop from `ccrc codex stop`, account removal, uninstall or the spine could stop another program's live gateway. A foreign or unmeasurable tier is left running and named.
  - **Cost if wrong:** a wedged ccrc tier that fails its own identity needs a manual `systemctl --user stop`. There is also a window where the gate refuses this lane's own tier. While a crash-looping ccrc tier sits in its `RestartSec` window, its unit is live with `MainPID=0` and nothing answers on the port. In that window `_codex_tier_ours` answers 2 with `CX_TIER_WHY=unit-unproven`, so a stop leaves the tier alone. The sentence says the identity is UNPROVEN (a unit of that name is live, with no process to prove it), suggests a retry, and never claims another tool owns it. The operator retries the stop once. (Added by Task 12, ruling PF-13.)
- **D-3489 — `ccrc account auth-start` does not exist (measured), so this plan routes a codex lane's login through the existing pane door.**
  Spec §9.3 names `ccrc account auth-start` as the route. Here, `ccd account-pane --method openai-login` → `_auth_openai_login` → `ccrc codex login <id>`.
  - **Cost if wrong:** when `auth-start` lands, it must route the same way (carried forward).
- **D-3490 — the uninstall half of the lane lands in this plan.**
  Plan 2a's wave table gave "uninstall behaviour" to Plan 3.
  - **Why pulled forward.** This plan installs a runtime (`~/.ccrc/runtime/codex/`, about 650 MB a generation) and can run tiers. The release that can place them must be able to remove them, so Task 11's `_uninst_codex` ships with it.
  - **What stays Plan 3's.** The usage-unit instance sweep (2b-1's item 14) and everything that follows the cutover.
  - **Cost if wrong:** one spine step that is a no-op on every box without a codex lane.
- **D-3491 — the no-secret pin is asserted over the `systemd-run` argv, not over `systemctl show` output.**
  Spec §5.4's pin says "no process argv or unit property carries the key (assert over `systemctl show` output in a fixture, and over the launcher's own `systemd-run` argv)".
  - **Measured.** No fixture models transient-unit properties, and a planted `show` answer would be a control derived from the measurement. It proves only what the test author typed.
  - **Result.** The honest fixture-level evidence is the recorded `systemd-run` argv: no `--setenv` pair carries the key, and the key reaches LiteLLM only through `-p EnvironmentFile=`. Real `Transient=yes` and unit properties exist only under a live user manager, which the containment rules forbid in tests.
  - **Cost if wrong:** a unit property set by some other mechanism would go unseen. None exists in `_svc_run_supervised`.

Found during execution. Task 12 Step 5 drew these six from one allocator block (`ccrc-api ledger allocate`, 2026-09-28) and defines them here in the same act. The pre-flight rulings (PF-1 to PF-43), the one-commit and round-bounding rulings, the Task 6, 7 and 9 fixes that brought code to this plan's own rulings, and Task 9's foreign-name pin carry no number: they are process or conformance, and the SDD ledger records them.

- **D-3528 — a LiteLLM tier is this lane's only when its argv-proven pid itself holds the LISTEN socket on the lane's port.**
  Task 5 (review F1, fix rounds 1 and 2), in Task 4's library. It departs from Task 4's `_codex_tier_ours` contract (Appendix A: "litellm = the unit's `MainPID` … or the pidfile pid … is alive AND its `ps -o args=` contains `--config $HOME/.ccrc/codex/<id>/litellm.yaml` AND something listens on litellmPort"). That contract never asked WHO listens.
  - **Measured.** A LiteLLM that `start` spawned is argv-proven from its fork until it dies on `EADDRINUSE`. If another process held the port in that window, the first readiness probe read 0, and `start` printed `litellm started` with exit 0 while it was attached to the other process's gateway. That is the failure spec §7.4 calls a real, dated incident.
  - **The tree's answer.** `_codex_pid_listens <pid> <port>` answers 0 (the pid holds a LISTEN socket on the port), 1 (a LISTEN socket is visible and is not the pid's, or the pid is gone) or 3 (cannot ask, with the reason in `CX_LISTEN_WHY`).
    - On Linux it reads the LISTEN (`st` `0A`) rows of `/proc/net/tcp` and `/proc/net/tcp6` for the port's inodes, then `readlink`s each `/proc/<pid>/fd` entry for `socket:[<inode>]`. It never parses `ls -l`, whose quoting follows `QUOTING_STYLE`.
    - On Darwin it runs a bounded `lsof -nP -a -p <pid> -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN -t`, then a port-wide query.
    - It answers 3 in each of these cases: no `readlink`, no `lsof`, an `lsof` that times out or exits other than 0 or 1, an unreadable fd directory, or no LISTEN socket visible at all.
  - **What `_codex_tier_ours`' LiteLLM arm does with it.** For a proven pid on an answering port: helper 0 → 0; helper 1 → 2 with the new `CX_TIER_WHY` word `listener-other-process`, the proven handle kept; helper 3 → 3 with the refusal code `tier-unmeasured`.
  - **The consumers.** `_codex_stop_tier` stops this lane's own proven process through its handle and leaves the port's holder running and named. The readiness wait ends at once on a 3. `ccrc codex status` names the shape, and `--json` keeps its `via` and `pid`. Two codes the same rounds ratified also belong here: `shim-absent` for a missing shim at the tier level, and `tier-foreign` for the rekey restart's foreign stop.
  - **Pins** (`server/test/ccrc-codex.test.ts`):
    - L24, L27, L29, L30, L33 and L34;
    - in Task 4's `_codex_tier_ours` describe, the `listener-other-process` case and the rc-3 `tier-unmeasured` case;
    - the `_codex_pid_listens` cases: /proc, a connected non-LISTEN socket, no `readlink`, five `QUOTING_STYLE`s, an unreadable fd table, the Darwin arm asked on Linux, and the `lsof` bound.
  - **Amended by the final-review fix wave (2026-09-28; review A1, A2, A4 and Task 5's residue, fixer F1).**
    - ONE predicate, `_codex_tier_is_our_handle <rc>`, reads whether an answer is this lane's own tier, to stop through its handle: 0, 4, or 2 with `listener-other-process`. `_codex_stop_tier` (both of its measurements), `_acct_remove`'s post-stop re-measure and `_uninst_codex`'s gate read it, and `ccrc codex status` keeps `via` and `pid` through it. So account removal puts a `listener-other-process` tier into `lane_left` and refuses, never reaping the pidfile under a live tier of its own, and uninstall stops that tier through `_codex_stop_tier`, which is identity-gated itself.
    - `unit-unproven` refuses account removal too (A2/D2): it is not proven foreign. Removal refuses on it exactly as on a 3, and every rc-2 consumer takes its words from `_codex_foreign_what`.
    - The shim twin: a shim pid proven by `--ccrc-lane=<id>` while another process holds its port answers 2, `listener-other-process`, and an owner that cannot be measured answers 3, `tier-unmeasured`.
    - `_codex_pid_listens` answers 3 when `readlink` reads none of the pid's fds. It used to fold to 1, "another process holds it", for the very pid that held it. On Darwin it answers 0 when the port-wide `lsof` list names the pid.
    - The `nohup` stop's SIGKILL requires `_codex_pid_is_tier` as well as `kill -0` (A4).
    - `_codex_tier_port <tier>` is the one tier-to-port mapping. There were four hand-written copies, one of them with an inverted default.
    - Pins (F1): in `ccrc-codex.test.ts`, "_codex_tier_is_our_handle: 0 and 4 are this lane's; of the 2s only listener-other-process is; …", the shim arm, the shim stop, readlink all-fail, lsof self, A4 and `_codex_tier_port`; in `ccrc-account.test.ts`, C10 and C11; in `ccrc-uninstall.test.ts`, "this lane's own process while another holds its port (listener-other-process) is STOPPED through _codex_stop_tier, never left alone (review A1)". F1's mutation rows M-A1a to M-A1d, M-shim, M-A2-remove, M-rl, M-lsof, M-A4, M-port-swap and M-port-inline red them.
  - Spec: §19.5.

One deleted line was enough to void the convention.

    - Both isolation harnesses (`runStepHarness`, `runUninstCodex`) call `assertIsolationWallFirst` on the line before their one spawn.
